Abysium Dragon (Adult).description: Drawing on radiation as both a force of destruction and a source of energy, abysium dragons are tied to the radioactive starmetal of the same name. These dragons grow deposits of pure abysium in their bodies, becoming more radioactive as they age, causing aggression, agitation, and even loneliness since not many creatures can long survive the company of an aging abysium dragon. Abysium dragons frequently turn to pursuits such as augmentation and weapon crafting (to take advantage of their innate power source) and the construction of robots (to keep them company). This work drives abysium dragons to seek out sturdy, radiation-resistant materials they can use for crafting, and they often spend years at a time scouring small moons and asteroids in search of precious materials.

5CufGY5r3qJcDtjv.description: Abysium dragons have ultimate control over the radioactive energy that grows within their bodies. Any time an abysium dragon deals fire or poison damage, they can choose whether that damage is magical, and they can change any amount of the fire damage to poison (or any amount of poison damage to fire).
5CufGY5r3qJcDtjv.name: Control Radiation

Aeon Guard Commander.description: Aeon Guard commanders are trained to lead from the front, using relatively short-range firearms and extraordinary skill with their dueling swords to press the advantage up close while motivating the rest of their unit to close in. Aeon Guard commanders are dispatched whenever there's a need to end a battle quickly and decisively.

DenynSu1hxVaDwhD.description:
Trigger The commander reduces an enemy to 0 Hit Points or critically hits an enemy with a Strike

Effect The commander makes a gruesome spectacle of their brutal hit. They attempt an Intimidation check to [[/act demoralize]] all enemies within 30 feet.
DenynSu1hxVaDwhD.name: Terrifying Takedown

avV2vqnq2H2XMjvQ.description:
Upgrades: 1

Flexible but sturdy plates layered together form this traditional armor worn by lashunta cavalry on Castrovel. In times past, a shotalashu cavalry member forged their armor from their mount's shed skin, or more rarely, the skin of a fallen mount, to honor them in future battles. Synthetic imitations are fashionable on some parts of Castrovel.
avV2vqnq2H2XMjvQ.name: Aeon Guard Armor

lyOtPwMLJrHgwBOA.description:
The commander Strides twice. If they end this movement within melee reach of at least one enemy, they can make a melee Strike against that enemy. The commander's allies gain a +1 circumstance bonus to attack the target of this Strike and ignore any cover the commander provides the target for 1 round.

@UUID[Compendium.sf2e.bestiary-effects.Item.UEnGE804ZFRJmQYN]{Effect: Lead the Charge}
lyOtPwMLJrHgwBOA.name: Lead the Charge

saGvWUscAHxydibO.description:
The commander issues an order for their allies to regroup. All Aeon Guard allies within 120 feet of the commander can use a reaction to Stride up to their Speed. Any Aeon Guards who end their movement adjacent to another Aeon Guard gain 5 temporary Hit Points that last 1 minute, or double that number of temporary Hit Points if they end their movement adjacent to the commander. The commander can't Rally the Troops again for [[/gmr 1d4 #Recharge Rally the Troops]]{1d4 rounds}.

@UUID[Compendium.sf2e.bestiary-effects.Item.p2GrXbOJbv0OT4Zr]{Effect: Rally the Troops}
saGvWUscAHxydibO.name: Rally the Troops

w3l5YRTQRu724SMV.description:
Frequency once per round

Effect The commander calls out an enemy within 60 feet then makes a Strike against that enemy, dealing an additional 1d6 precision damage on a hit. If the Strike hits, the commander changes the tide of the battle, inspiring their allies to greater feats of military prowess. All Aeon Guard allies within 60 feet of the commander gain a +1 status bonus to attack and damage rolls until the beginning of the commander's next turn.

@UUID[Compendium.sf2e.feat-effects.Item.ppKeWbPcSaVqD1Cj]{Effect: Tactical Strike}
w3l5YRTQRu724SMV.name: Tactical Strike

Aeon Guard Commander.name: Aeon Guard Commander

Aeon Guard Trooper.description:
Rank-and-file Aeon Guard troopers are easily identified by their distinctive green armor consisting of ceramic and polycarbonate plates overlaid with an energy-reflective molecular coating. Aeon Guards frequently upgrade their armor with aeon stones, further distinguishing them from soldiers of "lesser" armies.

Even the newest recruits have sworn personal oaths of loyalty to the Aeon Throne—a traitor or deserter of the Azlanti Star Empire is extraordinarily rare. These troopers are also loyal to one another and highly trained to fight in coordinated formations, and they obey their commanding officers without question, even if their orders mean certain death.

7ezssdkKVZnPDiB7.description:
After the trooper attempts a Strike against a target (regardless of success or failure), the next attack roll one of the trooper's allies makes against the same target gains a +2 circumstance bonus. If a Strike with a bonus from coordinated fire hits, the target becomes @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.enA7BxAjBb7ns1iF]{Suppressed} until the end of the attacking ally's next turn.

@UUID[Compendium.sf2e.bestiary-effects.Item.x9nA4lIcHmE7x8Tt]{Effect: Coordinated Fire}
7ezssdkKVZnPDiB7.name: Coordinated Fire

IsQHes2JROGSI8b5.description: When the trooper makes a ranged Strike against a target with an AC bonus from lesser or standard cover, they reduce the AC bonus by 1 for that Strike.
IsQHes2JROGSI8b5.name: Sharpshooter

Synthetic imitations are fashionable on some parts of Castrovel.

Q0GKusWo45x8L9wP.name: Show No Mercy

Aeon Guard Trooper.name: Aeon Guard Trooper

Akashic Dragon (Adult).description: Though rarely encountered outside their crumbling, relic-filled lairs, Akashic dragons occasionally live in hubs of knowledge, such as bustling space stations or cities. These dragons, bestowed with a direct connection to the Akashic Record, are arrogant curators of knowledge, assuming (often correctly) that no other being could possibly have a deeper understanding of the universe's secrets. Akashic dragons spend extensive time in the Akashic Record, often emerging after what they perceive as many days while mere hours have passed for the rest of the galaxy.

1glFKWbEEHLBydZu.description:
90 feet. The swirl of constant uploads and downloads near the Akashic dragon make attempts to @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.actions.Item.1OagaWtBpVXExToo]{Recall Knowledge} unpredictable. A creature other than an akashic dragon that enters or begins its turn in the area must attempt a @Check[will|dc:28] save. Regardless of the result of the saving throw, the creature is temporarily immune to this dragon's Akashic interference for 1 minute.

Critical Success For 1 round, when the creature attempts to Recall Knowledge, it gains a +3 status bonus to its check.

Success The creature is unaffected.

Failure For 1 round, when the creature attempts to Recall Knowledge, it takes a –3 status penalty to its check.

Critical Failure As failure, but the effect lasts 1 minute.
1glFKWbEEHLBydZu.name: Akashic Interference

3T8rhNzByQZrJDhv.description:
Requirements The dragon has successfully Recalled Knowledge about an enemy within 90 feet within the last minute

Effect The dragon utters a shocking truth about the creature that even it might not know, causing it and its allies to hesitate or act erratically. Every enemy within 90 feet that can hear the secret must attempt a @Check[will|dc:31|options:area-effect,inflicts:slowed] save. Each creature is then immune to Shocking Revelation for 24 hours.

Critical Success The creature is unaffected.

Success The creature is @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.xYTAsEpcJE1Ccni3]{Slowed 1} for 1 round.

Failure The creature is @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.xYTAsEpcJE1Ccni3]{Slowed 2} for 1 round.

Critical Failure The creature is @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.yblD8fOR1J8rDwEQ]{Confused} for 1 round.
3T8rhNzByQZrJDhv.name: Shocking Revelation

5T4RohwKxVJbmHxb.description: The dragon recharges their Akashic Barrage whenever they score a critical hit with a Strike.
5T4RohwKxVJbmHxb.name: Draconic Momentum

6bTILS2YSW9jQYQP.description: The first time each encounter the Akashic dragon hits and deals damage to a creature with their jaws Strike, they receive information about the creature as if they'd succeeded at a check to @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.actions.Item.1OagaWtBpVXExToo]{Recall Knowledge} about that creature.
6bTILS2YSW9jQYQP.name: Records of the Enemy

Ie2A6VEeEAaPtoW6.description: Instead of using their own memories, an Akashic dragon can ascertain information from the Akashic Records. This gives it the Akashic Record Lore skill, which it can use to @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.actions.Item.1OagaWtBpVXExToo]{Recall Knowledge} of any kind.
Ie2A6VEeEAaPtoW6.name: Akashic Eye

YNphbFGydAAzaQWx.description: The Akashic dragon can activate magic and tech items with the Cast a Spell activation of any tradition as if the spells they contain were occult spells.
YNphbFGydAAzaQWx.name: Akashic Adaptability

fPRg27BqEAJ6Md6V.description:
You execute a psychic search of the Akashic Record for information about a specific topic and magically transfer this data to your comm unit or computer. When you Cast this Spell, choose any skill in which you're trained that has the @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.actions.Item.1OagaWtBpVXExToo]{Recall Knowledge} action.

Any time during the duration, you can consult your comm unit while attempting a Recall Knowledge check using your chosen skill. This check gains a +1 status bonus. Checking your comm unit is part of the action to Recall Knowledge. You must be holding the comm unit to do so. The comm unit instantly compiles and displays snippets and selections from various media relevant to the topic, which grants you the bonus. If you roll a critical failure on this check, you get a failure instead. If the check is successful and the subject is a creature, you gain additional information or context about the creature. Once you reference the comm unit, the spell ends. When the spell ends, your access to the Akashic Record ends, and all the information you downloaded returns to the Akashic Record.

@UUID[Compendium.sf2e.spell-effects.Item.h1i8c47U0IOrMrHJ]{Spell Effect: Akashic Download}

Heightened (3rd) You can reference your comm unit three times before the spell ends.
fPRg27BqEAJ6Md6V.name: Akashic Download (at will)

jgthYrZ2jNZoV5Ta.name: +2 Status to All Saves vs. Occult

mdIGB9kjmEzFiA0k.description:
Requirements You have a planar key for the destination plane, used as a locus

You and your allies traverse the barriers between planes of existence. The targets move to another plane, such as the Plane of Fire, the Netherworld, or the Outer Rifts. You must know the destination plane exists and use a magic planar key created from material from that plane as a locus for the spell. While the planar keys for most prominent planes are uncommon, just like the spell interplanar teleport, more obscure planes and demiplanes often have rare or possibly even unique planar keys.

The spell is highly imprecise, and you appear 1d20×25 miles from the last place one of the targets (of your choice) was located the last time that target traveled to the plane. If it's the first time traveling to a particular plane for all targets, you appear at a random location on the plane. YNphbFGydAAzaQWx.description: The Akashic dragon can activate magic and tech items with the Cast a Spell activation of any tradition as if the spells they contain were occult spells.
YNphbFGydAAzaQWx.name: Akashic Adaptability

fPRg27BqEAJ6Md6V.description:
You execute a psychic search of the Akashic Record for information about a specific topic and magically transfer this data to your comm unit or computer. When you Cast this Spell, choose any skill in which you're trained that has the @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.actions.Item.1OagaWtBpVXExToo]{Recall Knowledge} action.

Any time during the duration, you can consult your comm unit while attempting a Recall Knowledge check using your chosen skill. This check gains a +1 status bonus. Checking your comm unit is part of the action to Recall Knowledge. You must be holding the comm unit to do so. The comm unit instantly compiles and displays snippets and selections from various media relevant to the topic, which grants you the bonus. If you roll a critical failure on this check, you get a failure instead. If the check is successful and the subject is a creature, you gain additional information or context about the creature. Once you reference the comm unit, the spell ends. When the spell ends, your access to the Akashic Record ends, and all the information you downloaded returns to the Akashic Record.

@UUID[Compendium.sf2e.spell-effects.Item.h1i8c47U0IOrMrHJ]{Spell Effect: Akashic Download}

Heightened (3rd) You can reference your comm unit three times before the spell ends.
fPRg27BqEAJ6Md6V.name: Akashic Download (at will)

jgthYrZ2jNZoV5Ta.name: +2 Status to All Saves vs. Occult

mdIGB9kjmEzFiA0k.description:
Requirements You have a planar key for the destination plane, used as a locus

You and your allies traverse the barriers between planes of existence. The targets move to another plane, such as the Plane of Fire, the Netherworld, or the Outer Rifts. You must know the destination plane exists and use a magic planar key created from material from that plane as a locus for the spell. While the planar keys for most prominent planes are uncommon, just like the spell interplanar teleport, more obscure planes and demiplanes often have rare or possibly even unique planar keys.

The spell is highly imprecise, and you appear 1d20×25 miles from the last place one of the targets (of your choice) was located the last time that target traveled to the plane. If it's the first time traveling to a particular plane for all targets, you appear at a random location on the plane. Interplanar teleport doesn't provide a means of return travel, though casting interplanar teleport again allows you to return to your previous plane unless there are extenuating circumstances.
mdIGB9kjmEzFiA0k.name: Interplanar Teleport (at will; self only; to and from Akashic Record and the Universe only)

q8rJvLjMTCznfXt0.description: The dragon makes two claw Strikes and one tail Strike in any order.
q8rJvLjMTCznfXt0.name: Draconic Frenzy

qYYH8A3ZYE1GohYf.description: The dragon condenses cutting truths and fiery revelations from the Akashic Record into sizzling laser fire that they project as a cone from their primary eye to assail their foes. This deals @Damage[10d6[fire]|options:area-damage] damage in a @Template[type:cone|distance:30] (@Check[reflex|dc:26|basic|options:area-effect,inflicts:stupefied] save). The dragon can't use Akashic Barrage again for [[/gmr 1d4 #Recharge Akashic Barrage]]{1d4 rounds}.

wZKJvFmBzPesW2Dv.description:

If the Akashic dragon has succeeded at a @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.actions.Item.1OagaWtBpVXExToo]{Recall Knowledge} check against the creature in the last minute, they gain resistance 11 instead.

Akashic Dragon (Young, Spellcaster).description: Though rarely encountered outside their crumbling, relic-filled lairs, Akashic dragons occasionally live in hubs of knowledge, such as bustling space stations or cities. These dragons, bestowed with a direct connection to the Akashic Record, are arrogant curators of knowledge, assuming (often correctly) that no other being could possibly have a deeper understanding of the universe's secrets. Akashic dragons spend extensive time in the Akashic Record, often emerging after what they perceive as many days while mere hours have passed for the rest of the galaxy.

6bTILS2YSW9jQYQP.description: The first time each encounter the Akashic dragon hits and deals damage to a creature with their jaws Strike, they receive information about the creature as if they'd succeeded at a check to @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.actions.Item.1OagaWtBpVXExToo]{Recall Knowledge} about that creature.

Akata.description:
Few creatures inspire more dread in isolated explorers and lonely space stations than the breathless, leonine akatas, which infest creatures with parasites to transform them into ravenous void zombies.

An akata's toothy maw, glowing yellow eyes, and lashing twin tails mark it as a silent predator. Their slinking, hairless blue flesh spreads out into a mane of rubbery tentacles. Despite lacking ears, these quadrupeds stalk prey with an enhanced sight and sense of smell. Akatas typically stand at about 3-1/2 feet tall and weigh 400 pounds.

In times of scarcity, akatas ooze noqual from their pores and spin pale green crystalline cocoons capable of holding them in stasis for centuries. They can even use their cocoons to traverse space and find new hosts for their larvae. When a host dies from this infestation, known as void death, the strongest offspring animates the cadaver as a void zombie. Fiercely territorial, they hunt in colonies that are capable of bringing a settlement to its knees within weeks.

AMnTAvqDDSvhK4rN.description: Salt water attacks an akata's cells and acts as a potent acid. If the akata is fully immersed in salt water, it takes @Damage[4d6[acid]] damage from the water immediately and at the end of each of its turns as long as it remains immersed. Its weakness to salt water applies to this damage.
AMnTAvqDDSvhK4rN.name: Salt Water Vulnerability

L17R2FDChGWE5pgD.description:
An akata implants microscopic larvae into any creature it bites, but only Small or Medium humanoids make suitable hosts; all other creatures are @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.fesd1n5eVhpCSS18]{Sickened 1} at Stage 2 and further instead.

Saving Throw @Check[fortitude|dc:17]

Stage 1 carrier with no ill effect 1 (1 day)

Stage 2 @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.4D2KBtexWXa6oUMR]{Drained 1} (1 day)

Stage 3 as stage 2 (1 day)

Stage 4 @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.4D2KBtexWXa6oUMR]{Drained 2} and @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.HL2l2VRSaQHu9lUw]{Fatigued} (1 day)

Stage 5 as stage 4 (1 day)

Stage 6 dead and corpse rises as a void zombie in [[/gmr 2d4 #hours]]{2d4 hours}
L17R2FDChGWE5pgD.name: Void Death

rsf1q6ooMNJFjdfh.description: Akatas are immune to auditory effects, automatically critically fail Perception checks that require it to hear, and take a –2 status penalty to Perception checks (but not initiative rolls) that involve sound but also rely on its other senses.
rsf1q6ooMNJFjdfh.name: No Hearing

sYzEwjtXD4GsP03b.description: An akata can secrete resin that encases it safely in a noqual cocoon. The cocoon has Hardness 9, 40 HP, and a BT of 18. It has resistance 5 to damage from magical sources. While ensconced within this cocoon, the akata can't be harmed, doesn't need to eat or drink, and gains @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.bestiary-ability-glossary-srd.Item.sebk9XseMCRkDqRg]{Lifesense} 30 feet. During its hibernation, the akata remains dormant until exposed to extreme heat or it senses a living creature. It can then break free of its cocoon within [[/gmr 1d4 #minutes]]{1d4 minutes}.
sYzEwjtXD4GsP03b.name: Hibernation

Alloid (Ship Stealer).description:
Alloids are interplanetary scavengers sent by the Dominion of the Black to plague the galaxy. These tall, thin, and spindly creatures appear to have metallic sheens to their smooth skin, often in copper or gold tones. An alloid's surprisingly pliable physiology allows them to mold their physical form to fit into tight spaces or stretch paper-thin against surfaces. It's rumored they can, with great effort, even mimic other people.

While few enough people have encountered alloids for the name to truly catch on, they've become colloquially known as "ship stealers" in the Pact Worlds. They frequently travel in groups of three to five, hanging around spaceports and scoping out potential marks. They often look for smaller ships with crews not much larger than their pack or massive ships with many hiding places. They then slip aboard inside containers or backpacks, often during resupply cycles.

Once the ship is out in space and the crew settled in, the pack gets to work, ideally taking out their targets one by one with barbs that make their prey's flesh as malleable as their own, allowing them to easily hide the bodies. After kidnapping a crew, they fly the ship to places where they can link up with other alloids—or their Dominion masters—to strip the starship for parts. What they do with their living prey is unknown.

Before the Gap, the Dominion of the Black had a strong presence on Aucturn and would occasionally invade other planets, such as Lost Golarion, in search of brains to devour and in pursuit of other mysterious agendas. Now, the people of the Pact Worlds understand that the Dominion has secret bases across the galaxy—the Pact Worlds might draw their attention from time to time, but their missions take them to many worlds and many star systems.

The Dominion creatures most commonly seen by others are mere scouts, while more powerful members of the Dominion conglomeration emerge only rarely to terrorize society. Stories of these creatures are as few as the scant number of people who survive such encounters—most spacefarers know to immediately flee any ship or territory with signs of Dominion presence.

9kFNb6bUd95hwmyY.description:
Trigger The alloid is hit or critically hit by a Strike or spell attack, and they aren't @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.AJh5ex99aV6VTggg]{Off-Guard}

Effect The alloid gains a +2 circumstance bonus to AC against the triggering attack.
9kFNb6bUd95hwmyY.name: Malleable Flesh

BeTEYhe7jp0lSNRF.description: The alloid's body melts and molds to fit into tight spaces or stretches paper-thin against a flat surface. They gain a +2 circumstance bonus to Stealth checks to [[/act hide]] and to their Stealth DC when using this ability while adjacent to walls or within tight spaces (at the GM's discretion). Alloids using this ability can squeeze into spaces, including into closed containers or through doors, as though they were Tiny. The alloid can use Putty Form again to return to their standard, more solid form.
BeTEYhe7jp0lSNRF.name: Putty Form

ZnB8xhiLlO4Bd2U4.description: The alloid deals an additional 1d6 precision damage to @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.AJh5ex99aV6VTggg]{Off-Guard} creatures.
ZnB8xhiLlO4Bd2U4.name: Sneak Attack

oNfNdrJOw6hQmzNv.description:

Animated Firearm.description:
Animated firearms make for great training aids but can just as easily defend goods and possessions from intruders or serve as hidden sentries.

Objects can be animated in multiple ways for a variety of functions. Since ancient times, weapons and armor have been given life as guardians and sentries through magic or ritual.

2ukgn8AhO0AxjhoH.description: Once an animated firearm is reduced to less than half its Hit Points, or immediately upon being damaged by a critical hit, it becomes permanently @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.6A2QDy8wRGCVQsSd]{Glitching 1} until its Hit Points are fully restored (such as by being Repaired).
2ukgn8AhO0AxjhoH.name: Unreliable Tech

TLKAuyPNGi56sFFz.description: In the hands of its creator, an animated firearm is a commercial laser pistol. The creator can Interact to release the firearm into an adjacent space to act on its own, or to retrieve it from an adjacent space and use it as a weapon.
TLKAuyPNGi56sFFz.name: Weapon Mode

kxHT2BI6bT2AgS3m.description:
A creature that takes damage from the animated firearm's stun gun must succeed at a @Check[fortitude|dc:15] save or become @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.dfCMdR4wnpbYNTix]{Stunned 1} (@UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.dfCMdR4wnpbYNTix]{Stunned 2} on a critical failure).

On a critical hit, the target creature uses the outcome one degree of success worse than the result of its roll. On a success, the target is immune to stun for 1 minute.
kxHT2BI6bT2AgS3m.name: Stun

After resolving the Shove, the animated tech armor attempts to [[/act trip]] the target using the same multiple attack penalty as the Shove. Apari.description:
An apari is a living hive beholden to its beetle-like queen, whose massive carapace houses generations of its insect brood. Millions of constituents across various developmental stages animate the exoskeleton of a single apari. At the direction of their queen's chemical signals, individual constituents, most no larger than a grain of rice, adapt to the hive's current needs, assuming diverse forms to fulfill specialized roles and supporting its gestalt biological functions.

Once introduced within an ecosystem, an apari asserts itself rapidly. Winged constituents forage for food as the hive itself hunts living prey, tearing its victims open with sharp claws while grub-like constituents writhe into fresh wounds and consume the prey from within. When an apari is threatened, combat-ready drones selflessly rush to defend the hive or to cover its escape.

9V2vbqUrDvZEdlcb.description: The apari's constituents can change their physiology, taking advantage of an opponent's weakness. The apari alters the type of damage it deals with its claw attack (which also affects the type of persistent damage), its Constituent Sortie ability, or its swarming bites aura, choosing from the following: bludgeoning, piercing, or slashing.
9V2vbqUrDvZEdlcb.name: Fungible

LWNf3yWvQ1NmEbQB.description: The apari's carapace has Hardness 10, reducing any damage the apari takes by that amount. Once the apari is reduced to fewer than half its Hit Points, or immediately upon taking damage from a critical hit, the carapace breaks, removing the Hardness and reducing its AC to 20. An apari with a broken carapace gains resistance 5 to precision damage and weakness 5 to both area damage and splash damage. It also gains the Swarming Bites aura.
LWNf3yWvQ1NmEbQB.name: Carapace

jilC2qnATcOEslbP.description:
Requirements The apari's carapace isn't broken

Effect The apari releases a bevy of tiny, flying constituents in a @Template[type:cone|distance:15] that sting all within. Each creature in the area takes @Damage[4d6[piercing]|options:area-damage] damage with a @Check[reflex|dc:21|basic|options:area-effect] save.
jilC2qnATcOEslbP.name: Constituent Sortie

mHAUCnEpELliiWiU.description: The apari Seeks by dispersing constituents to scan a wide area, attempting to find hidden or undetected creatures within 90 feet.
mHAUCnEpELliiWiU.name: Foraging Constituents

tvJ3jfQtykC7ARyt.description:
10 feet. The constituents of an apari with a broken carapace angrily swarm around its body. A creature that begins its turn in this aura takes @Damage[4d6[piercing]|options:area-damage] damage with a @Check[fortitude|dc:21|basic|options:area-effect] save. A creature that fails this save is also @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.fesd1n5eVhpCSS18]{Sickened 1} (or @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.fesd1n5eVhpCSS18]{Sickened 2} on a critical failure).

Can alternatively switch to @Damage[4d6[bludgeoning]|options:area-damage] or @Damage[4d6[slashing]|options:area-damage] with the Fungible ability.
tvJ3jfQtykC7ARyt.name: Swarming Bites

Appendage Cluster.description: Caypins are brawny predators with the agility of wolves and the scaly skin of crocodiles. Their most striking feature is a mass of wriggling, semi-sentient appendages that cover their heads. Each of these tentacle-like protuberances contains a bloodshot eyeball and a gaping mouth full of teeth, and the caypin—which has no eyes or mouth of its own—relies on these orifices to see and feed. Nutrients absorbed by the appendages are passed to the caypin via tiny receptive sockets in the beast's jaw, and caypins can detach these appendages into writhing clusters that independently move up to 100 feet from their bodies. In the wild, caypins use these clusters to ambush prey, and the creatures are known across the galaxy for their rapacious ability to consume half of their body weight in raw meat.

cvJiF6miOpAoZOOQ.description: An appendage cluster attempts an Acrobatics check to [[/act tumble-through]] a creature's space. On a success, the mouths of the cluster gnash and gnaw at the creature, dealing @Damage[3d8[piercing]] damage. If the Acrobatics check was a critical success, the target also takes @Damage[4[persistent,bleed]] damage.
cvJiF6miOpAoZOOQ.name: Cluster Onslaught

Appendage Cluster.name: Appendage Cluster

Arabuk.description:
Arabuks take 3 years to reach maturity. Each year that an arabuk lives, its antlers grow more impressive, sometimes reaching lengths greater than 15 feet.

Those traveling through Akiton's Winterlands risk stumbling on its apex predator: the carnivorous arabuk.

4fv4cddyfz8QSy5z.description: The arabuk clatters its antlers together by shaking its head. Until the end of its turn, any creature hit by its antlers must succeed at a @Check[fortitude|dc:22|options:inflicts:stunned] save or become @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.dfCMdR4wnpbYNTix]{Stunned 1} (@UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.dfCMdR4wnpbYNTix]{Stunned 2} on a critical failure).
4fv4cddyfz8QSy5z.name: Clatter

H7gPVBa3Xj3wn6xg.description: Snow doesn't impair an arabuk's vision; it ignores @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.DmAIPqOBomZ7H95W]{Concealment} from snowfall.
H7gPVBa3Xj3wn6xg.name: Snow Vision

kqQgtbGNJtxetbTd.description: A non-arabuk creature standing on snow that fails its Reflex save against an arabuk's antler reverberation is knocked @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.j91X7x0XSomq8d60]{Prone}. Up to a @Template[cube|distance:20] of snow in the area of an antler reverberation collapses, dealing @Damage[5d6[bludgeoning]|options:area-damage] damage to adjacent creatures (@Check[reflex|dc:24|basic|options:area-effect] save). On a slope, this causes the snow and any creatures that fail its save to move downhill 30 feet per round. At the start of its turn, each creature caught in the avalanche takes @Damage[3d6[bludgeoning]|options:area-damage] damage (@Check[reflex|dc:24|basic|options:area-effect] save) and, on a failure, is still caught in the avalanche.
kqQgtbGNJtxetbTd.name: Avalanche

vNyd7arQexBTqAs0.description: The arabuk Strides twice with a +10-foot circumstance bonus to Speed, ignoring difficult terrain caused by ice, snow, or other arctic conditions.
vNyd7arQexBTqAs0.name: Glacial Stride

Arabuk.name: Arabuk

Arqsheth.description:
Believed to have once taken the shape of ballista-sized arbalests, arqsheths are living cannons who line the walls of Heaven to defend it against fiends. They often make themselves known to pure-hearted mortals who are either in the path of an imminent fiendish incursion or else struggling to vanquish a vile foe. They can be obsessively goal oriented and have been known to abandon a stalwart ally to pursue a fiend rather than delay the fight against their target.

Once an arqsheth destroys the object of their pursuit or determines that their wielder no longer needs their aid, they typically return to Heaven, but rare circumstances sometimes lead an arqsheth to remain in the Universe for an extended time. These arqsheths might find themselves embarking on long journeys with a loyal starship crew, standing guard over a seemingly abandoned planet, or taking up a post near a Drift beacon. They never reveal their motivation for remaining, and some suspect that arqsheths have a sort of sixth sense that warns of potential threats and leads them to take up such posts.

2q7Nf7IxDehPIMGz.name: +1 Status to All Saves vs. Magic

46IbVW4uWtGVHvAn.description:
The next time you make an attack roll before the end of your turn, roll it twice and use the better result. The attack ignores circumstance penalties to the attack roll and any flat check required due to the target being @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.DmAIPqOBomZ7H95W]{Concealed} or @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.iU0fEDdBp3rXpTMC]{Hidden}. You are then temporarily immune to sure strike for 10 minutes.

@UUID[Compendium.sf2e.spell-effects.Item.fpGDAz2v5PG0zUSl]{Spell Effect: Sure Strike}
46IbVW4uWtGVHvAn.name: Sure Strike (At Will)

8JCRtox1izdzZV2A.description: An arqsheth can be the target of spells that can target a ranged weapon, such as @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.spells.Item.SbBqa1HStMrV47fb]{Supercharge Weapon}, while wielded by another creature.
8JCRtox1izdzZV2A.name: Righteous Cannon

HasYa2qKz3JTG65H.description:
You instantly transport yourself and any items you're wearing and holding from your current space to an unoccupied space within range you can see. If this would bring another creature with you—even if you're carrying it in an extradimensional container—the spell is lost.

Heightened (5th) The range increases to 1 mile. You don't need to be able to see your destination, as long as you have been there in the past and know its relative location and distance from you. You are then temporarily immune for 1 hour.
HasYa2qKz3JTG65H.name: Translocate (At Will)

RIjTFgkgkCNInH0l.description:
The target can understand all words regardless of language and also speak the languages of other creatures. When in a mixed group of creatures, each time the target speaks, it can choose a creature and speak in a language that creature understands, even if the target doesn't know what language that is.

Heightened (7th) The duration is 8 hours.
RIjTFgkgkCNInH0l.name: Truespeech (Constant)

TAoyZEjmGNYgL9Ir.description:
Frequency once per day

Requirements The arqsheth saw another creature teleport within the last round

Effect The arqsheth casts @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.spells.Item.VlNcjmYyu95vOUe8]{Translocate}, which is heightened to 5th rank and causes the arqsheth to arrive in an unoccupied space they choose within 30 feet of the creature they're pursuing. If the creature is too far away, the arqsheth arrives as close as possible.
TAoyZEjmGNYgL9Ir.name: Archon's Pursuit

VfuCt4KoYbrHA5B8.description:
Trigger An enemy damages the archon's ally and both are within 15 feet of the archon

@UUID[Compendium.sf2e.bestiary-effects.Item.IsNnfuzanT5teGt4]{Effect: Archon's Protection}
VfuCt4KoYbrHA5B8.name: Archon's Protection

yhQ6aluReV5HuC08.description:
A single creature can wield an adjacent willing arqsheth as a free action as long as it has two free hands. Once wielded by another creature, an arqsheth can't be wielded by a different creature until the start of the arqsheth's next turn. While wielded as a weapon, an arqsheth counts as a martial ranged weapon that deals @Damage[2d10[fire]] damage; is in the laser group; has a range increment of 40 feet; and has the analog, holy, and tracking +2 traits. Strikes made with this weapon deal an extra @Damage[1d10[spirit]] damage. They don't require ammunition and have no Bulk, as they support their own weight.

@UUID[Compendium.sf2e.bestiary-effects.Item.c3Y1xZ6IIxbsnPk1]{Effect: Armament of the Archons}
yhQ6aluReV5HuC08.name: Armament of the Archons

Arqsheth.name: Arqsheth
Arqsheth.npcAllSaves: +1 status to all saves vs. magic

Assembly Ooze.description:
The assembly ooze is believed to have been created by accident when a manufacturing company attempted to automate an object printer as a cost cutting measure. The original creature has long since left containment in the Pact Worlds, replicating itself across the cosmos. While often considered a nuisance akin to pests of yore, an assembly ooze left unchecked on a starship or space station can eventually turn into an existential threat.

An assembly ooze typically takes the form of an amorphous metallic cube. It has an outer shell composed of a liquid polycarbonate slurry that encases a core of replicating nanobots. The ooze's color can change based on the materials it breaks down, but it's most often a metallic amalgamation of brown or gray. To survive, the ooze attempts to constantly disassemble technological items in following its programmed subroutines then manufacture something new. The nanites within an assembly ooze do have a drive for reproduction, splitting in a process similar to cellular mitosis when the ooze absorbs enough material in a short period of time. Assembly oozes generally don't assault those not carrying the technological items they require as fuel but do lash out to protect themselves.

Oozes of many types lurk in dark and abandoned places across the galaxy, emerging only to satiate their appetites and threaten adventurers, explorers, and hapless workers alike.

0okwUTmLml9OzTNq.description: The assembly ooze engulfs an adjacent, unattended piece of gear of no more than 4 Bulk, deconstructing it into its component parts. The ooze gains a number of UPBs equal to the item's price in credits. An assembly ooze can hold up to 1,000 UPBs at a time.
0okwUTmLml9OzTNq.name: Disassemble

irFF9j1SfAkN6reX.description: Over the course of 1 minute, the assembly ooze crafts a random piece of gear (rolling a [[/r 1d6]]: 1–armor, 2–shield, 3–weapon, 4–armor upgrade, 5–weapon upgrade, or 6–tech item) using the UPBs stored inside of it. An assembly ooze can craft items with a cost up to the UPBs stored, but with an item level and Bulk of no greater than 4 each.
irFF9j1SfAkN6reX.name: Assemble

n049RXks64f7pZ9b.description: An assembly ooze can detect creatures and objects with the tech trait as a precise sense within the listed range.
n049RXks64f7pZ9b.name: Techsense

wmpTexPNzpyn7Cfm.description:
Requirements The assembly ooze's last action was a successful pseudopod Strike

Effect The ooze attempts to [[/act disarm options=sticky-disarm]] the creature it hit. It gains a +4 status bonus to the Athletics check. This attempt neither applies nor counts toward the ooze's multiple attack penalty.
wmpTexPNzpyn7Cfm.name: Sticky Disarm

Assembly Ooze.name: Assembly Ooze

Asteray.description:
Thought to be merely mischievous tricksters, asterays are in fact fey born where the Void and First World overlap. Gifted with the innate ability to survive in space, asterays suffer from extreme wanderlust and an overwhelming desire to stave off boredom, with a desperate thirst for amusement being the prime motivation of most of their kind. They find themselves attracted to interesting stellar phenomena, from the swirls in gas giants to the interplay of stellar debris in an asteroid field. By floating through space, asterays gather enough sustenance to survive from their innate ability to consume latent cosmic radiation. However, asterays have one simple nutritional need that makes them a terror of the space lanes: organic matter. As space is all but devoid of organic elements for consumption, asterays resort to trailing starships, often by riding in their wake and tormenting the crew until they either abandon their posts or descend into chaos. Once an asteray has sufficiently driven a crew to despair, they enter the vessel and consume the corpses of the fallen.

Luckily—or perhaps not—for travelers, asterays typically find the consumption of living creatures distasteful, though their alien mindsets open them to using their vacuous ability to consume matter on active foes when threatened. Most asterays hibernate for months or even years at a time, floating in the wrecks of abandoned ships until the cosmic eddies of a passing ship stirs them from their torpor.

8gFyFocyC0h1elJA.description: The asteray opens their mouth to suck in the molecules of an adjacent organic creature or object of Small size or larger. If the target is an object (including a corpse), then the asteray regains @Damage[30[healing]] Hit Points and becomes @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.nlCjDvLMf2EkV2dl]{Quickened} 1 for the next minute, and they can use the extra action only to Climb, Fly, or Stride. If the target is a creature, then the target takes @Damage[10d8[void]] damage (@Check[fortitude|dc:32|basic] save).
8gFyFocyC0h1elJA.name: Matter Consumption

akzU6sPrDb9mE461.description: By touching a starship, an asteray can bond to the energy wake it leaves as it travels. The asteray can match speeds with the starship and ride along with it, treating the ship as if it were the "ground" so long as they remain within 100 feet. If the starship enters the Drift, the asteray can choose to accompany it into the Drift, or they can disengage as a reaction and remain behind.
akzU6sPrDb9mE461.name: Wake Rider

rm4SF5FOOnB6kHGr.description:
You create an illusory visual image of a stationary object. The entire image must fit within the spell's area. The object appears to animate naturally, but it doesn't make sounds or generate smells. For example, water would appear to pour down an illusory waterfall, but it would be silent.

Any creature that touches the image or uses the @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.actions.Item.BlAOM2X92SI6HMtJ]{Seek} action to examine it can attempt to disbelieve your illusion.

Heightened (2nd) Your image makes appropriate sounds, generates normal smells, and feels right to the touch. The spell gains the auditory and olfactory traits. The duration increases to 1 hour.

Heightened (5th) As the 2nd-rank version, but the duration is unlimited.
rm4SF5FOOnB6kHGr.name: Illusory Object (At Will)

vzS37pMGTiBUgZrP.description: An asteray can "sing" electronic signals that mask or mimic sensor readings. The asteray creates a false image of an object, as a 5th-rank @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.spells.Item.2oH5IufzdESuYxat]{Illusory Object} spell. This false reading affects only electronic sensors, but creatures hear odd echoes in the area so long as the effect persists. Multiple asterays can sing together, doubling the range and area of illusory object for each asteray casting the spell in sync.
vzS37pMGTiBUgZrP.name: Sensor Song

Asteray.name: Asteray

Athraxer.description:
Swarm invasions deploy athraxers as infantry. Fearless and violent, they're crucial for providing reconnaissance of a world's environment and defenses. A single Swarm ship can carry thousands of eggs in stasis.

Developing far out in the Vast from an insectile species known as kucharns, the Swarm is considered the greatest threat in existence for several cultures. Composed of countless subcolonies, each consisting of myriad component subspecies, the Swarm is a vast host that acts in psychic union for the purpose of consuming all matter across the cosmos. Most frightening of all is the Swarm's ability to assimilate the knowledge and DNA of those they consume. Thanks to its pre-Gap development of star travel, the Swarm had already consumed innumerable systems before history short-circuited, and the Swarm's pace only accelerated once it received access to the Signal and the hyperspace dimension known as the Drift.

Worlds touched by the Swarm are drained of their natural resources and rendered barren places known as huskworlds. What outsiders consider to be "Swarm space" is little more than a swathe of lifeless worlds that the Swarm have consumed in its reckless advance. The Swarm so thoroughly strips these worlds that surveyors struggle to find even trace amounts of inorganic resources, such as rare minerals and water. Few of these huskworlds have been thoroughly explored, as oftentimes exploration awakens inert drones, theorized to have been left behind in case the devoured system was ever colonized and repopulated. Pockets of Swarm activity exist well beyond this region of space, as the Swarm sent out countless subcolonies in the ages before the Gap, and even now, only some of them have reached their intended destinations.

The Swarm is perhaps most known in the current era for two important facts. First, its assault on the Pact Worlds and the Veskarium led to the cessation of hostilities and tenuous alliance between the two powers. Second, the Swarm is the direct ancestor of the shirren species. Having broken away sometime during the Gap, shirrens found succor with the deity Hylax, who was believed to have evolved from a pre-Swarm kucharn and who turned her back on the ravenous entity the Swarm has evolved into.

In recent years, the Swarm had been seen as little more than a distant boogeyman with no activities save for classified actions in the Suskillon system in the Vast. However, the recent discovery of the missing Szandite world of Krethiskar inadvertently awoke a dormant subcolony that had been responsible for the world's consumption. Since then, the newly dubbed Krethiskar subcolony has become a scourge of Near Space, engaged in an active invasion of Szandite Collective worlds and poised to spill over into other powers like the Veskarium and Pact Worlds. This rediscovered subcolony has begun rapid evolution of its components and remains cut off from the wider Swarm, but it still represents a clear danger to Near Space.

0EQjT6T5UVC9AtBU.description: An adjacent creature that deals slashing or piercing damage to the athraxer is sprayed with acidic blood and takes 2 persistent acid damage (@Check[reflex|dc:14|basic] save).
0EQjT6T5UVC9AtBU.name: Acid Blood

BYyXL1KBW7A1e2I5.description: An athraxer can sense nearby creatures through vibrations in air or water caused by movement as an imprecise sense at the listed range.
BYyXL1KBW7A1e2I5.name: Motion Sense

O8UfYZg0bXitmYzK.description:
Trigger The athraxer would die

Effect The athraxer first makes a claw Strike against a creature in reach, then dies.
O8UfYZg0bXitmYzK.name: Death Throe

UIQdaYb1yqgkkBJw.description: 30 feet. All allies with colony mind within the listed range of each other are in constant telepathic communication and are aware of all threats any individual knows about. While within range of at least one ally with colony mind, when a creature rolls a success on a save against a mental effect, it gets a critical success instead.
UIQdaYb1yqgkkBJw.name: Colony Mind

Athraxer.name: Athraxer

Atlapak.description:
Atlapaks are aquatic ambush predators renowned for their ability to create a sonic pulse that can stun or kill targets from hundreds of feet away. These enormous arthropods have banded shells, three compound eyes on movable stalks, a dexterous right claw for grasping and tearing, and an oversized, highly specialized left claw that generates a cavitation bubble when it snaps shut, which then implodes with crushing force. The atlapak uses plates on its carapace to direct the resulting sonic burst toward prey with uncanny accuracy.

Despite their animalistic intelligence, atlapaks have an instinctive understanding of ballistics and fluid dynamics. Their antennae detect subtle changes in currents and fluid density, allowing them to detect moving targets from a great distance and calibrate their cavitation blasts accordingly. Their compound eyes detect multiple wavelengths of light and provide incredible depth perception comparable to advanced sniper scopes.

Atlapaks prefer sheltered burrows that provide commanding views, such as coral reefs or low hills where they can conceal themselves and pick off prey at a distance. Though they typically stay in the silt of their underwater lairs, atlapaks can range far to mate. Historically, a spawning atlapak sticks fertilized eggs onto migrating megafauna that carry their offspring to new environs with unclaimed territory and resources. In the modern era, this behavior has led to eggs being stuck to the hulls of ships, where they can survive even in humid terrestrial environments. Juvenile atlapaks sometimes haunt a jungle or coast before returning to the safety of the ocean.

Atlapaks can grow up to 10 feet long, while juveniles are typically at least 5 feet long. Their predatory instincts kick in almost immediately after birth.

38FSW1r11mRRENhY.description: The atlapak can "swim" through the air in a thick atmosphere by inflating its lightweight body. Its fly Speed is reduced by half in a normal atmosphere, and it loses its fly Speed entirely while in an environment with a thin atmosphere or no atmosphere.
38FSW1r11mRRENhY.name: Aerial Buoyancy

7KVHhHuPffg36Gpl.description:
The atlapak makes a sonic snap Strike with a +1 circumstance bonus to its attack roll. The range increment for this Strike increases to 125 feet, and the Strike ignores up to 5 Hardness, or 250 feet and 10 Hardness in a thick atmosphere.

On a critical hit, the target must attempt a @Check[fortitude|dc:23] or @Check[fortitude|dc:25] save in a thick atmosphere.

Success The target is unaffected.

Failure The target is @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.dfCMdR4wnpbYNTix]{Stunned 1}.

Critical Failure The target is @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.dfCMdR4wnpbYNTix]{Stunned 2}.
7KVHhHuPffg36Gpl.name: Cavitation Blast

l94x8qFRD2pJfaBj.description: An atlapak's sonic snap is most effective in thick atmosphere or underwater. In normal or thin atmosphere, the range increments of its Cavitation Blast and sonic snap Strike are reduced by half, its Cavitation Blast ignores only up to 5 Hardness, and the DC for its Cavitation Blast decreases by 2. An atlapak's sonic snap Strike can't function in environments with no atmosphere.
l94x8qFRD2pJfaBj.name: Dense Atmosphere Dependent

Atlapak.name: Atlapak

Barachius Angel.description:
Barachius angels are imposing, helmed figures with glowing wings made of digital circuitry. They monitor the development of technology to prevent it from being used for malevolent purposes. Toward this divine end, their armaments have been blessed with holy energy. They can produce a retractable data blade that extends from their hand and that can be used to interface universally with computer terminals and data ports on robots.

Barachius angels serve as divine vanquishers to benevolent gods—purging technology across the Universe deemed to be twisted or evil. Their philosophies on what constitutes evil can be unclear, as these angels might hunt down an individual malfunctioning robot yet leave nuclear missile silos untouched.

While many angels in modern times ascended from mortal souls across the cosmos, these celestial beings were among the first creatures to exist in all the cosmos. Warriors and messengers of the gods, they're utterly devoted to their cause, whether that be destroying evil or spreading a deity's message across the galaxy.

1vT7a5z0iKB4nmZl.description:
The barachius makes a digital dagger Strike against an adjacent creature or item that has the tech trait.

On a hit, the target must attempt a @Check[will|dc:25|options:inflicts:controlled,inflicts:dazzled,inflicts:stunned] saving throw as the angel's holy influence attempts to seize control over it. A target with the holy trait use the outcome one degree of success better than the result of its roll, while one with the unholy trait uses the outcome one degree of success worse than the result of its roll.

Critical Success The target is unaffected.

Success The target's vision is filled with holy sigils and code, giving it the @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.TkIyaNPgTZFBCCuh]{Dazzled} condition until the end of its next turn.

Failure As success, and the target is also @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.dfCMdR4wnpbYNTix]{Stunned 1}.

Critical Failure The target's core processes are seized by the angel, giving the target the @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.9qGBRpbX9NEwtAAr]{Controlled} condition for 1 minute. While the target is controlled by the barachius, the angel can also use any of their spells as if it originated from the target rather than the angel. The target can attempt a new saving throw at the end of each of its turns to end the controlled condition.
1vT7a5z0iKB4nmZl.name: Angelic Override

OmJ5GILxtKZ7gdQ5.description: 20 feet. All creatures within the angel's aura gain a +1 status bonus to their AC and saving throws against attacks and effects from creatures and hazards with the unholy trait.
OmJ5GILxtKZ7gdQ5.name: Divine Farewell

VwOtsYKU0LS84nHn.description: In the hands of a barachius angel, all weapons gain the holy and magical traits and are powered by divine will, negating the need for batteries or ammunition.
VwOtsYKU0LS84nHn.name: Holy Arms

oAOb38ORVRhVNdgg.description:
The target can understand all words regardless of language and also speak the languages of other creatures. When in a mixed group of creatures, each time the target speaks, it can choose a creature and speak in a language that creature understands, even if the target doesn't know what language that is.

Heightened (7th) The duration is 8 hours.
oAOb38ORVRhVNdgg.name: Truespeech (Constant)

xAhuUFxKPOhdSnGJ.description:
Requirements You have a planar key for the destination plane, used as a locus

You and your allies traverse the barriers between planes of existence. The targets move to another plane, such as the Plane of Fire, the Netherworld, or the Outer Rifts. You must know the destination plane exists and use a magic planar key created from material from that plane as a locus for the spell. While the planar keys for most prominent planes are uncommon, just like the spell interplanar teleport, more obscure planes and demiplanes often have rare or possibly even unique planar keys.

The spell is highly imprecise, and you appear 1d20×25 miles from the last place one of the targets (of your choice) was located the last time that target traveled to the plane. If it's the first time traveling to a particular plane for all targets, you appear at a random location on the plane. Interplanar teleport doesn't provide a means of return travel, though casting interplanar teleport again allows you to return to your previous plane unless there are extenuating circumstances.
xAhuUFxKPOhdSnGJ.name: Interplanar Teleport (Self Only)

Barachius Angel.name: Barachius Angel

Bastorox.description:

A5QfAfgM1tM12aSS.description: The bastorox unleashes a bolt of bioelectric energy from its arm blade. The bolt deals @Damage[6d8[electricity]|options:area-damage] damage to all creatures in a @Template[type:line|distance:30] with a @Check[reflex|dc:22|basic|options:area-effect] save. The bastorox can't use Bioelectric Jolt again for [[/gmr 1d4 #Recharge Bioelectric Jolt]]{1d4 rounds}.

lJnuIl8RHv6yf5q8.name: Colony Mind

sXgOAZKebKXiTtuq.description: A bastorox's battering arm can also be used as a shield (Hardness 5, 30 HP, BT 15). If the shield is destroyed, the bastorox takes a –2 circumstance penalty to attack rolls made with its battering arm Strikes. A destroyed shield arm regenerates over the course of 24 hours.
sXgOAZKebKXiTtuq.name: Shield Arm

Bastorox.name: Bastorox

Biotech Advanced War Machine.description:
Strong and ferocious, code name "thermatrod" is designed to maximize carnage and destruction on a battlefield. In contrast, the "vracinea" is among the weakest of the unidentified biotech war machines observed in the Pact Worlds. Sleek and stealthy, it darts in and out of enemy defenses while transmitting data to its pilot before departing. If discovered, the vracinea consumes itself to destroy records of the data it was carrying.

The incursion began with a series of probes detected by anacites on Aballon. Strange machines with blazing sensors and articulated tentacles appeared out of nowhere, ripping through infrastructure seemingly at random and collecting intelligence all around Pact Worlds space. Panic spread fast, but since the machines always vanished without a trace, or exploded when captured, the sightings couldn't be confirmed or identified. Rumors began to circulate that the machines were a form of biotech never encountered before. Soon the Stewards became formally involved, shuttering the incidents behind the adamantine partition of top security clearance.

In Sarenith of 325 ag, after dozens of military operations failed to engage the elusive probes, a wing of fighters dispatched from the Idari finally got lucky and disabled one of the machines before it could self-destruct. Coaxed into giving up some of its secrets by top Pact Worlds scientists, the biotech vessel became the prototype for the "home grown" remote war machines that are currently being tested for use in combat. The replicas aren't alive but are built using robotic construction templates since the core of the original biotech design has proven too complicated to reverse engineer with Pact technology.

Remote war machines are proxies that can be controlled from a great distance. The original biotech war machines connect to the pilot's mind through a psychic link or unknown radio frequency. Robotic remote war machines connect to a computer via data link, allowing the pilot to control their proxy using a keyboard, virtual reality rig, or even a vidgame controller.

0kuHDDei4DUVdhn3.description: The war machine Steps or Strides twice. The war machine gains a +10-foot circumstance bonus to its Speed during these moves.
0kuHDDei4DUVdhn3.name: Hypersonic Burst

BI95beS68v2FG2iI.description:
Trigger The war machine would be reduced to 0 Hit Points

Effect The war machine self-destructs, dealing @Damage[8d6[electricity]|options:area-damage] damage (@Check[reflex|dc:25|basic|options:area-effect] save) to all creatures in a 60-foot radius. For 1 minute after this ability is used, any creature that touches the war machine's remains is exposed to incredible radiation sickness.
BI95beS68v2FG2iI.name: Corpse Flower

Biotech Giant.description:
For eons, these giants traveled across the stars searching for a home. While exploring a potential new home in the Vast, they were overrun by a strange fungus that consumed everything they touched. The giants' size protected them from immediate annihilation, but most could only watch as the mycelium's blue-green tendrils covered their new home. In desperation, the giants devoted all their resources to science to find some way to eradicate the fungus. Instead, they learned how to adapt. The giants began living symbiotically with the fungus, grafting it onto their skin and incorporating it into their technology. Now, these giants explore the galaxy as scientists and preservers of myriad ecosystems. While they're most often found providing their scientific expertise to other species, a growing movement of daredevil explorers known as sporerunners travel some of the most dangerous locations in the galaxy on a quest to find a planet they can call home.

Giants are enormous humanoids of many varieties who live all across the galaxy.

YHSRSyFhTG2krB4P.description: When the biotech giant Strikes a creature with their mycelial whip or spore cannon, they leave some of the fungus behind, which immediately attempts to graft itself onto the targeted creature. The affected creature must attempt a @Check[fortitude|dc:28] save; on a failure, its implanted augmentations that count toward its implant limit cease to function for [[/gmr 1d4 #rounds]]{1d4 rounds}.
YHSRSyFhTG2krB4P.name: Mycelial Rewiring

c5hKWcmIx1UxZCIa.description: 10 feet. Any creature entering or starting its turn in the aura takes @Damage[5d8[electricity]|options:area-damage] damage (@Check[fortitude|dc:28|basic|options:area-effect] save). When the giant Steps or Strides, they end their current aura and leave behind fungal ground cover in those spaces, starting a new aura at the beginning of their next turn.
c5hKWcmIx1UxZCIa.name: Electrified Mycelium

iMbwa09gJvbrz4x0.description: Any creature that starts its turn in an area of fungal ground cover must succeed at a @Check[reflex|dc:26|options:area-effect,damaging-effect] save or take @Damage[3d8[electricity]|options:area-damage] damage. This area is also difficult terrain for creatures other than biotech giants and fungus. Any amount of fire damage automatically destroys a square of fungal ground cover.
iMbwa09gJvbrz4x0.name: Fungal Ground Cover

Biotech Superior War Machine.description:
Devised by engineers based on Kalo-Mahoi, the robotic war machine, code name "atlapak," was built for aquatic warfare. Just like its amphibious creators, the atlapak is equally proficient on land. Code name "ksarik" was first observed in a terrifying attack on a Diasporan mining outpost operated by Ulrikka Clanholdings. When unfurled for battle, the ksarik becomes a mass of spiked tentacles and glaring red sensors that can tear through platoons of troopers in minutes.

The incursion began with a series of probes detected by anacites on Aballon. Strange machines with blazing sensors and articulated tentacles appeared out of nowhere, ripping through infrastructure seemingly at random and collecting intelligence all around Pact Worlds space. Panic spread fast, but since the machines always vanished without a trace, or exploded when captured, the sightings couldn't be confirmed or identified. Rumors began to circulate that the machines were a form of biotech never encountered before. Soon the Stewards became formally involved, shuttering the incidents behind the adamantine partition of top security clearance.

In Sarenith of 325 ag, after dozens of military operations failed to engage the elusive probes, a wing of fighters dispatched from the Idari finally got lucky and disabled one of the machines before it could self-destruct. Coaxed into giving up some of its secrets by top Pact Worlds scientists, the biotech vessel became the prototype for the "home grown" remote war machines that are currently being tested for use in combat. The replicas aren't alive but are built using robotic construction templates since the core of the original biotech design has proven too complicated to reverse engineer with Pact technology.

Remote war machines are proxies that can be controlled from a great distance. The original biotech war machines connect to the pilot's mind through a psychic link or unknown radio frequency. Robotic remote war machines connect to a computer via data link, allowing the pilot to control their proxy using a keyboard, virtual reality rig, or even a vidgame controller.

Biotech Ultimate War Machine.description:
Only one member of the Stewards has ever encountered the biotechnical horror known as code name "moonflower" and lived to tell the tale—and only after they emerged from a months-long coma. According to her story, a single moonflower war machine was responsible for the massacre of Liavaran moon S-117, which used to house an entire Stewards deep space telescope array and planetary defense battery.

The incursion began with a series of probes detected by anacites on Aballon. Strange machines with blazing sensors and articulated tentacles appeared out of nowhere, ripping through infrastructure seemingly at random and collecting intelligence all around Pact Worlds space. Panic spread fast, but since the machines always vanished without a trace, or exploded when captured, the sightings couldn't be confirmed or identified. Rumors began to circulate that the machines were a form of biotech never encountered before. Soon the Stewards became formally involved, shuttering the incidents behind the adamantine partition of top security clearance.

In Sarenith of 325 ag, after dozens of military operations failed to engage the elusive probes, a wing of fighters dispatched from the Idari finally got lucky and disabled one of the machines before it could self-destruct. Coaxed into giving up some of its secrets by top Pact Worlds scientists, the biotech vessel became the prototype for the "home grown" remote war machines that are currently being tested for use in combat. The replicas aren't alive but are built using robotic construction templates since the core of the original biotech design has proven too complicated to reverse engineer with Pact technology.

Remote war machines are proxies that can be controlled from a great distance. The original biotech war machines connect to the pilot's mind through a psychic link or unknown radio frequency. Blight Drake.description:
Blight drakes have a well-earned reputation among draconic creatures for stench and pollution. They corrupt the air around them with the sort of filth and decay commonly found in the worst kinds of industrialization. These solitary monstrosities resemble their swamp-dwelling draconic cousins but are often surrounded with a miasma of thick, choking smog. Blight drakes revel in befouling clean and verdant environments, leaving a permanent trail of filth in their wake.

Drakes resemble their larger draconic cousins in more than just scaled, monstrous acclaim. Ranging in size from the diminutive fey drake to the massive, ship-sized star drake, drakes share a dragons' winged reptilian form, long necks, and breath weapons. But where dragons often have forelimbs and wings, a drake typically only has one or the other. Their long, winding tails and sharp jaws more than make up for this lack, however.

Despite being more animalistic than dragons, drakes still possess a formidable cunning, and most share a dragon's ability to generate some form of breath weapon. However, their lack of intelligence makes drakes substantially easier to domesticate than other draconic creatures, and their familial nature makes them excellent pack hunters.

2Zih3fIVn3fzj4uE.description:
The blight drake blasts a thick, fetid smog from slits around their neck, creating a cloud of smoke in a @Template[type:burst|distance:20] within 120 feet and that remains for [[/gmr 1d4 #rounds]]{1d4 rounds}. All creatures within the cloud become @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.DmAIPqOBomZ7H95W]{Concealed}, and all creatures outside the cloud become concealed to creatures in it.

Each creature that begins its turn inside the cloud takes @Damage[5d6[poison]|options:area-damage] damage (@Check[fortitude|dc:28|basic|options:area-effect,inflicts:sickened] save). A creature that fails the save is also @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.fesd1n5eVhpCSS18]{Sickened 1} (@UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.fesd1n5eVhpCSS18]{Sickened 2} on a critical failure).
2Zih3fIVn3fzj4uE.name: Smokestack

Creatures within the burst take @Damage[4d8[acid],4d8[poison]|options:area-damage] damage (@Check[reflex|dc:28|basic|options:area-effect] save). The blight drake can't use Toxic Breath again for [[/gmr 1d4 #Recharge Toxic Breath]]{1d4 rounds}.
6nCW9Q14DvQJ9hlt.name: Toxic Breath

h0WC8jGOemx0AOrC.name: Grisly Ambush

Botnib.description:
The lowly botnib, also called a computer glitch gremlin, is intuitively tied with the computerized devices and networks of the modern age. These cavorting fey make it their mission to create as much havoc as they can by influencing computer systems and creating chaos in their wake. Known for their innate ability to communicate with digital devices, computer glitch gremlins routinely become infatuated with such systems, which they subvert like one might put together a fun puzzle.

Gremlins have plagued the Universe with cruel tricks since long before the Gap, and they've fully adapted to a galaxy filled with technology. Whether meddling with a comm unit, a starship, or an entire space station, gremlins delight in ruination and chaos.

6uu9usooH9Eea7c7.description: A botnib can communicate telepathically with digital devices and with other creatures that can do so (such as other botnibs). This allows the botnib to attempt Computers checks to access any computer within the telepathy's range.
6uu9usooH9Eea7c7.name: Digital Telepathy

Caypin.description: Caypins are brawny predators with the agility of wolves and the scaly skin of crocodiles. Their most striking feature is a mass of wriggling, semi-sentient appendages that cover their heads. Each of these tentacle-like protuberances contains a bloodshot eyeball and a gaping mouth full of teeth, and the caypin—which has no eyes or mouth of its own—relies on these orifices to see and feed. Nutrients absorbed by the appendages are passed to the caypin via tiny receptive sockets in the beast's jaw, and caypins can detach these appendages into writhing clusters that independently move up to 100 feet from their bodies. In the wild, caypins use these clusters to ambush prey, and the creatures are known across the galaxy for their rapacious ability to consume half of their body weight in raw meat.

NpP3zOVmiMsuM8L5.description:
A caypin's detached appendage cluster is a Small, mindless, semi-independent creature controlled by the caypin. It has the minion trait, darkvision, @Damage[30[healing]] Hit Points, a land Speed of 20 feet, and a swim Speed of 15 feet. It shares the caypin's AC, saving throw bonuses, and skill modifiers. The caypin can see what its appendage cluster sees and otherwise shares its senses with the cluster. Each round, the caypin can Command a Minion to grant an appendage cluster 2 actions. An appendage cluster can make jaws Strikes (Melee 1 jaws +14, Damage 2d4+3 piercing) and has the Cluster Onslaught ability.

If the caypin is killed, any detached appendage clusters are also killed. Any appendage cluster that moves more than 100 feet from the caypin dies instantly.

If both the caypin's detached appendage clusters are destroyed but the caypin still lives, the caypin is @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.XgEqL1kFApUbl5Z2]{Blinded} until it regrows at least one of its appendage clusters. A dead appendage cluster regrows in 3 days.
NpP3zOVmiMsuM8L5.name: Appendage Cluster

XVxGbnXkfbD5JpuD.name: Aquatic Ambush

A caypin can have up to two appendage clusters detached at a time, and if both clusters are detached, the caypin can't make jaws Strikes or Detach Cluster again until at least one cluster reattaches. An adjacent appendage cluster can reattach to the caypin with an Interact action.

Caypin.name: Caypin

Cerebinite.description:
The mineral cerebinium, also known as memory crystal, naturally appears in the broken region of space known as Kazmurg's Absurdity. Typically, these minerals develop in remote subterranean locations, where they grow based on the presence of thinking minds within a planetary range. The more active minds in a region, the faster these mineral formations grow. A major world of millions can easily create vast underground stores, and in these majestic caverns, cerebinites spontaneously emerge.

Cerebinites are essentially mindless creatures—save for the memories that power them—who have developed as an offshoot of cerebinium growth. Though possessing no intellect of their own, they act off the impulses provided by the memories stored within the crystals that constitute their forms. In many ways, a cerebinite is like the many oozes that lie in wait throughout the cosmos.

Encountering these active mineral deposits often requires a delicate approach, as cerebinites can engage up close or at a short range by hurling cerebinium spikes and blasts of cerebinium shards charged with memories drawn from their surroundings. Even in death, these masses of cerebinium explode in a destructive burst of psychic energy, affecting the minds of those nearby with jumbled visions of countless different lives. When multiple injured cerebinites gather near one another, this proximity can cause an especially destructive chain reaction due to cerebinites' own susceptibility to mental attacks.

JqJ0EQynJMKW7MnZ.description:

Requirements Initiative hasn't yet been rolled

Effect The cerebinite automatically notices the creature, makes a crystalline growth Strike against one creature adjacent to itself, then rolls initiative.
JqJ0EQynJMKW7MnZ.name: Crystalline Ambush

L2bjATFhfFPhKBsz.description: When the cerebinite dies, it explodes in a blast fueled by the memories stored in its crystalline body, affecting all creatures in a @Template[emanation|distance:30]. Each creature in the area (including other cerebinites) must succeed at a @Check[will|dc:22|options:area-effect,inflicts:stunned] save or take @Damage[2d8[mental]|options:area-damage] damage and become @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.dfCMdR4wnpbYNTix]{Stunned 1} (or double damage and @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.dfCMdR4wnpbYNTix]{Stunned 2} on a critical failure).
L2bjATFhfFPhKBsz.name: Mind-Shattering Demise

esvM5ScHKH1XRqsl.description: Creatures that take mental damage are also @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.xYTAsEpcJE1Ccni3]{Slowed 1} for 1 round on a critical failure
esvM5ScHKH1XRqsl.name: Blast of Cerebinium Shards

Cerebinite.name: Cerebinite

Civusdaemon.description:
Born from infospheres and digital networks, the civusdaemon is a force of malign intent who bends online spaces to torment mortals. Representing death through oppression and hate from social media, these daemons act in the shadows, tormenting their foes to such a ruinous extent that they often take their own life.

Hailing from the plane of Abaddon, daemons are utterly devoted to the destruction of all life. Their existence is based around specific means of death, and they seek the death of all things in service to their lords: the Apocalypse Riders. Each daemon represents a different way to die, and they use their specific powers to further that means of death.

Advents in technology have only created new means of death and torment, so new types of daemons enter existence with regularity, each created once a sufficient mass of new deaths occurs to spawn them. These new advent daemons often prefer to spend their time in the galaxy rather than Abaddon, as they can better spread their torments to the mortals of creation.

If the invisible creature uses a hostile action against anyone who isn't the target that can see them, the spell ends after that hostile action is completed.

Heightened (5th) You can make up to 6 willing creatures within 30 feet invisible, but they all must have the same target.
FJsxjXLWZbdzvlwP.name: Selective Invisibility (At Will)

A creature who succeeds at this check automatically succeeds at further such flat checks for 1 round.
HSeKciJujlsJmVfc.name: Profile Picture
