Effect The attack becomes a hit instead of a critical hit, or the critical failure on the save becomes a failure instead.
M152qYUcKKR9btjd.name: Well, Actually

TbZOlmRNpGPCO0Ix.description: A civusdaemon knows the presence of any creatures connected to any local infospheres it has access to. A creature who is connected to an infosphere is visible to the civusdaemon as a precise sense. Disconnected creatures who've been active on an infosphere within the past day leave enough residual trace that a civusdaemon can sense them as an imprecise sense.
TbZOlmRNpGPCO0Ix.name: Eyes on the Infosphere

bFXjf0ML8ktO8IBB.name: +1 Status to All Saves vs. Mental

nBKzlpRbYMs1omod.description:
The civusdaemon targets the online reputation of a creature it's aware of on a shared infosphere. After 1 day of downtime, the civusdaemon attempts a @Check[computers|defense:computers] check against the target's Computers DC.

If successful, the target takes a –2 circumstance penalty to all checks made on that infosphere because of damage to their reputation. The civusdaemon can maintain this effect each day by spending another day of downtime without needing to attempt an additional check.

If the civusdaemon maintains this for a week or more, the penalty increases to –4. The creature or an ally of the creature can spend a day of downtime to attempt a @Check[computers|dc:26], @Check[deception|dc:26] or @Check[diplomacy|dc:26] check to counter the character attack.

On a success, the civusdaemon's efforts end, and the target becomes immune to this ability for 1 month.

On a critical success, the target or ally also identifies a specific location that the civusdaemon operates out of, such as one where it frequently connects to the infosphere.
nBKzlpRbYMs1omod.name: Character Assassination

oaHRIhX1FIPkn6ih.description:
You magically broadcast grim news onto nearby devices, holo projectors, screens, and other displays (including comm units on armor). Creatures in the area who can see one or more displays must attempt a Will save.

Critical Success The creature is unaffected.

Success The creature is @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.AdPVz7rbaVSRxHFg]{Fascinated} by the display.

Failure The creature is fascinated by the display and @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 2} (even if the fascination ends).

Critical Failure The creature is fascinated by the display, @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 3}, and @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.3uh1r86TzbQvosxv]{Doomed 1} (even if the fascination ends).
oaHRIhX1FIPkn6ih.name: Doom Scroll (At Will)

Civusdaemon.name: Civusdaemon
Civusdaemon.npcAllSaves: +1 status to all saves vs. mental

Clangit.description:
Clangits, or space station gremlins, know everything about the inner workings of their home stations and enjoy punishing or pranking the station's larger inhabitants who know less than they do. "Haunted" space stations and ships with mysterious power flickers, doors that randomly open and shut, equipment that malfunctions at just the wrong time, and frequent unexplainable accidents are probably the home of one or more clangits.

When they aren't playing pranks, some clangits monitor and repair the sensitive machinery keeping many older space stations afloat—a fact that has probably saved them from eradication on larger settlements like Absalom Station. Most clangits stand about 2 feet tall and weigh around 7 pounds—the perfect size for slipping through vents and squeezing down maintenance tunnels.

Gremlins have plagued the Universe with cruel tricks since long before the Gap, and they've fully adapted to a galaxy filled with technology. Whether meddling with a comm unit, a starship, or an entire space station, gremlins delight in ruination and chaos.

26e94RXZIquzqk4r.description: When a clangit has spent at least 1 hour exploring a ship or space station, the gremlin gains an innate sense of its inner workings and can remotely control mechanical infrastructure within 60 feet, performing simple actions such as opening and shutting airlocks and doors, opening heat vents, activating alarms, turning lights on and off, or tampering with gravity controls.
26e94RXZIquzqk4r.name: Mechanical Trickery

OiQhuNpUxinMeyTs.description: The clangit enters adjacent mechanical infrastructure, such as a control panel or pipe network, and instantly emerges from another within 100 feet.
OiQhuNpUxinMeyTs.name: Tech Travel

Clangit.name: Clangit

Cloud Ray.description: Enormous cloud rays are apex predators on gas giants such as Bretheda and Liavara. Cloud rays are incredibly maneuverable and can fly through the atmosphere at speeds few can match, rendering them nearly inescapable when on the hunt.

98fygCslZZaeLMZI.description: The cloud ray makes two consecutive tail lash Strikes at a –2 penalty against any targets within reach. These attacks count toward the cloud ray's multiple attack penalty, but the multiple attack penalty doesn't increase until after it makes all its attacks.
98fygCslZZaeLMZI.name: Lash Out

HFWt0uRFQyXWxanb.description:
Frequency once per hour

Effect Until the beginning of its next turn, the cloud ray gains a +80-foot status bonus to its fly Speed and deals an additional 1d10 slashing damage with its tail Strikes.
HFWt0uRFQyXWxanb.name: Natural Thruster

c7ZeUIk7gcAPNqhu.description: A creature that takes electricity damage from a cloud ray's tail Strike is @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.dfCMdR4wnpbYNTix]{Stunned 1} (@UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.dfCMdR4wnpbYNTix]{Stunned 2} on a critical hit), then becomes temporarily immune to stunning lash for 1 minute. Creatures with a weakness to electricity don't become temporarily immune.
c7ZeUIk7gcAPNqhu.name: Stunning Lash

eGmvSl1SL37Xx9G2.description: If a cloud ray dies due to fire or electricity damage, its internal reservoirs of explosive gases and combustible fluids detonate in a @Template[type:emanation|distance:20] that deals @Damage[11d8[fire]|options:area-damage] damage (@Check[reflex|dc:30|basic|options:area-effect] save).
eGmvSl1SL37Xx9G2.name: Explosive Death

Cloud Ray.name: Cloud Ray

Cloud Skate.description: Cloud skates are skittish creatures that avoid settlements whenever possible. They travel in large packs when in their docile periods and remain in small groups even during their aggressive hunting cycles, making them dangerous to travelers. They navigate through the clouds using three powerful tails, trapping prey with huge, baleen-filled mouths that span the full width of their single-segmented bodies.

1GUs6pHk0o5TrpRL.description:
Frequency once per hour

Effect Until the beginning of its next turn, the cloud skate gains a +75-foot status bonus to its fly Speed and deals an additional 1d10 slashing damage with its tail Strikes.
1GUs6pHk0o5TrpRL.name: Natural Thruster

hZTrWR3unDlaRpxj.description: If a cloud skate dies due to fire or electricity damage, its internal reservoirs of explosive gases and combustible fluids detonate in a @Template[type:emanation|distance:20] that deals @Damage[6d8[fire]|options:area-damage] damage (@Check[reflex|dc:21|basic|options:area-effect] save).
hZTrWR3unDlaRpxj.name: Explosive Death

Cloud Skate.name: Cloud Skate

Collapsing Structure.description:
The kyokor (or other kaiju) grazes a structure, severely compromising the building's stability and possibly causing it to collapse.

When a kyokor passes by or through a settlement—or even attacks!—it leaves a trail of destruction that can be represented by the following hazards.

Terrifying, skyscraper-sized beasts roam the wastelands of Daimalko. Called colossi by the population, these monsters erupted from deep within the earth to stomp cities into dust, decimating the population and destroying every surface civilization on the planet in a terrifying Awakening. Kyokors are among the most dreaded colossi. There's no hope of defeating one without a valko—a war machine created by Daimalko's stubborn survivors to fight the colossi.
Collapsing Structure.hazardDisable: @Check[athletics|dc:43] (master), @Check[civil-engineering-lore|dc:43] (master), or @Check[crafting|dc:43] (master) check to brace the structure to reduce the risk of collapse until the end of the creature's next turn. The DC of the flat check for this round (see Routine) is increased by 4 on a success, or by 8 on a critical success. Increasing the flat check DC to 21 or higher stabilizes the structure, ending this hazard.
Collapsing Structure.hazardReset: The building becomes susceptible to Demolish again [[/gmr 1d6 #rounds]]{1d6 rounds} after it's stabilized.
Collapsing Structure.hazardRoutine: (1 action) The GM rolls a @Check[flat|dc:9] to determine if the building collapses, increasing the DC as listed in Disable. On a success, dust and debris fall within the building and 30 feet around it, providing concealment and dealing @Damage[6d6[bludgeoning]] damage to [[/gmr 1d4 #Targets]] randomly chosen targets (@Check[reflex|dc:35|basic] save); on a critical failure, a creature is also knocked @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.j91X7x0XSomq8d60]{Prone}. On a critical success on the flat check, the effect is the same, but the debris deals @Damage[12d6[bludgeoning]] damage to [[/gmr 2d4 #Targets]] randomly chosen targets instead (@Check[reflex|dc:35|basic] save); on a critical failure, a creature is knocked prone and @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.VcDeM8A5oI6VqhbM]{Restrained} by rubble until freed ([[/act force-open dc=38]]; [[/act escape dc=35]]).
Collapsing Structure.name: Collapsing Structure

Coposirix.description: The rapid and careless industrialization of Tabrid Minor ruined the planet, particularly ravaging the population of copi—the coral that's the ancestor of the native copaxi people. In areas where the copi's magical connection to gravity was strongest, however, the rampant pollution instead mutated it into grotesque new forms. In a twisted mockery of copaxi evolution, clusters of copi fused together to form coposirixes, shambling mounds of mutated copi fused with a partial shell of crystallized waste that crackles and creaks as it moves. The form of a coposirix constantly changes, sometimes even taking on hauntingly humanoid features that melt away just as quickly.

FZbaJ1a8nCxQGjci.description:
The coposirix bends gravity around itself, causing it to fall toward its target. The coposirix Strides up to twice its Speed in a straight line in any direction. If it ends this movement within melee reach of at least one enemy, it can make a battering sludge Strike against that target. After this attack, the coposirix falls if it isn't on a solid surface, taking half the normal amount of damage for the distance fallen and not falling @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.j91X7x0XSomq8d60]{Prone}. If the coposirix passes within 10 feet of another creature at any point during this movement, that creature is affected by the fluctuating gravity and must attempt a @Check[reflex|dc:25] save.

Critical Success The creature can use the fluctuating gravity to its advantage to reposition itself. It can Step as a free action.

Success No effect.

Failure The creature is pulled 5 feet in the direction of the coposirix's travel. This follows the rules for forced movement. If at the end of this movement the creature is unsupported, it falls and lands prone, taking fall damage as normal.

Critical Failure As failure, but the creature is pulled 10 feet and falls prone even if supported.
FZbaJ1a8nCxQGjci.name: Falling Rush

X3KSW46iLG1a3m06.description:
Trigger The coposirix takes damage

Effect The coposirix's body absorbs some of what damaged it until the end of its next turn, the material seeping into its constituent copi and changing its composition. The effects of this change depends on the nature of the damage.

  • Energy Damage The coposirix's attacks deal an additional 2d6 damage of the same type as the energy damage dealt to it.

  • Physical Damage The coposirix gains resistance 6 to physical damage. If the damage was dealt by a weapon made of a special material, such as silver, the coposirix's battering sludge Strike counts as that same material for the duration of the effect.
X3KSW46iLG1a3m06.name: Seep In

Coposirix.name: Coposirix

Corchaaz.description:
The crab-like corchaazes of Tabrid Minor build their shells from copi, a coral-like polyp that also constitutes the bodies of humanoid copaxis. Copi contain hollows that collapse matter into dense stores, creating pressurized chambers that emulate black holes. Corchaazes break down copi with their claws and add the material to their shells, creating gravity wells on their bodies. Corchaazes are effectively immortal unless they die of injury or illness. Legend has it their shells continue to grow as they age—copaxi folk tales describe corchaazes as big as islands.

A coastal shelf collapse on Tabrid Minor in 322 ag destroyed the planet's major corchaaz spawning ground, but this wasn't the end for this hardy species. In 324 ag, a team of scientists in a nearby star system noticed wildly fluctuating gravimetric readings. Following the weird readings, the scientists discovered and tracked a group of corchaazes traveling along a local Drift lane. Corchaaz migrations were new, and many scientists were eager to study rafts, as the migratory groups were called. More corchaaz rafts showed up the following year in other systems, including the Ghavaniska and Pact Systems.

DqPpcoLRP7tbxYZi.description: The corchaaz raises a gravitational barrier around its copi shell and gains @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.DmAIPqOBomZ7H95W]{Concealment} against all creatures for 1 round.
DqPpcoLRP7tbxYZi.name: Copi Concealment

FAuvMe0Fh4IVLVQj.description:
A corchaaz can combine its gravitational forces with other willing corchaazes into an interstellar raft as an exploration activity that takes 10 minutes. While part of an interstellar raft, the corchaazes must remain within 100 feet of each other. Additionally, the raft members gain a 40-foot fly Speed and the cosmic trait (both of which they keep for 1 hour after this ability ends). An individual corchaaz can Dismiss the raft, which detaches all combined corchaazes. If half or more of the raft members die, the interstellar raft ends.

@UUID[Compendium.sf2e.bestiary-effects.Item.2UI9dt0QM2VEvpJV]{Effect: Interstellar Raft}
FAuvMe0Fh4IVLVQj.name: Interstellar Raft

JMTqSE3bVSwAvyUs.description: 20 feet. The corchaaz's body pulls nearby creatures toward it with dense gravitational forces. A creature that ends it turn within the aura must succeed at a @Check[reflex|dc:20|options:area-effect,forced-movement,inflicts:prone] save or be pulled 10 feet toward the corchaaz (also landing @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.j91X7x0XSomq8d60]{Prone} on a critical failure).
JMTqSE3bVSwAvyUs.name: Gravity Well

zBt6q6EcgZnPjFpY.description:
The corchaaz attempts to lock a creature within 40 feet into place with gravitational forces. The target must attempt a @Check[fortitude|dc:20] save.

Critical Success The target is unaffected.

Success The target takes a –5-foot status penalty to its Speeds until the end of its next turn.

Failure The target becomes @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.dfCMdR4wnpbYNTix]{Stunned 1}.

Critical Failure The target is @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.6uEgoh53GbXuHpTF]{Paralyzed} for 1 round.
zBt6q6EcgZnPjFpY.name: Graviton Grip

Corchaaz.name: Corchaaz

Corpse Fleet Infantry.description:
The Corpse Fleet's rank and file infantry are trained to work as a unit.

The Corpse Fleet is an army made up of undead supremacists who refuse to bow to the will of the living. Founded by defectors from the Eoxian navy, the Corpse Fleet aims to shatter Pact Worlds unity and liberate Eox from the influence of the living and those bone sages who sided with them. Unyielding and utterly ruthless, the Corpse Fleet deals in death and destruction, feeding on the living and exploiting the dead.

4tc8In6JzRT2PZ3N.description:
Trigger An adjacent ally moves away from the Corpse Fleet infantry

Effect The Corpse Fleet infantry Strides up to half their Speed. They must move in the same direction as the triggering ally.
4tc8In6JzRT2PZ3N.name: Coordinated Shuffle

zDhm0Ul1KIbLhKYB.description: The Corpse Fleet infantry's ranged Strikes deal an additional 1d4 precision damage when the Corpse Fleet infantry is within the first range increment of at least one other member of the Corpse Fleet wielding a ranged weapon.
zDhm0Ul1KIbLhKYB.name: Fusillade

Corpse Fleet Infantry.name: Corpse Fleet Infantry

Corpse Fleet Officer.description:
A Corpse Fleet officer is a bold combat leader who bolsters their undead allies and has trained to destroy the living.

The Corpse Fleet is an army made up of undead supremacists who refuse to bow to the will of the living. Founded by defectors from the Eoxian navy, the Corpse Fleet aims to shatter Pact Worlds unity and liberate Eox from the influence of the living and those bone sages who sided with them. Unyielding and utterly ruthless, the Corpse Fleet deals in death and destruction, feeding on the living and exploiting the dead.

AAC7KNUZzlLr0lCN.description: The Corpse Fleet officer makes a ranged or melee Strike against a creature. Each undead within 100 feet of the officer can immediately use a reaction and expend ammunition from a ranged weapon they're wielding equal to its expend value to increase the damage of Lead Salvo by @Damage[1d4[void]] damage for each undead ally, to a maximum of an additional @Damage[4d4[void]] damage.
AAC7KNUZzlLr0lCN.name: Lead Salvo

Bj8yOLKbm7xVqHvz.description:
20 feet. Undead that begin their turn in the aura (including the Corpse Fleet officer) gain 8 temporary Hit Points for 1 hour, then become temporarily immune to bolstering aura for 1 hour.

@UUID[Compendium.sf2e.bestiary-effects.Item.ZWOPndNX0EIhYCG9]{Effect: Bolstering Aura}
Bj8yOLKbm7xVqHvz.name: Bolstering Aura

YXj0OZhv8lJ8AfS6.description: The Corpse Fleet officer has trained to decimate the living. Their Strikes deal an additional 1d6 void damage.
YXj0OZhv8lJ8AfS6.name: Decimate the Living

qr1s3bZrWNgIX3du.description: The Corpse Fleet officer makes one ranged Strike and one melee Strike in any order. These attacks count toward their multiple attack penalty, but the penalty doesn't increase until after both attacks are made.
qr1s3bZrWNgIX3du.name: Tireless Flurry

Corpse Fleet Officer.name: Corpse Fleet Officer

Corpse Fleet Recruiter.description:
Corpse Fleet recruiters are powerful necromancers capable of maintaining control of mindless undead, creating new undead, and turning their magic against the living.

The Corpse Fleet is an army made up of undead supremacists who refuse to bow to the will of the living. Founded by defectors from the Eoxian navy, the Corpse Fleet aims to shatter Pact Worlds unity and liberate Eox from the influence of the living and those bone sages who sided with them. Unyielding and utterly ruthless, the Corpse Fleet deals in death and destruction, feeding on the living and exploiting the dead.

E9yFBGTwnXFqhbkq.description:
Frequency once per day

Requirements A formerly living creature that died within the last round is within 10 feet

Effect The Corpse Fleet recruiter immediately performs the @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.spells.Item.c3b6LdLlQDPngNIb]{Create Undead} ritual, as if it were a spell with a casting time of 2 actions and the Corpse Fleet recruiter rolled a critical success on the ritual.
E9yFBGTwnXFqhbkq.name: Rapid Recruitment

JuRYafRJ4UvuIvWH.description:
Upgrades: 1

This flexible nanocarbon circuit can be installed as an upgrade into gloves, kneepads, or similar appendage protectors to emit a powerful electric shock when forcefully applied to a target.
JuRYafRJ4UvuIvWH.name: Integrated Shock Pad

NUckU1mEqJQI5FNr.description:
Upgrades: 1

Zero pistols use transparent canisters of supercooled liquid as ammunition.
NUckU1mEqJQI5FNr.name: Integrated Zero Pistol

WMuFRGHlVFuCZJhB.description:
You transform the target into an undead creature with a level up to that allowed in the Creature Creation Rituals table. There are many versions of this ritual, each specific to a particular type of undead (one ritual for all zombies, one for skeletons, one for ghouls, and so on), and the rituals that create rare undead are also rare. Some forms of undead, such as liches, form using their own unique methods and can't be created with a version of create undead.

Critical Success The target becomes an undead creature of the appropriate type. If it's at least 4 levels lower than you, you can make it a minion. This gives it the minion trait, meaning it can use 2 actions when you command it, and commanding it is a single action that has the auditory and concentrate traits. You can have a maximum of four minions under your control. If it's intelligent and doesn't become a minion, the undead is helpful to you for awakening it, though it's still a horrid and evil creature. If it's unintelligent and doesn't become a minion, you can give it one simple command. It pursues that goal single-mindedly, ignoring any of your subsequent commands.

Success As critical success, except an intelligent undead that doesn't become your minion is only friendly to you, and an unintelligent undead that doesn't become your minion leaves you alone unless you attack it. It marauds the local area rather than following your command.

Failure You fail to create the undead.

Critical Failure You create the undead, but its soul, tortured by your foul necromancy, is full of nothing but hatred for you. It attempts to destroy you.

YFN9FqeqxnFp0sGj.description: The Corpse Fleet recruiter detonates one mindless undead minion under their control, causing it to explode in a @Template[burst|distance:15]{15-foot-radius burst}, dealing @Damage[4d6[slashing],4d6[void]|options:area-damage]{4d6 slashing damage and 4d6 void damage} to creatures in the area (@Check[reflex|dc:25|basic|options:area-effect] save).
YFN9FqeqxnFp0sGj.name: Corpse Bomb

qFdNx2icqRpXEdZJ.description: 20 feet. Mindless undead that begin their turn in the area must attempt a @Check[will|dc:22|options:area-effect] save; on a failure, the Corpse Fleet recruiter seizes control of that undead. It gains the minion trait.
qFdNx2icqRpXEdZJ.name: Seize Control

xjTWKo8W7XYnMyTb.description: The Corpse Fleet recruiter Sustains each spell they cast to create minions and Commands any number of their minions.
xjTWKo8W7XYnMyTb.name: Efficient Commands

Corpse Fleet Recruiter.name: Corpse Fleet Recruiter

Corzad.description:
Packs of wolflike corzads act as the eyes and mouths of the corzadai fungal colony.

Corzadais spawned from the broken remains of Aucturn. Explosively launched into space, these fungal colonies are held together by mysterious forces. Their strange fruiting bodies have taken on numerous shapes, of which two have been more commonly seen in the Pact Worlds than others: corzads and corzadors.

ewNiCE0dKOsIBSVt.description: A corzad's Strikes deal an extra 1d4 damage to targets within 20 feet of at least two of the corzad's allies.
ewNiCE0dKOsIBSVt.name: Fungal Symbiosis

pkqWJQcjykhNVhgW.description: The corzad dissolves into a mass of slimy spores and Strides twice, ignoring difficult terrain and other creatures. This movement doesn't trigger reactions. Any creature in the corzad's path must succeed at a @Check[will|dc:15|options:area-effect,inflicts:sickened] save or become @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.fesd1n5eVhpCSS18]{Sickened 1}. The corzad re-forms at the end of this movement.
pkqWJQcjykhNVhgW.name: Spore Tide

Corzad.name: Corzad

Corzador.description:
Vaguely humanoid corzadors herd corzad packs as they carry out their grim tasks.

Corzadais spawned from the broken remains of Aucturn. Explosively launched into space, these fungal colonies are held together by mysterious forces. Their strange fruiting bodies have taken on numerous shapes, of which two have been more commonly seen in the Pact Worlds than others: corzads and corzadors.

9tqJECldoMS9wTdX.description:
Hundreds of wirelike nerve endings erupt from the corzador's head in a @Template[type:emanation|distance:30]. Each non-corzadai in the area must succeed at a @Check[reflex|dc:18|options:area-effect] save or be instantly observed by all corzadais within 100 feet. Corzadais in the area gain a +1 circumstance bonus to attack and damage rolls against the detected creatures as long as the targets remain in the emanation. The corzador's emanation remains in effect until it takes a move action to leave its current space.

@UUID[Compendium.sf2e.bestiary-effects.Item.Bw1u0YIbG0ZV1CIR]{Effect: Follicle Germination}
9tqJECldoMS9wTdX.name: Follicle Germination

obnMCe9iRpCgUY0E.description:
Trigger A non-corzadai creature moves within the corzador's active Follicle Germination

Effect The corzador emits a high-pitched shriek. All non-corzadai creatures within the corzador's Follicle Emanation take @Damage[2d8[sonic]|options:area-damage] damage with a @Check[fortitude|dc:18|basic|options:area-effect] save.
obnMCe9iRpCgUY0E.name: Shrieking Utricle

Corzador.name: Corzador

Cosmic Dragon (Adult).description: These majestic dragons embody the stellar forces that underly and balance all that exists in the universe. Cosmic dragons are wise, social, and patient beings, accepting of all whom they come across; they see all creatures as equal components of the universe and are just as likely to be found discussing astrophysics in the company of scholars as they are to be found lamenting the twists and turns of fate in the company of the downtrodden. Most cosmic dragons can change their shape, though they usually only do so to make other creatures comfortable. They detest deception and always introduce themselves as dragons even while in another form.

0IKGS9tY1IczBC94.name: +2 status to all saves vs. divine

1uUnV98pyw2Rx0IC.description:
The cosmic dragon is always attuned to an underlying stellar force: either photons or gravitons. They can swap attunement as a free action once at the start of their turn in combat and is otherwise attuned to whichever force they choose at any time outside of combat. The dragon's melee Strikes deal an additional @Damage[2d6[fire]] damage while they're photon-attuned and an additional @Damage[1d6[bludgeoning]] damage plus Knockdown while they're graviton-attuned. The damage of their cosmic blast Strike is likewise determined by their current attunement, as are the effects of some of their other abilities. The dragon can choose to exclude any creatures from any effect of the aura or action that uses the aura.

The dragon can always sense the distance and direction to the nearest Drift beacon and to the Starstone on Absalom Station.
1uUnV98pyw2Rx0IC.name: Cosmic Attunement

7BM1lv70mnF5DCry.description: The dragon makes two claw Strikes and one tail Strike in any order.
7BM1lv70mnF5DCry.name: Draconic Frenzy

CfGvCAbVZg83PorB.description: The dragon recharges their Stellar Breath whenever they score a critical hit with a Strike.
CfGvCAbVZg83PorB.name: Draconic Momentum

ImHPje7uuTyH88N8.description:
A globe of freezing darkness explodes in the area, dealing 8d10 cold damage to creatures in the area, plus an additional 8d4 void damage to living creatures. Each creature in the area must attempt a Reflex save.

If the globe overlaps with an area of magical light or affects a creature affected by magical light, eclipse burst attempts to counteract the light effect.

Critical Success The creature is unaffected.

Success The creature takes half damage.

Failure The creature takes full damage.

Critical Failure The creature takes double damage and becomes @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.XgEqL1kFApUbl5Z2]{Blinded} by the darkness for an unlimited duration.

Heightened (+1) The cold damage increases by 1d10 and the void damage against the living increases by 1d4.
ImHPje7uuTyH88N8.name: Eclipse Burst

NFTKRYKnIhHrHmjS.description: The dragon unleashes divine power like that from the core of a star or black hole, dealing @Damage[10d10[spirit]|options:area-damage] damage in a @Template[type:cone|distance:40] (@Check[will|dc:34|basic|options:area-effect] save). The dragon can't use Stellar Breath for [[/gmr 1d4 #rounds]]{1d4 rounds}.
NFTKRYKnIhHrHmjS.name: Stellar Breath

U07XTUETgCe5IXhd.description: The dragon conjures a mote of stellar energy that shares their current attunement. They direct the mote to a square within 90 feet. While the mote is deployed, the dragon's attunement aura also emanates from that square, with the same emanation radius. The dragon can Sustain to move the mote up to 90 feet or to recall the mote from any distance. The mote is made of cosmic energy, doesn't occupy a space, and can't be targeted or destroyed by any effect.
U07XTUETgCe5IXhd.name: Stellar Mote

WKbjdRL8LmfP69IO.description:
Trigger A creature within range enters an environment that would be harmful to it.

A shimmering bubble envelops the target's body, allowing it to breathe normally in a vacuum or other unsafe environment and protecting it from severe temperatures and radiation.

Heightened (7th) You can target up to 5 additional creatures to gain protection against the environment the triggering creature entered. The spell lasts for 8 hours and also protects against extreme temperatures and radiation.

Heightened (10th) You can target up to 10 additional creatures to gain protection against the environment the triggering creature entered. The spell lasts until your next daily preparations and also protects against incredible temperatures and radiation.
WKbjdRL8LmfP69IO.name: Life Seal (at will)

u4oZ5dmcEUYUE8ma.description:
The dragon imposes an effect on creatures within their attunement aura. The effect is based on the dragon's current attunement. The dragon can't use Stellar Pulse again for [[/gmr 1d4 #Recharge Stellar Pulse]]{1d4 rounds}.

  • Graviton Each creature must succeed at a @Check[fortitude|dc:34|options:area-effect] save or be @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.eIcWbB5o3pP6OIMe]{Immobilized} for 1 round.

  • Photon Each creature becomes @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.nlCjDvLMf2EkV2dl]{Quickened} and can use the extra action only to Stride or Strike.
u4oZ5dmcEUYUE8ma.name: Stellar Pulse

wW3iG2EYMceB91E4.description:
The target can understand all words regardless of language and also speak the languages of other creatures. When in a mixed group of creatures, each time the target speaks, it can choose a creature and speak in a language that creature understands, even if the target doesn't know what language that is.

Heightened (7th) The duration is 8 hours.
wW3iG2EYMceB91E4.name: Truespeech (constant)

xamE1Uh41hqJFQHa.description: 60 feet. All allied creatures in the aura gain a +5-foot status bonus to Speeds (if the dragon is photon-attuned), or all enemies take a –5-foot status penalty to Speeds (if the dragon is graviton-attuned).
xamE1Uh41hqJFQHa.name: Attunement Aura

Cosmic Dragon (Adult).name: Cosmic Dragon (Adult)

Cosmic Dragon (Adult, Spellcaster).description: These majestic dragons embody the stellar forces that underly and balance all that exists in the universe. Cosmic dragons are wise, social, and patient beings, accepting of all whom they come across; they see all creatures as equal components of the universe and are just as likely to be found discussing astrophysics in the company of scholars as they are to be found lamenting the twists and turns of fate in the company of the downtrodden. Most cosmic dragons can change their shape, though they usually only do so to make other creatures comfortable. They detest deception and always introduce themselves as dragons even while in another form.

0IKGS9tY1IczBC94.name: +2 status to all saves vs. divine

1uUnV98pyw2Rx0IC.description:
The cosmic dragon is always attuned to an underlying stellar force: either photons or gravitons. They can swap attunement as a free action once at the start of their turn in combat and is otherwise attuned to whichever force they choose at any time outside of combat. The dragon's melee Strikes deal an additional @Damage[2d6[fire]] damage while they're photon-attuned and an additional @Damage[1d6[bludgeoning]] damage plus Knockdown while they're graviton-attuned. The damage of their cosmic blast Strike is likewise determined by their current attunement, as are the effects of some of their other abilities. The dragon can choose to exclude any creatures from any effect of the aura or action that uses the aura.

The dragon can always sense the distance and direction to the nearest Drift beacon and to the Starstone on Absalom Station.
1uUnV98pyw2Rx0IC.name: Cosmic Attunement

ImHPje7uuTyH88N8.description:
A globe of freezing darkness explodes in the area, dealing 8d10 cold damage to creatures in the area, plus an additional 8d4 void damage to living creatures. Each creature in the area must attempt a Reflex save.

If the globe overlaps with an area of magical light or affects a creature affected by magical light, eclipse burst attempts to counteract the light effect.

Critical Success The creature is unaffected.

Success The creature takes half damage.

Failure The creature takes full damage.

Critical Failure The creature takes double damage and becomes @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.XgEqL1kFApUbl5Z2]{Blinded} by the darkness for an unlimited duration.

Heightened (+1) The cold damage increases by 1d10 and the void damage against the living increases by 1d4.
ImHPje7uuTyH88N8.name: Eclipse Burst

Crest-Eater.description:
Crest-eaters are large four-legged beasts with traits of both reptiles and mammals. Originating from the distant world of Kasath, they've spread throughout the cosmos, accompanying numerous kasathas and even having a small enclave aboard the Idari worldship in the Pact Worlds. A crest-eater is a predator known for consuming the bones of their prey. They use a highly corrosive acidic venom that eats through minerals with ease. Their name comes from their history of tracking down kasathas and cracking open their prey's elongated skulls to feed on the "bony crests" within. As crest-eaters consume bones and other substances, they produce large mineral protrusions across their bodies. Crest-eaters are social creatures and often form prides to hunt together or join with other nearby species if they're accepted—it's not uncommon to find a starship crew or local raider gang with one or more crest-eaters they've adopted. Tamers who have hunted with crest-eaters for generations craft a ceremonial cestus from their comrade's body after a crest-eater passes, a tradition still practiced to this day despite the high value and demand for crest-eater bones.

Most crest-eaters can grow as long as 14 feet and about 6 feet tall (not including their noticeable mineral protrusions). Thanks to their mineral-laden composition, they often weigh in excess of 1,000 pounds, somewhat hampering their mobility in environments that can't support their girth. Young and mature crest-eaters tend to stay together in small prides, though some act as solitary hunters in environments where food sources are scarce. Especially large males frequently become increasingly aggressive as they age, and they're often driven away by the rest of the pride for both their hostility and gluttonous appetites. If these solitary beasts survive long enough, they can become unpredictable and dangerous threats that attempt to establish territory and find food by attacking desert settlements. Many kasathan epics feature one or more brave warriors defending their village against an ancient male crest-eater. Whether dispatched by local legends or eventually dying off in secret, these oversized crest-eaters can leave behind a valuable cache of minerals for enterprising adventurers.

Necrograft zombies are animated by necrografts created from the body parts and internal organs of undead creatures. On Eox, it's common to augment animals and beasts with necrografts to ensure their survival on the dead planet. After death, many of these creatures return as true undead to continue serving their creators.

Technological zombies are created when a dead creature is reanimated (or otherwise kept moving) by an internal or integrated technological item—usually an augmentation. Despite the vast differences in form and hardware between different tech zombies, they do have similarities—they're mindless undead driven to harm the living, with technological components and weaknesses that can be leveraged.

Cyanoscum.description:
While these wood elementals bear the adorable appearance of a rodent, their main bodies are unfortunately composed of toxin-producing algae. Cyanoscums thrive in any warm, wet environment. Cyanoscum blooms are easy to spot; from a distance, they look like blue-green meadows floating atop still waters or clusters of fuzzy, teal moss clinging to plants and rocks. An explorer moved by this majestic sight might venture too close to the water's edge or reach out to touch the soft, resplendent moss—inviting contact with these beautiful but poisonous creatures.

Elementals are energetic intrusions from the primal planes of existence. They take many forms, from mindless eddies in the wind or water to complex entities capable of wielding primal magic. The advent of space travel and the progress of technology have allowed even more living embodiments of the elements to manifest in the Universe.

Natural events like wildfires, solar storms, and floods can unleash hordes of unruly elementals on a planet or into a region of space. Sometimes, a gathering of powerful elementals causes a natural disaster on an epic scale, like an off-the-charts solar flare that fries a planet's power grid or a ceaseless storm swirling in a gas giant's atmosphere.

The most common form of tech zombie is the cybernetic zombie, but tech zombies can also arise through other types of technologies, including nanites.

Technological zombies are created when a dead creature is reanimated (or otherwise kept moving) by an internal or integrated technological item—usually an augmentation. Daipex.description:
Daipexes are formed from souls of sinful mortals whose lives were consumed by rage and indiscriminate violence. Their hulking figures consist primarily of a pair of chain guns merged into the flesh of their large arms. By comparison, their legs are disproportionately small and incapable of bracing completely against the force of their attacks. Daipexes only use their legs when necessary and otherwise rely on their arms to move about to reduce the strain on their leg muscles.

Daipexes carry about the entrails of their prey, sometimes dangling loops of intestines from their necks or simply dragging it along the ground. They feed these organs into their arms and, by flexing their muscles there, condense the putrid flesh into ammunition that can then be fired directly from their bodies. While they often have enough ammunition to fire off their arm weapons for hours, in the rare instances that they run out of ammunition mid-combat, they either retrieve more from corpses on the battlefield or sacrifice their own flesh in the name of victory.

All mortal creatures have souls that are usually judged in the Boneyard after their demise. The souls of individuals who lived sinful lives—usually by hurting others or acting selfishly—are sent to the Outer Rifts, where they eventually coalesce into demons. These fiends care for nothing but the corruption of mortal life to ensure that the ranks of their fellow demons never wane.

Deh-Nolo.description:
Deh-nolos are the Dominion's foremost engineers, seamlessly and deviously merging technology and biological systems to create any device imaginable, from sinister weapons to massive starships to shipmind oozes. These creations are grown, not built, but they're neither cybernetics nor biotech—rather, something in between. Deh-nolos seek to understand all technology they encounter, and they believe it's their right to consume the brain of anyone they think might help them better understand an unfamiliar device. Then again, deh-nolos have no qualms about consuming brains for nearly any reason, seeing all forms of life outside the Dominion as lesser beings.

While mostly organic, deh-nolos can concentrate their shimmering liquid metal secretions into foul crystals that they can use as projectiles or mechanical components for their twisted inventions. A casual onlooker might assume these creations are biotechnological in nature, as they often look like atrophied organs and mutated body parts held together by seemingly crude or incomplete circuitry. Those who attempt to incorporate deh-nolo technology into their bodies as augmentations typically experience terrible pain and grisly deaths, even if they somehow manage to isolate or drain the toxins naturally produced by a deh-nolo's alien flesh. Even less intrusive experiments with deh-nolo technology are unpredictable and dangerous, and the results of a "successful" outcome are disturbing at best.

  • Creature If your target is a creature with the tech trait, it attempts a Will save. On a failure, the creature is @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.6A2QDy8wRGCVQsSd]{Glitching 1}; on a critical failure, the creature is @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.6A2QDy8wRGCVQsSd]{Glitching 2}.
  • Object If you target an attended object, the creature with the object attempts a Will save. On a success, the object loses half of its maximum charges. On a failure, or if you target an unattended object, the object loses all its remaining charges.

Demolition-Class Assassin Robot.description:
Named for their tendency toward extreme violence and aggressiveness, demolition robots nevertheless start their mission with stealth being a priority. Outwardly, these robots conceal their true nature with an outer casing resembling that of industrial, civic, or even domestic robots and drones.

Once the target has been detected, all stealth flies out the window as these killer machines unfurl their weapons and sensory suite from hidden panels and rush toward the mark at full speed. With their encyclopedic data banks on the stress points and emergency release mechanisms of most doors, only the most solid barriers can hold them at bay for long.

In some societies, machines automate many processes. It only makes sense, then, that some would attempt to automate the act of murder. Most manufacturers would never admit to creating such designs, forcing wealthy figures to go through hidden channels to acquire units from secret facilities or unscrupulous manufacturers. Regardless of their origins, these robots can be programmed with a target and set loose, the owner assured that either their target will be dead or will be unable to prove who tried to kill them thanks to the unit's fried circuitry.

2WYTUrCQDODPvkGJ.name: Integrated tools appropriate for disguise shell

FbNdPfxJmeStAg2S.description: The circuitry of an assassin robot self-destructs upon the robot's destruction, making tracing its owner extremely difficult. Add 10 to the DC of a Computers check to recover data from a destroyed assassin robot.
FbNdPfxJmeStAg2S.name: Burn Protocol

Upgrades: 1

This snub-nosed scattergun is commonly used to blast through doors and walls. Smaller than a reaction breacher, this scattergun is infamous for its mighty recoil.

QUlL6EsdrLuxfU44.description: The demolition-class assassin robot's Strikes deal an additional 2d6 precision damage to @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.AJh5ex99aV6VTggg]{Off-Guard} creatures.
QUlL6EsdrLuxfU44.name: Sneak Attack

The robot makes a ranged Strike with its breaching gun against the Force Open DC of a door or other obstacle. If successful, the obstacle gains the broken condition. The robot then Strides twice toward (and even through) the obstacle, but if the obstacle still bars the robot's movement, it stops adjacent to the obstacle and attempts an Athletics check to [[/act force-open]] the obstacle with a +4 circumstance bonus.

While in its disguised form, it loses the ability to make Strikes or use its Breaching Rush ability, but it becomes indistinguishable from a noncombatant robot or drone model that it's based on; it gets an automatic result of 33 on Deception checks and DCs to pass as a robot of that model. Damage to the robot can prevent this disguise from being effective at the GM's discretion.

Deprimogon.description:
Deprimogons stalk hidden tunnels, shadowed alleys, and looming towers of settlements whose governments have made infernal pacts as they silently monitor citizens for any signs of sedition. Agitators or freedom fighters are harassed or chased down and trapped by these devils before disappearing forever. Deprimogons hide their faces behind sleek metallic masks that suppress their own emotions, blocking out any pleas, threats, or bargaining that might dissuade them from their mission. Deprimogons delight in summoning diabolic creatures from eras long forgotten to torment their prisoners.

In the shadows of space stations, halls of courtrooms, and offices of corporations, devils tempt mortals with promises of power and lay the groundwork for their conquest. A devil's pacts can vary from elaborate contracts to quick promises, but they all end the same way: a mortal soul condemned, and Hell's forces bolstered. From the open rule of Malfane, the unseen control of Embroi, and hidden pacts with souls across the galaxy, devils continue their relentless work to spread tyranny and force the universe to resemble the hellish bureaucracy of their home.

ARsLDfh77tiJcZsL.description:
You make an appeal to a powerful devil, asking them to bind some of their subordinates to your service. If you succeed, the devil sends you their choice of one devil of level 2 or lower, two devils of level 0 or lower, or three devils of level –1 or lower.

Critical Success The devils are sent to you and serve you for [[/gmr 1d4 #Weeks]]{1d4 weeks}.

Success The devils are sent to you and serve you for [[/gmr 1d4 #Days]]{1d4 days}.

Failure Your request is denied.

Critical Failure Not only is your request denied, but the powerful devil sends word of its displeasure to your master.

Heightened (+1) Increase the level of devil sent to you by 2 for each option.
ARsLDfh77tiJcZsL.name: Diabolic Pact (DC 27)

DpEJpiqKeyiX7aAn.description: The deprimogon's Strikes count as magical and unholy.
DpEJpiqKeyiX7aAn.name: Infernal Disgrace

UyBKWBZHcU9Ktp2J.description: The deprimogon casts a 6th-rank @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.spells.Item.7Iela4GgVeO3LfAo]{Wall of Force} that dampens sound. Any creature that moves and begins its turn adjacent to the wall must attempt a @Check[will|dc:27] save. On a failure, the creature can't speak and can't use any actions and effects with the sonic or auditory traits while adjacent to the wall; this also prevents the creature from casting spells, with the exception of subtle spells.
UyBKWBZHcU9Ktp2J.name: Silent Prison

ZkjV2R7fZpwMNTZs.description: The deprimogon loses their immunity to emotion and mental effects if they aren't wearing a mask. In addition, an unmasked silencer devil uses the outcome one degree of success worse than they roll on saving throws against mental effects. A deprimogon's mask can be Disarmed as if it were a held item.
ZkjV2R7fZpwMNTZs.name: Masked Emotions

qSRwu0CLlvjqtYaz.description:
The deprimogon infuses their weapons with paranoia and mistrust, instilling doubt in their victims with every attack. A creature damaged by a deprimogon's Strikes must attempt a @Check[will|dc:27] save.

Critical Success The creature is unaffected and temporarily immune to the deprimogon's evoke paranoia for 1 minute.

Success The creature is unaffected and temporarily immune to the deprimogon's evoke paranoia for 1 round.

Failure Until the beginning of the deprimogon's next turn, the creature believes everyone it sees is a potential threat. It becomes unfriendly to all creatures to which it wasn't already hostile, even those who were previously allies. It treats no one as an ally.

Critical Failure As failure, except the target believes that everyone it sees is a mortal enemy. It uses its reactions and free actions against everyone, regardless of whether they were previously its allies, as determined by the GM. It otherwise acts as rationally as it normally does and likely prefers to attack creatures that are actively attacking or hindering it over those leaving it alone.
qSRwu0CLlvjqtYaz.name: Evoke Paranoia

Deprimogon.name: Deprimogon

Diaspora Worm.description:
Resembling fanged eels with manes of tendrils instead of eyes, diaspora worms originally ruled the inky depths of the ocean that later became the icy planetoid Nisis. The worms' hostility toward trespassers and lack of observable speech lead most people to consider them mere beasts, but xenobiologists know the worms' tendrils respond to electromagnetic waves, which they manipulate to see, communicate, and interact with their surroundings. Bioelectric radiation from coral samples recovered from the worms' home reef documents millennia of worm culture and history from even before the Diaspora's formation.

Juvenile members of this species are sleek, sinuous, and nimble despite their size. Their electromagnetic manipulation lets them briefly change the molecular structure of water, making it murky like their original depths. Young worms tend to commit brazen attacks, requiring decades of experience to value more complex strategies.

"Space worm" is a nonscientific term for a xenobiologically complex clade of invertebrate animals and beasts that make their home in the vastness of space. Some, like the diaspora and dust worms, show signs of intelligence and are directly related to each other. Others, like the surnoch, evolved separately, with their origins completely unknown to science.

B6EYNzwveiQx77Pz.description:
Requirements The diaspora worm has @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.kWc1fhmv9LBiTuei]{Grabbed} a creature with its tongue

Effect The diaspora worm attempts to [[/act reposition]] the grabbed creature toward the worm. If the grabbed creature is brought to within 10 feet or less of the worm, the worm can attempt to Swallow Whole the creature.
B6EYNzwveiQx77Pz.name: Tongue Reel

BBj8Sgle9M9KkjYP.description: A creature hit by the diaspora worm's tongue becomes @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.kWc1fhmv9LBiTuei]{Grabbed}. A creature can sever the tongue with a Strike against AC 19 that deals at least 12 slashing damage. This prevents the worm from using its tongue Strike until it regrows its tongue, which takes 1 day.
BBj8Sgle9M9KkjYP.name: Tongue Grab

D0pUwUgnKIrp2oq3.description:
Requirements The diaspora worm is in water

Effect The worm alters the structure of water within a @Template[type:emanation|distance:10], forming light-absorbing nanotubes. This field moves with the worm and lasts for 1 minute. The emanation deactivates non-magical light sources and automatically attempts to counteract magical light (counteract rank 4, counteract modifier [[/r 1d20+17 #Counteract]]{+17}). This field also provides cover for creatures inside of it from those outside, and vice versa.
D0pUwUgnKIrp2oq3.name: Darkwater Veil

E5wRJDAr3Uqo97fr.description:
Diaspora worms that take electricity damage must attempt a @Check[fortitude|dc:23] save.

Critical Success The worm is unaffected.

Success The worm is @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.TkIyaNPgTZFBCCuh]{Dazzled} for 1 round.

Failure The worm is @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.XgEqL1kFApUbl5Z2]{Blinded} for 1 round.

Critical Failure The worm is blinded for 1 round, then dazzled for 1 round.
E5wRJDAr3Uqo97fr.name: Electromagnetic Blindness

MmZCgR5g40oyBClB.description: Diaspora worms sense their surroundings by reading electromagnetic fields, including disruptions caused by creatures or objects. This is a precise sense within the listed range. Intense fields, such as areas emitting radiation or auras of electricity, make creatures within them @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.DmAIPqOBomZ7H95W]{Concealed} to the diaspora worm.
MmZCgR5g40oyBClB.name: Electromagnetic Sight

k6aAJV1toBtej5lY.description: Diaspora worms communicate by shaping and reading electromagnetic fields. This functions like telepathy with creatures that share this ability.
k6aAJV1toBtej5lY.name: Electrocommunication

Diaspora Worm.name: Diaspora Worm

Diaspora Worm Sage.description:
Diaspora worms that survive for centuries grow significantly in size, power, and intelligence. They mostly protect their ancestral home, preserving bioelectric coral records and directing the actions of younger worms.

"Space worm" is a nonscientific term for a xenobiologically complex clade of invertebrate animals and beasts that make their home in the vastness of space. Some, like the diaspora and dust worms, show signs of intelligence and are directly related to each other. Success The worm is @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.TkIyaNPgTZFBCCuh]{Dazzled} for 1 round.

Failure The worm is @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.XgEqL1kFApUbl5Z2]{Blinded} for 1 round.

Critical Failure The worm is blinded for 1 round, then dazzled for 1 round.
E5wRJDAr3Uqo97fr.name: Electromagnetic Blindness

MTBqLTq4O78XzMPy.description: The diaspora worm sage stirs up a 40-foot-tall cylinder of water with a @Template[burst|distance:20]{20-foot radius} within 300 feet. If the area isn't already filled with water, this ability fails. The vortex buffets all creatures, dealing @Damage[5d10[bludgeoning]|options:area-damage] damage (@Check[reflex|dc:35|basic|options:area-effect] save). Creatures that fail the save are pulled 5 feet toward the center of the vortex (or 10 feet on a critical failure).
MTBqLTq4O78XzMPy.name: Darkwater Vortex

MmZCgR5g40oyBClB.description: Diaspora worms sense their surroundings by reading electromagnetic fields, including disruptions caused by creatures or objects. This is a precise sense within the listed range. Intense fields, such as areas emitting radiation or auras of electricity, make creatures within them @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.DmAIPqOBomZ7H95W]{Concealed} to the diaspora worm.

k6aAJV1toBtej5lY.description: Diaspora worms communicate by shaping and reading electromagnetic fields. This functions like telepathy with creatures that share this ability.
k6aAJV1toBtej5lY.name: Electrocommunication

nkDanjToNqSLqKDY.description:
The diaspora worm sage emits a concentrated wave of electromagnetism in a @Template[type:cone|distance:50]. Each creature in the area must attempt a @Check[fortitude|dc:35|options:area-effect,inflicts:glitching,inflicts:stunned,inflicts:paralyzed] save. A creature with the tech trait uses the outcome one degree of success worse than the result of its roll.

Critical Success The creature is unaffected and becomes immune to Electromagnetic Surge for 1 hour.

Success The creature's items with the tech trait become @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.6A2QDy8wRGCVQsSd]{Glitching 1} for 1 round.

Failure The creature becomes @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.dfCMdR4wnpbYNTix]{Stunned 1}, and its items with the tech trait become @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.6A2QDy8wRGCVQsSd]{Glitching 2} for 1 minute. A creature with the tech trait also gains this glitching condition.

Critical Failure The creature becomes @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.6uEgoh53GbXuHpTF]{Paralyzed} for 1 round, and its items with the tech trait become @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.6A2QDy8wRGCVQsSd]{Glitching 3} for 10 minutes. A creature with the tech trait also gains this glitching condition.
nkDanjToNqSLqKDY.name: Electromagnetic Surge

Diaspora Worm Sage.name: Diaspora Worm Sage

Diatha.description:
Often called "boom bugs" or "exploding slugs," diathas are invertebrates that store nutrients as hydrocarbon chains rather than fat deposits. Threatened diathas secrete hormones that prime their energy stores to combust, detonating themselves to drive off or kill predators. Even if several diathas sacrifice themselves this way, their hive rarely suffers thanks to their rapid reproductive cycle.

Diathas are hardy scavengers that can convert almost any carbon-based molecules into energy. Originally, diathas consumed biowaste in underground warrens, but their appetite for hydrocarbon-based fuels and industrial runoff drew them into contact with modernized civilizations, where they quickly adapted to urban environments. Though some entrepreneurs try to use these creatures as an organic means of converting plastic waste into petrol products, most see diathas as vermin that do far more harm than good when allowed to propagate.

Diathas can easily stow away in the nooks and crannies of starships, and interstellar travelers often don't notice them until it's too late. Because they can digest almost any carbon-containing matter, diathas that colonize new worlds can adapt to a wide range of biomes and persist as a threat to native species for generations. Efforts to eradicate invasive diathas carry substantial risks to the exterminators and the environment they're trying to protect, as the explosive vermin use literal scorched earth tactics to protect their hives. To make matters worse, diathas are hermaphroditic and can grow new hives from a single organism if they have sufficient food sources to multiply. As a result, the Pact Worlds and Veskarium maintain strict quarantine measures for vessels suspected of carrying diatha infestations.

As diathas age, their stored internal gases allow them to become buoyant. These "elder" diathas instinctively take prominent roles as scouts and guards for other diathas. To create an elder diatha, apply the aerial and elite adjustments to a diatha, or increase its level using the guidelines from GM Core.

4GSaAuzSCryFiBVo.description:
Trigger The diatha takes acid, electricity, fire, piercing, slashing, or sonic damage

Requirements The diatha has 5 or fewer Hit Points

Effect The diatha dies, its body combusting in a flash of flame. All creatures in a @Template[emanation|distance:5] take @Damage[1d6[fire]|options:area-damage] damage (@Check[reflex|dc:16|basic|options:area-effect] save).
4GSaAuzSCryFiBVo.name: Detonate

ezn9Zjb587sVCpXd.description:
Requirements The diatha has 5 or fewer Hit Points

Effect The diatha Strides twice and makes a melee Strike at the end of that movement. After the Strike, the diatha uses Detonate.
ezn9Zjb587sVCpXd.name: Explosive Charge

lIjB3YSSzjoRkM5g.description:
If a diatha dies before it can detonate, its body rapidly decomposes into a slick of highly volatile hydrocarbons. Any effect that deals acid, electricity, or fire damage in an area that includes the square where the diatha died, or targets a creature in that square, causes a small explosion and consumes the slick.

All creatures in the square and in a @Template[type:emanation|distance:5] take @Damage[1d6[fire]|options:area-damage] damage (@Check[reflex|dc:16|basic|options:area-effect] save). The slick evaporates after 10 minutes if it isn't ignited.
lIjB3YSSzjoRkM5g.name: Hydrocarbon Slick

Diatha.name: Diatha

Digital Ghost Vidgamer.description:
Some vidgamers are so terminally online that they can manifest as a digital ghost.

Digital ghosts are data constructs crafted from forgotten user accounts and metadata that are gathered and formatted into a simulacrum of the source user.

0890yZFNlpoAkYqy.description:
Frequency once per day

Effect The digital ghost attempts to infect an item with the tech trait being held or used by a creature within 30 feet. The bearer can attempt a @Check[will|dc:21] save.

Critical Success The item is unaffected, and the digital ghost can't use Malware Infection for 1 week.

Success The item is unaffected.

Failure The item becomes glitching 2.

Critical Failure The item becomes glitching 2, and an offline digital ghost based on the bearer is created on the device in [[/gmr 2d4 #days]]{2d4 days}.
0890yZFNlpoAkYqy.name: Malware Infection

76nTWet1UH9JzrPB.description: A digital ghost can stray only a short distance from the device where they're stored. A typical limit is 120 feet.
76nTWet1UH9JzrPB.name: Device Bound

IqHVc9kJi2Gu2WlK.description: A digital ghost senses creatures and items with the tech trait at the listed range.
IqHVc9kJi2Gu2WlK.name: Techsense (Imprecise) 30 feet

bMYUj5D2BECNG1rc.description:
An offline copy of the digital ghost is stored in a device. When an active digital ghost is destroyed, it reforms after [[/gmr 2d4 #days]]{2d4 days} within the device that the copy is stored in, fully healed, but with no memory of what destroyed them. A digital ghost can be permanently removed from that device by attempting a @Check[computers|dc:24] check against the digital ghost's Will DC.

On a success, the copy of the digital ghost is purged from the device, and no new copies will be generated. On a critical success, any active copies are also purged.
bMYUj5D2BECNG1rc.name: Backup

nK0YavlmWxPjOl1E.description: A digital ghost's weapons deal mental damage, have the ghost killer upgrade, and disappear if dropped.
nK0YavlmWxPjOl1E.name: Virtual Arms

Digital Ghost Vidgamer.name: Digital Ghost Vidgamer

Draiclipsed.description:
Draiclipsed are the undead heralds of the Insatiable Eclipse, an ancient and terrifying tzitzimitl warlord buried when the Blackmoon fell on Eox and recently awakened by the Newborn. The Insatiable Eclipse amasses its forces, including legions of draiclipsed, to retake Eox, a world he feels has fallen to decadence and frivolity, whose disgraceful leaders have made the blasphemous decision to ally with the living.

Draiclipsed are canny skeletal undead whose pitch-black bones absorb light, allowing them to cast deep shadows. They can also consume magical light, using the absorbed photons to obscure their form before unleashing it in a blast of electromagnetic energy. Utterly loyal to their creator and liege, draiclipsed are trained for open warfare and even more dangerous when fighting alongside one another.

98h1UUPgHEBC6Nbd.description:
Requirements The draiclipsed is photonic

Effect The draiclipsed releases the light they've consumed in a blast of corrupted electromagnetic energy, dealing @Damage[3d8[electricity],3d8[void]|options:area-damage] damage in a @Template[type:cone|distance:30] (@Check[reflex|dc:24|basic|options:area-effect] save). The draiclipsed is no longer photonic.
98h1UUPgHEBC6Nbd.name: Darkness Falls

DSo7t1nxsBtz5WyO.description: A draiclipsed can detect infrared radiation (such as that given off by warm-blooded creatures) as an imprecise sense at the listed range.
DSo7t1nxsBtz5WyO.name: Infrared Vision

VIe57oFghrf78ULO.description: Whenever a draiclipsed would deal void damage to an undead or other creature with void healing, that void damage becomes cold damage instead.
VIe57oFghrf78ULO.name: Cull the Betrayers

WV5MzVNg9kdFEam7.description: The draiclipsed opens their mouth and sucks in a magical light, consuming it to fuel their own powers. The draiclipsed attempts a counteract check against one magical light effect within 60 feet ([[/r 1d20+15 #Counteract]]{+15} counteract modifier). If successful, the draiclipsed becomes ringed in diffuse light, becoming photonic for the next 24 hours. While a draiclipsed is photonic, they're @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.DmAIPqOBomZ7H95W]{Concealed}.
WV5MzVNg9kdFEam7.name: Consume Light

hJcr1POZPn7qVQyc.description: If at least one other draiclipsed is within the draiclipsed's eclipse shroud, the draiclipsed's Strikes deal an additional 1d8 void damage.
hJcr1POZPn7qVQyc.name: Gathering Darkness

nzB62fjSZClGt3UE.description: 15 feet. A draiclipsed absorbs light and is perpetually surrounded by shifting shadows and lengthening darkness. Light in the area decreases by one step (for example, bright light becomes dim light).
nzB62fjSZClGt3UE.name: Eclipse Shroud

Draiclipsed.name: Draiclipsed

Dread Empathnid.description:
Dread empathnids are deadly hunters native to jungle planets. They thrive on populated worlds, and their preferred prey are intelligent humanoids. Drawn to negative emotions, dread empathnids absorb the terror of their dying victims and infuse their webbing with these horrific experiences.

Empathnids have tremendous empathy for other creatures. The fact that the 8-inch spidery creatures come in a variety of colors and have a lifesaving venom likely explains why they're frequently used as companions or pets across the Pact Worlds.

GVd6x2Qm8B3QKzoy.description: A non-flying creature damaged by the dread empathnid's psychic web Strike or psychic burst is @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.eIcWbB5o3pP6OIMe]{Immobilized}, stuck to the ground or nearest adjacent surface until it [[/act escape dc=18]]{Escapes}. A flying creature must instead succeed at a @Check[reflex|dc:18] save or fall 20 feet (or 40 feet on a critical failure).
GVd6x2Qm8B3QKzoy.name: Mental Mire

JiypkCia9xHaDvXw.description:
Saving Throw @Check[fortitude|dc:18]

Maximum Duration 6 rounds

Stage 1 @Damage[1d6[mental]] damage and @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 1} (1 round)

Stage 2 @Damage[2d6[mental]] damage and @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 2} (1 round)

Stage 3 As stage 2, plus @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.3uh1r86TzbQvosxv]{Doomed 1} (1 round)
JiypkCia9xHaDvXw.name: Dread Venom

bpIrrPK5WD0B8aB8.description: This is a precise sense against creatures under an emotion effect or in the grips of overwhelming emotions (at the GM's discretion). Against other creatures, this is an imprecise sense. Creatures immune to emotion or mental effects or under the effects of a @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.spells.Item.b515AZlB0sridKSq]{Calm} spell are undetectable by emotionsense.
bpIrrPK5WD0B8aB8.name: Emotionsense

Dread Empathnid.name: Dread Empathnid

Dreamer.description:
Dancing between Liavara's peach-colored clouds are the Dreamers, the psychically gifted cousins of barathus. Not native to Liavara, the Dreamers were originally barathu explorers. They arrived by sailing one of the first living oma-ships long before the Gap. What exactly transformed them is still unknown to this day, though barathus as a people have been extremely protective of their prophetic cousins ever since.

The Dreamers lack barathus' ability to combine consciousnesses as well as their collectivist culture. That said, the Dreamers often dance through the skies of Liavara in flotillas together. To most of the Pact Worlds, they're a curiosity. To barathus, they're charges to be protected. The Dreamers themselves seem unconcerned with any such attention, giving neither care nor notice as to what's going on around them.

2kgkyXzpc01ccQGd.description: Any creature that uses an emotion or mental effect on a Dreamer must succeed at a @Check[will|dc:24|options:inflicts:slowed] save or become @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.xYTAsEpcJE1Ccni3]{Slowed 1} for the next [[/gmr 1d4 #rounds]]{1d4 rounds} as fragments of prophetic songs fill its mind.
2kgkyXzpc01ccQGd.name: Sluggish Mind

EKwLUXD6Xo8zSEdZ.description:
Any creature struck by a Dreamer's tentacle must attempt a @Check[will|dc:24|options:inflicts:dazzled,inflicts:stupefied,inflicts:stunned,inflicts:suppressed] save to resist a wave of sensory overstimulation. The creature is then temporarily immune to all synesthetic shocks for 1 minute.

Critical Success The creature is unaffected.

Success The creature is @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.enA7BxAjBb7ns1iF]{Suppressed} and @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.e1XGnhKNSQIm5IXg]{Stupefied 1} until the end of its next turn.

Failure As success, but the creature is also @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.TkIyaNPgTZFBCCuh]{Dazzled} until the end of its next turn.

Critical Failure As failure, but with a duration of 2 rounds, and the creature is also @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.dfCMdR4wnpbYNTix]{Stunned 2}.
EKwLUXD6Xo8zSEdZ.name: Synesthetic Shock

Pls0ljKEEktuqn45.description:
Trigger The Dreamer is reduced to half or less than half their total Hit Points

Effect The injured Dreamer erupts into a terrifying state of psychic fury, requiring all non-Dreamers in a @Template[type:emanation|distance:30] to attempt a @Check[will|dc:24|options:area-effect] save. The Dreamer gains a +2 status bonus to attack and damage rolls for 1 minute but can't use their innate spells. After they stop raging, a Dreamer can't enter an Atavistic Rage again for 1 minute.

Critical Success The creature is unaffected.

Success The creature is @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 1}.

Failure The creature is @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 2} and @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.dfCMdR4wnpbYNTix]{Stunned 1}.

Critical Failure The creature becomes @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 3} and @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.sDPxOjQ9kx2RZE8D]{Fleeing} for 1 round.
Pls0ljKEEktuqn45.name: Atavistic Rage

Dreamer.name: Dreamer

Dredgelit.description:
Dredgelits linger as flickers on the silver screen or neon silhouettes glimpsed backstage. They seethe in shortwave static and stare out from fading gravure tableaux. Dredgelits are the undead specters of deceased media megastars who haunt the venues of their former glories and crave the attention of forgetful fans.

Most dredgelits live in a fantasy version of their former lives, but once their delusions are shattered, a burning desire to recapture their lost fame drives them. At this point, they become unpredictable, and even the smallest perceived slight can lead to a murderous fit of rage.

Dredgelits embody their former stage personas. These decaying debutantes ensnare admirers into their eternal fan clubs, blissfully unaware of the life-draining consequences they have upon new admirers. Dredgelit seek sacrificial fans, luring in the unwary and draining their vitality to stay famous and fabulous forever.

aNFD0eNndUfnZGTg.description: 20 feet. A rowdy spectral crowd always surrounds the dredgelit. The dredgelit has @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.DmAIPqOBomZ7H95W]{Concealment} against all creatures, and the crowd counts as difficult terrain.
aNFD0eNndUfnZGTg.name: Phantasmal Fans

bVysYHdsIKKLs7Bf.description: A dredgelit maintains a bond with up to six other willing creatures. Creatures in the fan club always know the general distance and direction toward other bonded creatures, any conditions affecting them, and if they're @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.fBnFDH2MTzgFijKf]{Unconscious}, @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.yZRUzMqrMmfLu0V1]{Dying}, or dead. Creatures in the fan club can always communicate telepathically while on the same plane of existence.
bVysYHdsIKKLs7Bf.name: Fan Club

psCMa9aY4X9pT8TN.description:
Frequency once every 10 minutes

Effect The dredgelit attempts a @Check[performance|defense:will] check against the Will DC of a single creature within 30 feet, recreating an iconic show.

Critical Success The creature becomes part of their fan club for 24 hours, even if it's unwilling.

Success As critical success, but only for 1 hour.

Failure The creature is unaffected.

Critical Failure The creature is unaffected, and the dredgelit is so embarrassed by their failure to perform that they take @Damage[2d8[mental]] damage.
psCMa9aY4X9pT8TN.name: Alluring Debut

vTpl6y3UY52Cm6xd.description:
Frequency once per hour

Effect The dredgelit leeches vitality from a creature in their fan club. The dredgelit attempts a @Check[performance|defense:will|options:inflicts:immobilized,inflicts:stunned] check against the Will DC of the creature. The creature takes @Damage[6d6[void]] damage, and the dredgelit regains @Damage[10[healing]] Hit Points.

Critical Success The target takes double damage and is @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.dfCMdR4wnpbYNTix]{Stunned 2} and @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.eIcWbB5o3pP6OIMe]{Immobilized} for 1 round.

Success The target takes full damage and is @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.dfCMdR4wnpbYNTix]{Stunned 1} and immobilized for 1 round.

Failure The target is unaffected.

Critical Failure The target is unaffected. The dredgelit's abysmal performance results in them taking @Damage[2d8[mental]] damage instead of regaining Hit Points.
vTpl6y3UY52Cm6xd.name: Parasocial Leech

Dredgelit.name: Dredgelit

Driftdead Amalgam.description:
Amalgams are collections of driftdead that have fused together into one flesh ambulated by the shattered remnants of their component souls. The first amalgams formed spontaneously, but synthetic versions have been created in the Corpse Fleet's fleshforges and deployed as shock troops on the front lines of many battles.

Driftdead are created when a restless soul fuses with planar energies and reanimates its own corpse into a disturbing parody of life. Rarely, disturbed spirits snatched from elsewhere fuse together to inhabit a single dead body. Any death within the Drift might spawn a driftdead, but creatures that die in a frenzy of intense emotion are more likely to make the transition.

2sxZxc9Mti6I9SEP.description:
Frequency once per round

Effect The driftdead teleports up to its Speed. If it's in the Drift, the distance a driftdead can teleport is doubled.
2sxZxc9Mti6I9SEP.name: Drift Ambush

WrpGZ7a2NpxQJGOB.description:
The amalgam calls out in a cacophony of voices from those slain in the Drift. Each living creature within 30 feet must attempt a @Check[will|dc:25|options:area-effect] save.

Success The creature is temporarily immune to this amalgam's Voice of the Damned for 1 minute.

Failure The creature is @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.xYTAsEpcJE1Ccni3]{Slowed 1} for 1 round.

Critical Failure The creature is slowed 1 for 2 rounds.
WrpGZ7a2NpxQJGOB.name: Voice of the Damned

sr2jaLdNjDme6Crr.description: The amalgam's claws rip through reality in a @Template[type:cone|distance:30], dealing @Damage[8d6[slashing]|options:area-damage] damage with a @Check[reflex|dc:25|basic|options:area-effect] save. On a critical failure, a creature is also @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.4D2KBtexWXa6oUMR]{Drained 1}. The amalgam can't use Ripping Blast again for [[/gmr 1d4 #Recharge Ripping Blast]]{1d4 rounds}.
sr2jaLdNjDme6Crr.name: Ripping Blast

x83qx9b30W8KbCTP.description: While outside the Drift, the amalgam gains the incorporeal trait, becomes immune to precision damage, and gains resistance 10 to all damage (except force, ghost killer, or spirit; double resistance vs. non-magical).
x83qx9b30W8KbCTP.name: Torn from the Drift

ybQ59hh5fSaoXiRH.description: 30 feet. The area around a driftdead amalgam bristles with chaotic space torn from the Drift. The area is zero gravity. A creature that enters or begin its turn in the area take @Damage[4d6[void]] damage (@Check[fortitude|dc:25|basic] save).
ybQ59hh5fSaoXiRH.name: Dead Zone

Driftdead Amalgam.name: Driftdead Amalgam

Driftdead Crasher.description:
While most driftdead are spirits inhabiting their own corpses, some souls get ejected from their shells at death. These wraiths desperately struggle to return to their bodies, following their fragmented memories down aimless paths—woe to the living who cross them.

Crashers don't actually take their name from the Drift Crash that created many of them—they earned this name for their tendency to possess starships and reroute them into collision courses. If passengers trapped aboard a possessed ship don't survive, the victims might themselves twist into crashers instead of departing for the afterlife.

Driftdead are created when a restless soul fuses with planar energies and reanimates its own corpse into a disturbing parody of life. Rarely, disturbed spirits snatched from elsewhere fuse together to inhabit a single dead body. Any death within the Drift might spawn a driftdead, but creatures that die in a frenzy of intense emotion are more likely to make the transition.

1KIQCUWxSJQftnDW.description:
The driftdead crasher calls out in the voice of someone who was lost in the Drift. Each living creature within 30 feet must attempt a @Check[will|dc:18|options:area-effect] save.

Success The creature is temporarily immune to this driftdead's Voice of the Lost for 1 minute.

Failure The creature is @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.yblD8fOR1J8rDwEQ]{Confused} for 1 round.

Critical Failure The creature is confused for 2 rounds and @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.e1XGnhKNSQIm5IXg]{Stupefied 2} for 1 round.
1KIQCUWxSJQftnDW.name: Voice of the Lost

kKXsAIEwPACCxQuj.description:
While Inhabiting a Ship, the driftdead crasher extends its senses. It has vision anywhere within the ship and gains all-around vision while within the ship.

@UUID[Compendium.sf2e.bestiary-effects.Item.4J30S9nhyfaCX1Cm]{Effect: Starship Possession}
kKXsAIEwPACCxQuj.name: Starship Possession

lEJvy4rokoReTAMu.name: Drift Ambush

zstOpO1OgIjc04u6.description:
Frequency once per day

Effect The driftdead crasher possesses a starship it's onboard or adjacent to. While inhabiting a ship in this manner, the crasher imposes a –2 circumstance penalty to all Piloting checks attempted by the ship's pilot. If the target ship is currently piloted by a creature, the pilot can attempt a @Check[will|dc:18] save to resist the possession.
zstOpO1OgIjc04u6.name: Inhabit Ship

Driftdead Crasher.name: Driftdead Crasher

Driftdead Returned.description:
The least of these wretched spirits are the returned. Appearing as twisted versions of the shapes they wore in life, the returned drag themselves through space with wriggling, clawed appendages or float with hideous grace. The returned haunt Drift beacons, castaway ships, and airless rocks.

Driftdead are created when a restless soul fuses with planar energies and reanimates its own corpse into a disturbing parody of life. Rarely, disturbed spirits snatched from elsewhere fuse together to inhabit a single dead body. Any death within the Drift might spawn a driftdead, but creatures that die in a frenzy of intense emotion are more likely to make the transition.
