Dust Manta.description: Deadly stealth predators, dust mantas lurk just below the surface on desert worlds across the Universe. Despite a wingspan averaging 10 feet across and weighing 1 ton, dust mantas are nearly undetectable in their native habitat thanks to their pebbly, sand-colored hide. Like a ray through water, they can sense nearby vibrations and glide through sand flats and dunes to ambush unfortunate prey. Their wicked stinger injects a lethal toxin that breaks down flesh and bone, dissolving it into sand so filter-feeding dust mantas can strain particles of food from the resulting suspension.

0BVlwEjwpZTjpEJf.description:
The dust manta sprays a cloud of sand from its gills in a @Template[type:burst|distance:30]. All creatures in the cloud become @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.DmAIPqOBomZ7H95W]{Concealed}, and all creatures outside the cloud become concealed to creatures within it. The cloud lasts until the end of the dust manta's next turn. The dust manta can't use Spray Sand again for [[/gmr 1d4 #Recharge Spray Sand]]{1d4 rounds}. A non-dust manta creature that enters or starts its turn in the cloud must attempt a @Check[fortitude|dc:24|options:area-effect,inflicts:blinded,inflicts:dazzled] save.

Success The creature is unaffected.

Failure The creature is @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.TkIyaNPgTZFBCCuh]{Dazzled} for 1 minute or until it spends an Interact action to wipe the dirt and grit from its eyes.

Critical Failure The creature is @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.XgEqL1kFApUbl5Z2]{Blinded} for 1 round, after which it's dazzled for 1 minute or until it spends an Interact action to wipe its eyes.
0BVlwEjwpZTjpEJf.name: Spray Sand

EgWQJLHwTykDZ9kU.description:
Saving Throw @Check[fortitude|dc:24]

Maximum Duration 6 rounds

Stage 1 @Damage[2d4[poison]] damage (1 round)

Stage 2 @Damage[3d4[poison]] damage and @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.MIRkyAjyBeXivMa7]{Enfeebled 1} (1 round)

Stage 3 @Damage[3d4[poison]] damage and @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.MIRkyAjyBeXivMa7]{Enfeebled 2} (1 round)

Stage 4 @Damage[4d4[poison]] damage and @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.MIRkyAjyBeXivMa7]{Enfeebled 3} (1 round)

Stage 5 death, and the victim's body disintegrates into dust and can only be brought back via a wish ritual or similarly powerful magic
EgWQJLHwTykDZ9kU.name: Dust Manta Toxin

W7CXzVQ4H0jmfmoH.description: The dust manta can feel the slightest disturbance in nearby sand, granting it the ability to sense other creatures moving through or on top of the same body of sand that it's in. In addition, the dust manta ignores @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.DmAIPqOBomZ7H95W]{Concealment} from sandstorms, and they're immune to being @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.TkIyaNPgTZFBCCuh]{Dazzled} by sand or other grit.
W7CXzVQ4H0jmfmoH.name: Sandsense

eJLLrv9j7INHL4WH.description: The dust manta surges through sand to attack unwary prey. It Burrows up to twice its burrow Speed, then Leaps vertically up to 25 feet high, making a stinger Strike against a creature at any point during the jump (this lets it attack a creature within 35 feet of the surface). After the Leap, the dust manta falls to the ground but takes no damage from the fall if it lands on sand.
eJLLrv9j7INHL4WH.name: Burrowing Charge

obwRffH5SEiEpI9D.description: The dust manta's sand-colored hide allows it to [[/act hide]] in sand or any other fine, similarly colored substance even without cover or concealment.
obwRffH5SEiEpI9D.name: Disappear in Dust

Dust Manta.name: Dust Manta

Dust Worm.description:
Diaspora worms mutated to navigate sandy or barren asteroid surfaces, and as a result, dust worms trade agility for bulk and can resist radiation. Their electromagnetic manipulation affects small bits of ferrous material, allowing them to telekinetically wield sand and small metallic shards as weapons or cloaks.

"Space worm" is a nonscientific term for a xenobiologically complex clade of invertebrate animals and beasts that make their home in the vastness of space. Some, like the diaspora and dust worms, show signs of intelligence and are directly related to each other. Others, like the surnoch, evolved separately, with their origins completely unknown to science.

9SGJDR4iCNqdwIzI.description: A creature hit by the dust worm's tongue becomes @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.kWc1fhmv9LBiTuei]{Grabbed}. A creature can sever the tongue with a Strike against AC 21 that deals at least 14 slashing damage. This prevents the worm from using its tongue Strike until it regrows its tongue, which takes 1 day.
9SGJDR4iCNqdwIzI.name: Tongue Grab

ED4g5aTD9ZqccaqI.description:

This shroud moves with the worm and lasts for [[/gmr 1d6 #rounds]]{1d6 rounds}. The shroud grants the worm resistance 6 to physical damage, and any creature that ends its turn within the area takes @Damage[2d6[slashing]|options:area-damage] damage (@Check[reflex|dc:24|basic|options:area-effect] save).
ED4g5aTD9ZqccaqI.name: Sandstorm Veil

Pcnrr1GdwNXITJ1x.description:

Pcnrr1GdwNXITJ1x.name: Tongue Reel

dGhFgk1B0j9of59A.description: Dust worms sense their surroundings by reading electromagnetic fields, including disruptions caused by creatures or objects. dGhFgk1B0j9of59A.name: Electromagnetic Sight

Dust worms that take electricity damage must attempt a @Check[fortitude|dc:23] save.

Failure The worm is @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.XgEqL1kFApUbl5Z2]{Blinded} for 1 round.

Critical Failure The worm is blinded for 1 round, then dazzled for 1 round.

Ancient diaspora dust worms become paragons of worm colonization, conquering asteroids and painstakingly terraforming them to support worm society.

"Space worm" is a nonscientific term for a xenobiologically complex clade of invertebrate animals and beasts that make their home in the vastness of space. Each creature in the area must attempt a @Check[fortitude|dc:40|options:area-effect,inflicts:glitching,inflicts:stunned,inflicts:paralyzed] save. A creature with the tech trait also gains this glitching condition.

fmdL1CD5WWQITDHY.description: Psychic fungi are connected to a network of psychic filaments bonding all psychic fungi from the same colony. fmdL1CD5WWQITDHY.name: Mycelium Network

nwLCmCiSIvoxRQu9.description: The elder psychic fungus consumes the fluids and psychic essences from the brain of a creature within 10 feet that has been dead for no more than 1 minute. The elder psychic fungus regains the use of their highest-ranked spent innate spell. The creature is considered to have died due to a death effect.
nwLCmCiSIvoxRQu9.name: Drain Brain

pKa8pWaDXjw6sf9G.name: Lore (all subcategories of all creatures trained in Lore skills within 1 mile)

Electrovore.description:
Electrovores consume electricity as their sole source of sustenance. On their native planet, they fed on a species of three-headed electric eels, but volcanic activity wiped out their food source, sending electrovores to the brink of extinction. Electrovores found their salvation when explorers landed on their planet. The explorer's equipment and vessels had ample amounts of the electricity that the electrovores require. They stowed away on the vessels and soon spread throughout the Pact Worlds, causing damage and mayhem wherever they appeared.

Nothing terrifies a team of engineers more than finding an electrovore chewing on wires in a remote part of their starship. Where there's one electrovore, a dozen more likely await discovery. These 3-foot-tall reptilian creatures, sometimes called "conduit rats," breed rapidly and create such a disturbance in power sources that, over the course of days or weeks, a starship or factory might completely shut down from lack of power. There are many lifeless star vessels adrift in space because an electrovore infestation wasn't stopped in time.

Removing an infestation is no easy task, as electrovores are single-minded and cunning. The creatures are adept at finding places to hide, stalking their preferred energy sources and finding the correct moment to strike. Packs of electrovores even coordinate feedings in different areas at the same time to make it harder to stop them.

When confronted, electrovores rarely fight to the death, preferring to eat some electricity and retreat, hide, and heal, then return for another feast.

9yxF87SmovtifLvK.description: When an electrovore scores a critical hit with a tail Strike against a living creature wielding or wearing tech gear or a creature with the tech trait, it siphons off a portion of the target's electrical energy. This restores @Damage[5[healing]] Hit Points to the electrovore immediately, plus 1 Hit Point per minute for the next 10 minutes; the additional healing doesn't increase if the electrovore siphons multiple times.
9yxF87SmovtifLvK.name: Siphon

JDDwARFo31xQnvbo.description:
Effect The electrovore unleashes a shock wave that deals @Damage[2d6[electricity]|options:area-damage] damage to creatures in a @Template[type:emanation|distance:10] (@Check[reflex|dc:15|options:inflicts:glitching]). It can't use Electrical Discharge again for [[/gmr 1d4 #Recharge Electrical Discharge]]{1d4 rounds}.

Critical Success The target is unaffected.

Success The target takes half damage. Items in its possession with the tech trait becomes glitching 1. If the target has the tech trait, it becomes @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.6A2QDy8wRGCVQsSd]{Glitching 1}.

Failure As success, but full damage and @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.6A2QDy8wRGCVQsSd]{Glitching 2}.

Critical Failure As success, but double damage and @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.6A2QDy8wRGCVQsSd]{Glitching 3}.
JDDwARFo31xQnvbo.name: Electrical Discharge

gAkv1AF9ZQOF04Ks.description: An electrovore can sense electricity, including the electrical impulses found in most living creatures' nervous systems, as an imprecise sense at the listed range.
gAkv1AF9ZQOF04Ks.name: Electricsense

Electrovore.name: Electrovore

Elimination-Class Assassin Robot.description:
Elegant and deadly, elimination models rely upon their stealth fields to keep foes guessing and strike where least expected. Their advanced intelligence gives them the capacity to set up more complex ambushes as well as react to changes in the situation as needed and handle requests from the client. This could mean making the killing as subtle or as gruesome as possible, depending on the intent and message intended.

In some societies, machines automate many processes. It only makes sense, then, that some would attempt to automate the act of murder. Most manufacturers would never admit to creating such designs, forcing wealthy figures to go through hidden channels to acquire units from secret facilities or unscrupulous manufacturers. Regardless of their origins, these robots can be programmed with a target and set loose, the owner assured that either their target will be dead or will be unable to prove who tried to kill them thanks to the unit's fried circuitry.

0Qt2dqS8FwJWPa85.description:
Upgrades: 1

The edge of this precision-crafted foil is sharpened to the thickness of a single atom, using regenerating nanites to maintain itself after countless strikes.
0Qt2dqS8FwJWPa85.name: Integrated Advanced Nano-edge Rapier

1WzD7bSEDQqq4Z85.description: The elimination-class assassin robot's Strikes deal an additional 3d6 precision damage to @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.AJh5ex99aV6VTggg]{Off-Guard} creatures.
1WzD7bSEDQqq4Z85.name: Sneak Attack

6QyO7lbS4dpsEhvO.description:
Trigger The target of the elimination-class assassin robot's Target Tracking attempts a Strike against the robot

Effect The robot reads its target's movements, gaining a +2 circumstance bonus to AC against the triggering Strike.
6QyO7lbS4dpsEhvO.name: Accelerated Response

99gon6f4RWg8lI5r.description:
Frequency once per hour

Effect The elimination-class assassin robot becomes invisible for 10 minutes. If the robot uses a hostile action or moves more than half its Speed in a single action, the robot becomes visible again after it completes that action.
99gon6f4RWg8lI5r.name: Holographic Camouflage

EUhhqCOevU380JhI.description: The elimination-class assassin robot can Interact to draw or retract any of its integrated weapons as a free action. An observer must succeed at a @Check[perception|dc:40] check to notice a retracted weapon.
EUhhqCOevU380JhI.name: Retractable Weapons

MwA6fv2MlCFf7Aqs.description:
Upgrades: 1

This pistol automatically ejects used cartridges and loads new ammunition after every shot fired.
MwA6fv2MlCFf7Aqs.name: Integrated Advanced Semi-Auto Pistol

Rg30dQfBM0KbhJb1.description: The elimination-class assassin robot establishes a target lock on a creature it can see within 120 feet. The creature can't become @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.DmAIPqOBomZ7H95W]{Concealed} against the robot or [[/act create-a-diversion]] against the robot. This ability lasts until the robot loses line of sight with the target or the target otherwise becomes hidden.
Rg30dQfBM0KbhJb1.name: Target Tracking

l2mD1OoVZvjk8ju9.description: The circuitry of an assassin robot self-destructs upon the robot's destruction, making tracing its owner extremely difficult. Add 10 to the DC of a Computers check to recover data from a destroyed assassin robot.
l2mD1OoVZvjk8ju9.name: Burn Protocol

spFsX2ySNKEkIpWI.description:
Frequency once per day

Effect The elimination-class assassin robot restores @Damage[45[healing]] Hit Points to one technological creature or item.
spFsX2ySNKEkIpWI.name: Nanite Surge

Elindrian Acolyte.description:
These elindrians are the rank-and-file worshippers of the Terror of Ukulam. Recently risen from the dead by some primal force or occult upheaval—no one is sure—they single-mindedly pursue their grisly task of unearthing fellow elindrians across Castrovel; many others have risen from the dead, but most still remain buried. They stop only to attack other living creatures that intervene.

The people known as elindrians vanished eons ago into desolate husk-hives beneath the surface of the planet Castrovel. Until recently, they were creatures of legend, existing only in the most obscure formian histories. Now, scholars on Castrovel desperately search for additional records about elindrians, their origins, and—most importantly—the truth about their connection to the terrifying ooze-like creature that recently descended from their moon, Elindrae. One theory is that elindrians share some primal bond with the ooze-thing called the Terror of Ukulam, and perhaps both originate from Elindrae—other theories claim that elindrians created the ooze in the first place or that they're distant cousins to formians, corrupted by the Terror long ago.

RwNY58b7Xc1oAFDg.description:
Elindrians can communicate nearly instantaneously via a primal bond similar to a formian hive mind. While within telepathic range of at least one other elindrian with husk mind, an elindrian acolyte gains a +2 circumstance bonus to initiative rolls, Perception checks, and saving throws against mental effects. If one elindrian is aware of a combatant, all members of the husk mind within range are aware of it.

The elindrian's husk mind is integrated with their scent; for purposes of detecting other elindrians, formians, undead, or corpses, their scent is a precise sense, rather than imprecise.

An elindrian always knows the precise distance and direction to the @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.alien-core-bestiary.Actor.BFtNnevWKUCnocyn]{Terror of Ukulam}, so long as they're on the same plane of existence.
RwNY58b7Xc1oAFDg.name: Husk Mind

j5hWIfZMDWiH8LEz.name: Unfetter Allies

Elindrian Celebrant.description:
These elindrian warriors relish violence. Their only motivation seems to be spreading pain, which they themselves are immune to; their nerve endings developed in such a way that they can't feel pain at all, experiencing it in some way that causes them little to no suffering. As long as there's an elindrian queen nearby to revive them, celebrants spend most of their time battling one another, honing their capability to do violence until a better target comes along.

EZXkdZva06hZY8CE.description: A celebrant's painsaw is powered by the heart of another celebrant. If a celebrant is within 30 feet of a painsaw that contains their heart when the painsaw Strikes a creature, the celebrant regains a number of Hit Points equal to their level (typically 4). It's taboo for a celebrant to wield a painsaw made from their own heart or a heart from any celebrant whose death they didn't witness (or cause) themself. A painsaw otherwise functions in all ways like a painglaive but doesn't function with normal batteries. A single celebrant heart functions as a tactical battery when used with a painsaw; it recharges if the celebrant spends 10 minutes in the presence of an elindrian queen.

While no one has confirmed the existence of elindrian queens, the elindrians' few similarities to formians have led scholars to believe they must exist. Indeed, these formidable matriarchs are the primary force driving elindrians to unite with the Terror of Ukulam.

Hbujcj0OvYaahWAX.description:
You attempt to call forth the target's soul and return it to its body. This requires the target's body to be present and relatively intact. The target must have died within the past year. If @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.deities.Item.QZD0u1jxwz0kj8uI]{Pharasma} has decided that the target's time has come or the target doesn't wish to return, this ritual automatically fails, but you discover this after the successful Religion check and can end the ritual without paying the cost.

Critical Success You resurrect the target. They return to life with full Hit Points and the same spells prepared and points in their pools they had when they died, and still suffering from any long-term debilitations of the old body. The target meets an agent of their deity during the resurrection who inspires them, granting them a +1 status bonus to attack rolls, Perception, saving throws, and skill checks for 1 week. The target is also permanently changed in some way by their time in the afterlife, such as gaining a slight personality shift, a streak of white in the hair, or a strange new birthmark.

Success As critical success, except the target returns to life with 1 Hit Point and no spells prepared or points in any pools, and still is affected by any long-term debilitations of the old body. Instead of inspiring them, the character's time in the Boneyard has left them temporarily debilitated. The target is @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.i3OJZU2nk64Df3xm]{Clumsy 1}, @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.4D2KBtexWXa6oUMR]{Drained 1}, and @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.MIRkyAjyBeXivMa7]{Enfeebled 1} for 1 week; these conditions can't be removed or reduced by any means until the week has passed.

Failure Your attempt is unsuccessful.

Critical Failure Something goes horribly wrong-an evil spirit possesses the body, the body transforms into a special kind of undead, or some worse fate befalls the target.

Heightened (6th) You can resurrect a target of up to 12th level, and the base cost is 1,250 credits.

Heightened (7th) You can use resurrect even with only a small portion of the body; the ritual creates a new body on a success or critical success. The target must have died within the past decade. The ritual requires four secondary casters, each of whom must be at least half the target's level. The target can be up to 14th level, and the base cost is 2,000 credits.

Heightened (8th) As 7th rank, but the target can be up to 16th level and the base cost is 3,000 credits.

Heightened (9th) You can use resurrect even without the body as long as you know the target's name and have touched a portion of its body at any time. The target must have died within the past century, and it doesn't gain the negative conditions on a success. The ritual requires eight secondary casters, each of whom must be at least half the target's level. The target can be up to 18th level, and the base cost is 6,000 credits.

Heightened (10th) As 9th rank, except it doesn't matter how long ago the target died. The ritual requires 16 secondary casters, each of whom must be at least half the target's level. The target can be up to 20th level, and the ritual's base cost is 10,000 credits.
Hbujcj0OvYaahWAX.name: Resurrect (elindrians only; up to 10 elindrians with one casting and a cast time of only 10 minutes if they perished within the last hour)

The creatures take @Damage[3d6[mental],1d6[persistent,mental]] damage (@Check[will|dc:40|basic] save) and are @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 2} on a failure (or @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 4} on a critical failure). On a critical success, creatures are temporarily immune to Vision of Elindrae for 24 hours.
N1MvcFZ9e7YTZSC7.name: Vision of Elindrae

You point at a creature and invoke the demise of all things. The target takes 70 void damage with a basic Fortitude save. Heightened (+1) The damage increases by 10.

Emganat.description:
Emganats were first encountered during the Krethiskar subcolony's sudden emergence and the first attacks on Szandite Collective space. These wolf-sized components can burrow beneath the ground, and they move at great speeds to reach a location where they can set up an ambush. Then, once they detect a threat, the emganats spring forth from their burrowed positions and lay into their foes with an acidic cannon located in their mouths. The more emganats that unleash their bio-acid on foes, the faster the substance dissolves their targets in an agonizing display.

Developing far out in the Vast from an insectile species known as kucharns, the Swarm is considered the greatest threat in existence for several cultures. Composed of countless subcolonies, each consisting of myriad component subspecies, the Swarm is a vast host that acts in psychic union for the purpose of consuming all matter across the cosmos. Most frightening of all is the Swarm's ability to assimilate the knowledge and DNA of those they consume. Thanks to its pre-Gap development of star travel, the Swarm had already consumed innumerable systems before history short-circuited, and the Swarm's pace only accelerated once it received access to the Signal and the hyperspace dimension known as the Drift.

Worlds touched by the Swarm are drained of their natural resources and rendered barren places known as huskworlds. What outsiders consider to be "Swarm space" is little more than a swathe of lifeless worlds that the Swarm have consumed in its reckless advance. The Swarm so thoroughly strips these worlds that surveyors struggle to find even trace amounts of inorganic resources, such as rare minerals and water. Few of these huskworlds have been thoroughly explored, as oftentimes exploration awakens inert drones, theorized to have been left behind in case the devoured system was ever colonized and repopulated. Pockets of Swarm activity exist well beyond this region of space, as the Swarm sent out countless subcolonies in the ages before the Gap, and even now, only some of them have reached their intended destinations.

The Swarm is perhaps most known in the current era for two important facts. First, its assault on the Pact Worlds and the Veskarium led to the cessation of hostilities and tenuous alliance between the two powers. Second, the Swarm is the direct ancestor of the shirren species. Having broken away sometime during the Gap, shirrens found succor with the deity Hylax, who was believed to have evolved from a pre-Swarm kucharn and who turned her back on the ravenous entity the Swarm has evolved into.

In recent years, the Swarm had been seen as little more than a distant boogeyman with no activities save for classified actions in the Suskillon system in the Vast. However, the recent discovery of the missing Szandite world of Krethiskar inadvertently awoke a dormant subcolony that had been responsible for the world's consumption. Since then, the newly dubbed Krethiskar subcolony has become a scourge of Near Space, engaged in an active invasion of Szandite Collective worlds and poised to spill over into other powers like the Veskarium and Pact Worlds. This rediscovered subcolony has begun rapid evolution of its components and remains cut off from the wider Swarm, but it still represents a clear danger to Near Space.

19ZPmLm8To1xuw1L.description: 30 feet. All allies with colony mind within the listed range of each other are in constant telepathic communication and are aware of all threats any individual knows about. While within range of at least one ally with colony mind, when a creature rolls a success on a save against a mental effect, it gets a critical success instead.

BCxeOJPLyWJkKdMd.name: Burrowing Reveal

Emissar Angel.description:
Emissars, or propaganda angels, are a divine embodiment of radical hope and the celestial answer to information warfare. Some emissars spring from the sainted souls of revolutionary leaders or celebrities who used their platforms to help people in life, having been transformed into a celestial in their afterlife. Others spontaneously form out of the condensed faith and desires of a movement or ideal.

Emissar angels take on the role of celestial spin doctors and political organizers, inspiring their allies to rally together and keep pushing toward a goal even when defeat seems inevitable. Emissars often support mortal causes that align with their own beliefs and goals, and while they always hope to change hearts with an inspiring speech or an act of radical kindness, emissars aren't afraid to fight for what they believe in—no matter the cost to themselves. As soon as a battle ends, their first priority is caring for their allies and saving any enemies who might be swayed to join the cause. While their allies usually appreciate their unshakable hope and upbeat attitude, their opponents resent what can be construed as the emissars' toxic positivity and comforting lies.

While many angels in modern times ascended from mortal souls across the cosmos, these celestial beings were among the first creatures to exist in all the cosmos. Warriors and messengers of the gods, they're utterly devoted to their cause, whether that be destroying evil or spreading a deity's message across the galaxy.

Byb80uNPBX3kcpUL.description:
The emissar commands an ally within 30 feet to ignore a harmful effect and keep fighting. The target gains 2d10 temporary Hit Points for 1 minute and suppresses one condition that's currently affecting it for the next [[/gmr 1d4 #rounds]]{1d4 rounds}, chosen from the following list: @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.yblD8fOR1J8rDwEQ]{Confused}, @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.HL2l2VRSaQHu9lUw]{Fatigued}, @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.sDPxOjQ9kx2RZE8D]{Fleeing}, @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened}, or @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.e1XGnhKNSQIm5IXg]{Stupefied}. The target is then temporarily immune to Spin Doctor for 1 hour.

@UUID[Compendium.sf2e.bestiary-effects.Item.ncmWr1EPq7nGErQf]{Effect: Spin Doctor}
Byb80uNPBX3kcpUL.name: Spin Doctor

K8FhkEV1xxbysmNY.description: 30 feet. Allies within the angel's aura gain a +1 status bonus to all saves against emotion and mental effects. Enemies in the area take a –1 status penalty to all saves against emotion and mental effects.
K8FhkEV1xxbysmNY.name: Encouraging Hope

p64pQczzyNooGJ1q.description:
You materialize a handheld @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.equipment.Item.oRuWi8EhgBiS3cbh]{Musical Instrument (Handheld, Commercial)} in your grasp. The instrument is typical for its type, but it plays for only you. It vanishes when the spell ends. If you cast summon instrument again, any instrument you previously summoned disappears.

Heightened (3rd) The instrument is instead a @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.equipment.Item.TwnyjvE7ZX35lCrj]{Musical Instrument (Handheld, Tactical)}.
p64pQczzyNooGJ1q.name: Summon Instrument

qjvG1y1Ax1IjxXDr.description: The emissar angel urges their allies to hustle for the cause. Until the beginning of the emissar's next turn, the emissar and their allies within 100 feet that can sense the angel gain a +5-foot status bonus to their Speeds.
qjvG1y1Ax1IjxXDr.name: Morale Boost

Emissary-Class Infiltrator Robot.description:
While many of the earliest infiltrator robots were designed for more direct stealth missions, the emissary-class infiltrator robots were created for more insidious tasks. These include planting evidence, spreading rumors and propaganda, and generally creating unrest or fomenting open rebellion.

Programmed with a sophisticated virtual intelligence and constructed with the ability to disguise itself as a creature of flesh and blood, an emissary-class infiltrator robot can wreak havoc on an organization or settlement without ever having to engage in combat. They are considered the ultimate tool in corporate or governmental espionage and fetch a high price on most illegal markets.

Brought to the forefront during the war against the Veskarium, and further perfected by various corporate interests within the Pact Worlds, infiltrator robots are known for being able to get into places where no one else could. Generally small and agile, infiltrator robots sneak into enemy territory and either download precious data or record incriminating evidence.

J14b99eUm89shHfx.description: An emissary-class infiltrator robot is covered in a layer of synthetic programmable skin that counts as a disguise kit. The robot can alter the skin over the course of a minute to Impersonate a Medium humanoid ancestry or specific person (if it has information about that person or has previously interacted with them). If the robot makes a retractable spike Strike or uses Morphing Visage, it takes a –4 circumstance penalty to its Deception DCs and skill checks to Impersonate against any who witnessed the action.
J14b99eUm89shHfx.name: Adaptive Disguise

PtbwlOhW40i6etQb.description: An emissary-class infiltrator robot's Strikes deal an additional 3d6 precision damage to sickened creatures.
PtbwlOhW40i6etQb.name: Exploit Nausea

pmwJ903phA7cZi5t.description:
By sending ripples through its synthetic skin, the emissary-class infiltration robot creates a nauseating display that affects all creatures within 20 feet that can see it. Each creature in the area must attempt a @Check[will|dc:30] save.

Critical Success The creature is unaffected and becomes immune to the robot's Morphing Visage for 10 minutes.

Success The creature is unaffected.

Failure The creature is @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.fesd1n5eVhpCSS18]{Sickened 1}.

Critical Failure The creature is @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.fesd1n5eVhpCSS18]{Sickened 2}.
pmwJ903phA7cZi5t.name: Morphing Visage

Emissary-Class Infiltrator Robot.name: Emissary-Class Infiltrator Robot

Empathnid.description:
Empathnids take a liking to those who show them genuine empathy. While they usually avoid combat, empathnids jump into action if their friends are threatened.

Empathnids have tremendous empathy for other creatures. The fact that the 8-inch spidery creatures come in a variety of colors and have a lifesaving venom likely explains why they're frequently used as companions or pets across the Pact Worlds.

OX4szBZ1VDeLQJSs.description:
Frequency once per day

Requirements The empathnid is sharing a space with a creature with the dying condition

Effect The empathnid injects its proto-venom into the creature. That creature loses the dying condition, though it remains @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.fBnFDH2MTzgFijKf]{Unconscious} at 0 Hit Points.
OX4szBZ1VDeLQJSs.name: Stabilizing Antivenom

dFPhNJAb6OJn8jLO.description: This is a precise sense against creatures under an emotion effect or in the grips of overwhelming emotions (at the GM's discretion). Against other creatures, this is an imprecise sense. Creatures immune to emotion or mental effects or under the effects of a @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.spells.Item.b515AZlB0sridKSq]{Calm} spell are undetectable by emotionsense.
dFPhNJAb6OJn8jLO.name: Emotionsense

ntvojTjEjKSSYLp5.description: Allies sharing the same space as the empathnid receive a +1 circumstance bonus on saving throws against emotion and mental effects.
ntvojTjEjKSSYLp5.name: Moral Support

Empathnid.name: Empathnid

Emvermod.description:
A form of house spirit, the emvermod, or "moderator fey," is a shy resident of one or more online communities who helps keep the online space vibrant, engaged, and orderly. They often take on the appearance of their avatar, choosing one that fits with the other members of their infosphere niche.

When given proper respect, an emvermod is a diligent administrator who helps an online community thrive while working alongside other moderators in the online space. When disrespected or accused of causing harm to the community, they cause all sorts of mischief, such as deleting posts, shadow banning members, and even imitating other users.

3PuUtfjiAJF9Si1c.description:
You delete data from a device or object with a flamboyant magical gesture. This data might be handwritten, printed, or digital. You delete up to 1,500 words' worth of text, one page of content, or one display screen worth of text or other visual information. Non-magical writing in or on an unattended or held object is automatically deleted. Attempt a counteract check to delete digital or magical writing. If you fail to delete writing that's part of a hazard, you trigger the hazard. This can't be used to delete the contents of a spellbook or similar means of storing magical formulas or spells.

If you target an attended tech item with the tracking trait, attempt a counteract check. On a success, the item becomes glitching 1. A creature holding the item can Interact to restart the software, reducing the glitching value by 1.

Heightened (7th) You can delete all the data stored locally on a single device or book, or all the data on a device or book related to a specific name, topic, or category.
3PuUtfjiAJF9Si1c.name: Delete (At Will)

DnTmUydEMQUuQJsM.description: An emvermod can sense items and creatures with active accounts on any community they moderate as an imprecise sense at the listed range. They recognize community members, even if they use an infosphere alias.
DnTmUydEMQUuQJsM.name: Modvision

cFXI3b2CCQlwgIme.description: An online community moderated by an emvermod never experiences random bugs or downtime. Any checks to @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.actions.Item.Yn4jLPVWVE1vtAaF]{Access Infosphere}, @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.actions.Item.rmwa3OyhTZ2i2AHl]{Craft} virtual items, @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.actions.Item.QyzlsLrqM0EEwd7j]{Earn Income}, or @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.actions.Item.RF8xNJ8QsMwogerB]{Hack} using the community as a tool receive a +2 circumstance bonus. If the emvermod is unfriendly, such checks take a –2 circumstance penalty instead. An emvermod must spend a week in an online space to become a moderator.
cFXI3b2CCQlwgIme.name: Dutiful Moderator

kdCRn1cxL4csIXrl.description:
The target can understand all words regardless of language and also speak the languages of other creatures. When in a mixed group of creatures, each time the target speaks, it can choose a creature and speak in a language that creature understands, even if the target doesn't know what language that is.

Heightened (7th) The duration is 8 hours.
kdCRn1cxL4csIXrl.name: Truespeech (Constant)

kqKGJp0qyEKflHZ8.description:
Frequency once per 10 minutes

Effect A creature within 60 feet with a comm unit or other computer connected to an infosphere must attempt a @Check[will|dc:18] save as the emvermod tries to ban it from communicating.

Critical Success No effect, and the creature is temporarily immune to Shadow Ban for 1 day.

Success The creature is unaffected.

Failure The creature can't use auditory actions or communicate, even by gesturing, generating text, or using telepathy. This also prevents the target from casting spells due to the magical words involved in casting, with the exception of subtle spells. This effect lasts for 1 minute, or until the moderator fey retracts the Shadow Ban or dies, whichever comes first.

Critical Failure As failure, except this effect lasts 24 hours.
kqKGJp0qyEKflHZ8.name: Shadow Ban

y9ZxiKiImUFlrrOB.description: An emvermod is naturally invisible while holding a comm unit or in a virtual space. They don't appear to have an account in any infosphere space they moderate. They can become visible, or even selectively visible, allowing only specific people to see them.
y9ZxiKiImUFlrrOB.name: Shy

Emvermod.name: Emvermod

Enraged Noquasar.description:
A noquasar's rage increases as its torture extends over many years.

When a solarian perishes while out of sync with the cycle of stars, their soul might become entangled with their solar mote. Extreme cosmic forces act on the soul as it attempts to reach the River of Souls, stretching it infinitely thin for all of eternity.

pJc2a4FjHle9zxZ5.description: A creature critically hit by an enraged noquasar's graviton flare is knocked @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.j91X7x0XSomq8d60]{Prone}. If the target is flying, it falls up to 30 feet.
pJc2a4FjHle9zxZ5.name: Gravity Crash

qdvZgxq1BwufOJrR.description: The enraged noquasar unleashes plasma in a @Template[type:emanation|distance:10] or @Template[type:line|distance:30]. Each creature in the area takes @Damage[3d6[fire]|options:area-damage] damage (@Check[reflex|dc:21|basic|options:area-effect] save). A creature that critically fails its save also takes @Damage[1d8[persistent,electricity]|options:area-damage] damage and is knocked @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.j91X7x0XSomq8d60]{Prone}. The enraged noquasar can't use Ionized Plasma Blast again for [[/gmr 1d4 #Recharge Ionized Plasma Blast]]{1d4 rounds}.
qdvZgxq1BwufOJrR.name: Ionized Plasma Blast

Enraged Noquasar.name: Enraged Noquasar

Erabryth.description:
When androids die or give their bodies up for renewal—a celebrated and respected event akin to procreation—it's the silent and calm erabryths who usher their souls into the Boneyard. Beings of reflection and introspection, these psychopomps help androids come to terms with their choices, reconcile the trying events of their lives, and realize that the time for renewal has finally come.

Erabryths are lanky and androgynous, with reflective, ribboned flesh and a mirrored disk for a face. They communicate through posture and emotive lights, offering comfort through their soothing, persistent presence.

Psychopomps are death's shepherds who safeguard the cycle of life, death, and the afterlife by slaying undead or ushering souls safely through the Boneyard.

2f9jMSQfqTP2oWKt.description:
Illusions bend light around the target, rendering it @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.zJxUflt9np0q4yML]{Invisible}. This makes it @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.VRSef5y1LmL2Hkjf]{Undetected} to all creatures, though the creatures can attempt to find the target, making it @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.iU0fEDdBp3rXpTMC]{Hidden} to them instead. If the target uses a hostile action, the spell ends after that hostile action is completed.

Heightened (4th) The spell lasts 1 minute, but it doesn't end if the target uses a hostile action.
2f9jMSQfqTP2oWKt.name: Invisibility (at will; self only)

7SXoFgzCKSyWLlQJ.description:
The erabryth forces a creature within 60 feet to relive its most painful memories and regrets in an instant, confronting it with it difficult memories to help it reconcile its actions and let go of its pain. The target must attempt a @Check[will|dc:17|options:inflicts:frightened,inflicts:stunned] save. Regardless of the result, the target is then temporarily immune to Forced Reflection for 1 day.

Critical Success The target is unaffected.

Success The target is @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 1}.

Failure The target is @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.dfCMdR4wnpbYNTix]{Stunned 1} and frightened 1.

Critical Failure The target is @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.dfCMdR4wnpbYNTix]{Stunned 2} and @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 2}.
7SXoFgzCKSyWLlQJ.name: Forced Reflection

HIxj8NAGalDHg7Mv.description:
Trigger A creature hits the erabryth with a melee or ranged Strike

Effect The erabryth reflects some of their attacker's anger and aggression back at them. The erabryth gains resistance 3 to the triggering damage and deals @Damage[3[mental]] damage to their attacker.
HIxj8NAGalDHg7Mv.name: Reflect Aggression

i1OoK1fCXrmApXm4.description: An erabryth's Strikes have the benefit of a ghost killer upgrade and deal an extra 1d4 void damage to living creatures or 1d4 vitality damage to undead.
i1OoK1fCXrmApXm4.name: Shepherd's Touch

k1hxrHhmAgRb0zbw.description:
15 feet. A creature that begins its turn within the area must attempt a @Check[will|dc:14] save.

Critical Success The creature is unaffected and is temporarily immune to buffering zone for 1 day.

Success The creature treats the buffering zone as difficult terrain for 1 round.

Failure As success, and the creature is pushed back 5 feet and takes a –1 status penalty to attack rolls for 1 round.

@UUID[Compendium.sf2e.bestiary-effects.Item.X5oMEjGHa8WsCiqW]{Effect: Buffering Zone (Failure)}

Critical Failure As failure, but the creature is pushed back beyond the boundary of the buffering zone and can't reenter the buffering zone for 1 round.
k1hxrHhmAgRb0zbw.name: Buffering Zone

Erabryth.name: Erabryth

Excuba.description:
Unlike all other known types of spectra, excuba spectra are fragmented creatures made of countless tiny pieces that act together as a single networked whole. No accounts of an excuba encounter exist before the Drift crashed, and prevailing theories hold that either the trauma of the crisis created them, or they were created by the Drift as a response to the crisis itself. Whatever the case, excuba encounters have become all too common. These spectra swarms are often dispatched to infiltrate mortal worlds as spies or observers. They collect information for more powerful spectra like wyspirias to analyze and preserve. Some speculate that excubas have always lurked in the galaxy as invisible spies for other spectra, and that the Drift Crisis merely caused them to take a new, less cohesive form.

In the Great Beyond, time is measured not in hundreds, thousands, or millions of years, but rather in eons—in iterations of reality itself. Only rising to prominence within the last three centuries alongside the advent and proliferation of Drift technology, spectra have thrived in a burgeoning niche of the otherwise stagnant zeitgeist of the Great Beyond.

Though their origins and objectives remain shrouded in mystery, encounters with spectra revolve around new technological discoveries, sharing the knowledge of faster-than-light travel, and protecting the Drift. No one knows if spectra existed before the Drift, but their connection to the hyperspace plane is indisputable. Prominent metaphysicians believe spectra were created as amalgams of raw quintessence pulled into the Drift, just as the Drift itself grows from pieces of the Multiverse. If this is true, spectra's interest in the proliferation of Drift technology takes a subtle sinister turn, as each new Drift engine serves to harvest the Great Beyond and all its denizens for the growth of the Drift and spectra themselves.

2c3B9s3gDpRzSv9l.description: 100 feet. An excuba can communicate telepathically with any item or creature with the tech trait within their aura as well as with other technologically telepathic creatures (such as those with shortwave and similar abilities). This ability also allows the spectra to remotely attempt Computers checks within their aura.
2c3B9s3gDpRzSv9l.name: Digital Telepathy

771vU0P9EccjLB6w.description: The excuba can communicate through items and creatures with the tech trait, projecting sound from and speaking through the item or creature's voice, speakers, or other audio output. In addition, the excuba can use any item or creature with the tech trait within their digital telepathy aura as the point of origin for their spells and abilities when calculating range, distance, line of effect, and area of effect.
771vU0P9EccjLB6w.name: Arc Network

9BqZmg06HAzysR6Y.description: An excuba can store data within their body as if they were a computer. Hacking an excuba requires three successes against their Will DC to access their data.
9BqZmg06HAzysR6Y.name: Data Vault

PPXVa8efjBsgOpXE.description: Each enemy creature in the swarm's space takes @Damage[2d8[sonic]|options:area-damage] damage (@Check[reflex|dc:21|basic|options:area-effect,inflicts:glitching] save). On a failure, creatures and objects with the tech trait become @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.6A2QDy8wRGCVQsSd]{Glitching 1} (or @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.6A2QDy8wRGCVQsSd]{Glitching 2} on a critical failure).
PPXVa8efjBsgOpXE.name: Swarming Synchronization

Syx02TRJsDTbFTXy.description:
You touch one object and concentrate on a dataset contained within it, such as a story, message, file, infosphere site, audio recording, or video. You understand the gist of the dataset and can quickly locate the most relevant pages or sections to your search. If the dataset is written or otherwise communicated in a language you don't know, or you attempt to gain information from a computer you don't have access to (such as one with a password you don't know), the spell fails.

If you Cast this Spell as part of a @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.actions.Item.t5nBkpjroaq7QBGK]{Research} activity, you treat a critical failure as a failure instead.
Syx02TRJsDTbFTXy.name: Skim Data (at will)

bSGMqAD0MHu8veSv.description: An excuba's visual appearance is altered when the excuba is perceived by creatures, items, and objects with the tech trait (such as robotic creatures, cameras, and sensors) unless they succeed at a @Check[perception|against:deception] check against the excuba's Deception DC. Excubas in their swarm form appear to be formless shadows and are additionally @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.DmAIPqOBomZ7H95W]{Concealed}, while excubas in their humanoid forms register as familiar- or unremarkable-looking humanoids.
bSGMqAD0MHu8veSv.name: Autoencode

eJm2qUdCE9QyTBge.description: An excuba has an internal biomechanical Drift engine, allowing them to function as a Drift engine for a starship or vehicle they pilot as a 1-minute activity. An excuba can enter or exit the Drift themself as a 1-minute activity. When an excuba gets a critical failure on a Piloting check to Navigate or Plot a Course through the Drift, they get a failure instead.
eJm2qUdCE9QyTBge.name: Slip Drive

eYSNACkAPlsgVxkS.description:
The target can understand all words regardless of language and also speak the languages of other creatures. When in a mixed group of creatures, each time the target speaks, it can choose a creature and speak in a language that creature understands, even if the target doesn't know what language that is.

Heightened (7th) The duration is 8 hours.
eYSNACkAPlsgVxkS.name: Truespeech (constant)

kWHb8KYyngZXzWb0.description:
The excuba can take on the appearance of any Small or Medium humanoid.

@Localize[PF2E.NPC.Abilities.Glossary.ChangeShape]
kWHb8KYyngZXzWb0.name: Change Shape

lhWDzb0y7ioOWlor.description:
Frequency once per minute

Effect The excuba selects one creature with the tech trait in their space, searching its mind and memories. The creature must attempt a @Check[will|dc:21] save.

Critical Success The creature is unaffected and immune to Data Search for 24 hours.

Success The creature is unaffected.

Failure The excuba accesses the creature's memories of the last 24 hours, downloading a holographic copy into their data vault and gaining insights into the creature's tactics. The creature must roll twice and take the lower result on its next attack roll, skill check, or saving throw against the excuba or one of the excuba's spells or abilities. This effect has the misfortune trait.

Critical Failure As failure, but the excuba also obtains a specific type of memory (such as what happened during the last time the creature encountered a Drift beacon) regardless of how long ago it was. The target creature loses this memory until it gains access to the excuba's data vault.
lhWDzb0y7ioOWlor.name: Data Search

zpqUH68Ikt0xGYm5.description: The excuba senses creatures and objects with the tech trait as a precise sense within the listed range.
zpqUH68Ikt0xGYm5.name: Techsense

Excuba.name: Excuba

Ferrofluid Magneto-Cluster.description:
Magneto-clusters are usually created when several smaller ferrofluid oozes combine. There have, however, been documented cases of these creatures spontaneously appearing after large industrial accidents. Like their smaller "cousins," magneto-cluster oozes seek out sources of electromagnetism. They also search for and consume magnetic objects and metals capable of being magnetized. They completely disregard organic life and usually are only a danger when a life-form doesn't want to relinquish their magnetic material. Some clusters consume so much metal and objects they're mistaken for scavenger slimes. Any metal consumed by a magneto-cluster immediately becomes magnetic.

As living magnetic accelerators, ferrofluid magneto-cluster oozes are capable of launching the metal they collect at high speeds as a defense mechanism. They do so at such high velocities as to make even a simple metal shard accelerate fast enough to puncture high-tech ballistic armor.

Oozes of many types lurk in dark and abandoned places across the galaxy, emerging only to satiate their appetites and threaten adventurers, explorers, and hapless workers alike.

8LYt0QTjLRu5rZeO.description: The ferrofluid magneto-cluster instantly Attaches to a creature within its magnetic field that meets the requirements of that ability. A ferrofluid ooze can't use this ability again for [[/gmr 1d4 #Recharge Magnetic Leap]]{1d4 rounds}.
8LYt0QTjLRu5rZeO.name: Magnetic Leap

AWkRzGrUBdHaHGHL.description: 30 feet. A ferrofluid magneto-cluster is surrounded by a constant field that interferes with nearby equipment. Items with the tech trait inside the aura take a –1 circumstance penalty to all checks using them. Unattended metal objects in the aura of 1 Bulk or less are pulled adjacent to the ooze.
AWkRzGrUBdHaHGHL.name: Magnetic Field

DXn2Z8czJb1FO6KW.description:
A ferrofluid magneto-cluster can attach itself to any creature its size or larger that has the tech trait or is wearing or wielding items with the tech trait. This is similar to Grab, but the ooze moves with that creature rather than holding it in place.

As long as the ooze is attached, it's @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.AJh5ex99aV6VTggg]{Off-Guard}, and the creature it's attached to must succeed at a @Check[flat|dc:11] to Interact with items with the tech trait. On a failure, the item becomes attached to the ooze (treat as if being held by the ooze).
DXn2Z8czJb1FO6KW.name: Attach

Ig0gF87YLvDavWVI.description: A ferrofluid magneto-cluster can feel magnetic fields, allowing it to detect large sources of magnetic metal (Bulk 1 or greater) and items with the tech trait within the listed range.
Ig0gF87YLvDavWVI.name: Magnetic Sense

TZsF3N5NFXl3Z3qo.description:
The ferrofluid magneto-cluster shifts the polarity of its magnetic field, causing it to briefly repulse magnetic objects. Each creature in a @Template[type:emanation|distance:30] must attempt a @Check[reflex|dc:30] save or else they're forced to drop any items with the tech trait they're wielding in an adjacent square.

In addition, each creature with the tech trait or wearing armor with the tech trait must succeed at a @Check[fortitude|dc:30] save or be knocked @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.j91X7x0XSomq8d60]{Prone}.
TZsF3N5NFXl3Z3qo.name: Polarity Shift

lFGhYQ0e3gyr2scc.description: A ferrofluid magneto-cluster that takes fire damage has its magnetic field deactivated until the end of the ooze's next turn. It releases itself from any creature it was attached to, drops any held items, and can't use Magnetic Leap or Attach until its magnetic field returns.
lFGhYQ0e3gyr2scc.name: Demagnetization

wa4NJ2GeUbimOSNx.description: The ferrofluid magneto-cluster contracts, then spews metal shards in a @Template[type:cone|distance:30], dealing @Damage[5d8[piercing]|options:area-damage] damage (@Check[reflex|dc:30|basic] save). Any creature that fails its save is also @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.i3OJZU2nk64Df3xm]{Clumsy 1} for 1 round (@UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.i3OJZU2nk64Df3xm]{Clumsy 2} on a critical failure).
wa4NJ2GeUbimOSNx.name: Metal Storm

Ferrofluid Magneto-Cluster.name: Ferrofluid Magneto-Cluster

Ferrofluid Ooze.description:
Since the earliest days of space travel, engineers have used ferromagnetic fluids to help with the construction, operation and maintenance of starships. It was only a matter of time before overeager spellcasters tinkered with this substance and inadvertently imbued a modicum of life into it, creating yet another strain of ooze to plague the cosmos. These strange oozes exert magnetic powers and have an instinctive desire to seek out sources of electromagnetism. Ferrofluid oozes are considered galactic nuisances, and many shipyards across the Pact Worlds have begun retaining the services of expert "ooze control" agents to ensure these fluids don't impede their day-to-day operations.

A common ferrofluid ooze appears as a spiked pool of dark metal liquid that shifts in erratic ways but always reacts to nearby magnetic sources. They're mostly found hiding in the darkest corners of starships and space stations.

Oozes of many types lurk in dark and abandoned places across the galaxy, emerging only to satiate their appetites and threaten adventurers, explorers, and hapless workers alike.

fTNPtMto9oFQMt9W.description: A ferrofluid ooze can feel magnetic fields, allowing it to detect large sources of magnetic metal (Bulk 1 or greater) and items with the tech trait within the listed range.

A ferrofluid ooze can attach itself to any creature its size or larger that has the tech trait or is wearing or wielding items with the tech trait. This is similar to Grab, but the ooze moves with that creature rather than holding it in place.

As long as the ooze is attached, it's @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.AJh5ex99aV6VTggg]{Off-Guard}, and the creature it's attached to must succeed at a @Check[flat|dc:11] to Interact with items with the tech trait. On a failure, the item becomes attached to the ooze (treat as if being held by the ooze).
jGlbekQnUM3FQyhj.name: Attach

lRZz886ytCXBzyha.description: The ferrofluid ooze instantly Attaches to a creature within its magnetic field that meets the requirements of that ability. A ferrofluid ooze can't use this ability again for [[/gmr 1d4 #Recharge Magnetic Leap]]{1d4 rounds}.
lRZz886ytCXBzyha.name: Magnetic Leap

oYFsSKQObiuzY2wE.description: A ferrofluid ooze that takes fire damage has its magnetic field deactivated until the end of the ooze's next turn. It releases itself from any creature it was attached to, drops any held items, and can't use Magnetic Leap or Attach until its magnetic field returns.

Ferrofluid Ooze.name: Ferrofluid Ooze

Finitrium Fatebender.description: Finitrium fatebenders are powerful magical constructs created from refined finitrium, a rare starmetal with divinatory properties. Thanks to their ability to see—and react to—the future, finitrium fatebenders make exceptional guardians and formidable foes.

8bq2F3IQg0EVOsd9.description: The finitrium fatebender releases a wave of twisted futures and shattered possibilities, dealing @Damage[16d6[mental]|options:area-damage] damage in a @Template[type:cone|distance:60] (@Check[will|dc:36|basic] save). The finitrium fatebender can't use Fate Wave again for [[/gmr 1d4 #Recharge Fate Wave]]{1d4 rounds}.
8bq2F3IQg0EVOsd9.name: Fate Wave

CQ1hxKV0MEM8LqbK.description:
Frequency once per day

Trigger The finitrium fatebender fails or critically fails an attack roll or saving throw

Effect The finitrium fatebender rerolls the triggering check and takes the better result.
CQ1hxKV0MEM8LqbK.name: Fated Outcome

HMUooRII309NV9fK.description:
Frequency once per round

Trigger The finitrium fatebender would be hit by a Strike

Effect Having foreseen the incoming attack, the finitrium fatebender shifts position, gaining a +4 circumstance bonus to AC against the triggering attack.
HMUooRII309NV9fK.name: Tactical Prescience

ShTXxV2xdI86CAPV.description: The finitrium fatebender Strides up to its Speed, pushing back each creature whose space it moves into and damaging creatures that try to stop its movement. A creature can attempt a @Check[fortitude|dc:40] save to bar the way, stopping the finitrium fatebender's movement on a success. On a critical success, the resisting creature takes no damage; otherwise, it's damaged as if hit by the finitrium fatebender's fist Strike.
ShTXxV2xdI86CAPV.name: Inexorable March

wyHrDIBNHnLKIeDW.description: 20 feet. A finitrium fatebender is surrounded by an aura of countless shifting potential futures—fragmented milliseconds of possibility all overlapping in a tumultuous blur. A creature that ends its turn in the aura must attempt a @Check[will|dc:33] save. If it fails, it's @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.fesd1n5eVhpCSS18]{Sickened 2} for 1 round (or [[/gmr 1d4 #rounds]]{1d4 rounds} on a critical failure). A creature that critically succeeds becomes temporarily immune to the aura for 1 day.
wyHrDIBNHnLKIeDW.name: A Million Fates

x37Qq2zNX0lGTruC.description: A finitrium fatebender gains a +5 circumstance bonus when rolling Perception for initiative, as it acts on flashes of insight harvested from potential futures.
x37Qq2zNX0lGTruC.name: Glimpse Fate

yL5ID8QZ9R8gSkjI.description: Any creature hit by the finitrium fatebender's fist or ray of twisted fate Strikes receives a vision of their impending death at the hands of the finitrium fatebender. It must succeed at a @Check[will|dc:36] save or become @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.e1XGnhKNSQIm5IXg]{Stupefied 2}; on a critical failure, the creature is also @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.dfCMdR4wnpbYNTix]{Stunned 1}. If the creature is already affected by foretold doom, it increases the appropriate stunned and stupefied values by 1 on a failed save, to a maximum of @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.dfCMdR4wnpbYNTix]{Stunned 2} and @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.e1XGnhKNSQIm5IXg]{Stupefied 4}. When the finitrium fatebender is destroyed, the creature has avoided this tragic fate and immediately recovers from its stupefied condition.
yL5ID8QZ9R8gSkjI.name: Foretell Doom

Finitrium Fatebender.name: Finitrium Fatebender

Flarysca.description:
What seem to be glimmering motes of dust drifting in a sunbeam might be the scattered forms of flaryscas drifting across space, dormant but poised to ignite at any moment. Flaryscas materialize ethereally within a sun's rays, dancing to the farthest reaches of space where they flare up for a brief, intense period, then presumably fade away into repose.

While pleasant to look at, flaryscas are responsible for unexplained deaths occurring on many worlds, and even in space. Their soporific aura lulls creatures to curl up lazily in the sun, ignoring cravings for sustenance as flaryscas cavort around these slumberers. While perfect for an afternoon nap or a leshy cosmonaut in search of a snack, on rare occasions such a slumber might prove deadly.

Elementals are energetic intrusions from the primal planes of existence. They take many forms, from mindless eddies in the wind or water to complex entities capable of wielding primal magic. The advent of space travel and the progress of technology have allowed even more living embodiments of the elements to manifest in the Universe.

Natural events like wildfires, solar storms, and floods can unleash hordes of unruly elementals on a planet or into a region of space. Sometimes, a gathering of powerful elementals causes a natural disaster on an epic scale, like an off-the-charts solar flare that fries a planet's power grid or a ceaseless storm swirling in a gas giant's atmosphere.

9A2MITu4XiQUDG1O.description:
Frequency once per round

Requirements The flarysca is standing within direct sunlight

Effect The flarysca teleports themself to another sunbeam or area of direct sunlight they can sense within 60 feet, with the effects of the translocate spell.
9A2MITu4XiQUDG1O.name: Light Jump

9pDq5zoadCGjsNsT.description:
Frequency once per minute

Effect The flarysca shines brightly, increasing the radius of their lazy sunlight aura by 5 feet for 1 minute.
9pDq5zoadCGjsNsT.name: Creeping Warmth

GpsTGSV55v6HOJ96.description:
The flarysca has @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.bestiary-ability-glossary-srd.Item.lR9R5Vld8Eu2Dha5]{Regeneration} 20 (deactivated by cold) while in direct sunlight. In addition to being deactivated by cold, this regeneration deactivates for 1 round whenever the flarysca takes an Attack action.

@Localize[PF2E.NPC.Abilities.Glossary.Regeneration]
GpsTGSV55v6HOJ96.name: Rejuvenate (Deactivated by Cold)

I36VtsGqzjXCv8Bm.description:
Trigger A creature interacts with or moves through a sunbeam containing a sleeping flarysca

Effect The flarysca startles awake, letting out a burst of fire as their body reconstitutes within the sunlight. The triggering creature and any other creature within 30 feet of the flarysca must succeed at a @Check[reflex|dc:25|basic] save or take @Damage[8d6[fire]] damage.
I36VtsGqzjXCv8Bm.name: Reactive Burst

bLQXCVYxsVGPIqlD.description:
15 feet. Creatures other than the flarysca that enter or begin their turn within the aura must attempt a @Check[fortitude|dc:25] save. On a failure, a creature becomes @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.i3OJZU2nk64Df3xm]{Clumsy 1}, or increases it clumsy value by 1 if it was already clumsy.

If it was already @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.i3OJZU2nk64Df3xm]{Clumsy 2} or greater, it instead becomes @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.fBnFDH2MTzgFijKf]{Unconscious} until it begins its turn outside the lazy sunlight aura. Creatures can't reduce their clumsy values while within the lazy sunlight aura.

On a critical success, a creature becomes temporarily immune to lazy sunlight for 1 hour.
bLQXCVYxsVGPIqlD.name: Lazy Sunlight

fsajWJabeib9uDRS.description: A flarysca can sense the presence of sunlight within 60 feet as a precise sense.
fsajWJabeib9uDRS.name: Sun Sense

Flarysca.name: Flarysca

Flayer Leech.description:
Flayer leeches are tiny, invertebrate hunters with multi-hinged mouths that have developed an interesting life cycle: they wear their victim's skin to pose as them, consuming their innards to reproduce.

Flayer leeches will kill and feed on living creatures, feasting on the bone marrow of their victims. This consumption gives them sustenance to survive for weeks. Flayer leeches disengage the tendrils of their petallike mouths, extending them up to 2 meters and using them to stitch together a prey's remains, leaving the brain for it to consume. They then use these tendrils as a pseudo-skeleton to give structure to the body and move it, allowing them to convincingly reanimate the corpse and take on its movements and previous life. The flayer leech lacks the corpse's specific memories, however, which can make it easy to spot for those familiar with the leech's victim. Flayer leeches use this disguise as a safe harbor while feeding off the remaining marrow and nervous system and will defend these new bodies like their home.

0CeIZZ2Amky50Gqb.description: A flayer leech consumes the brain of the corpse of a Medium or Small creature dead for no longer than an hour, taking over its body. It also stitches together any wounds the corpse might have, presenting only barely visible lines. It can use Stealth to [[/act impersonate skill=stealth]] and doesn't need a disguise kit to do so, but it takes a –2 circumstance penalty to the check if any creature engages the flayer leech in conversation for 1 minute. When in this effigy form, it loses its weakness to bludgeoning and gains weakness 5 to sonic damage. It can make proboscis melee Strikes through extension in its wrists, but it can't make subsonic blast ranged Strikes. A flayer leech can Dismiss the effigy.
0CeIZZ2Amky50Gqb.name: Create Effigy

4cUwXqWGoGffH0c0.description: While a flayer leech is in an effigy, it gains the ability to understand and speak all languages known by the corpse as well as knowledge of the corpse's physical abilities, identity, role in society, and personality. However, it doesn't gain the specific memories or knowledge of the corpse.
4cUwXqWGoGffH0c0.name: Effigy Identity

ETCfLQZKu9Rh90hz.description:

Effect The flayer leech vibrates its proboscis at subsonic speed, drilling into a creature's marrow or equivalent bone structure. The required creature must succeed at a @Check[fortitude|dc:21] saving throw or become @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.fesd1n5eVhpCSS18]{Sickened 1}. On a critical failure, it can't reduce this sickened condition for 1 minute.
ETCfLQZKu9Rh90hz.name: Drink Marrow

IntJhubTwQneDX3y.description:
Requirements The flayer leech is in an effigy

Any creature within 40 feet with the sickened condition from the flayer leech's Drink Marrow ability takes @Damage[3d8[sonic]] damage (@Check[fortitude|dc:21|basic] save).
IntJhubTwQneDX3y.name: Warp Bones

s0t3f3fWfKiZvsYv.description:
Requirements The flayer leech isn't currently in an effigy

s0t3f3fWfKiZvsYv.name: Mandible Dance

Flayer Leech.name: Flayer Leech

Free Captain.description:
Captain is the highest rank on board any vessel. They answer only to admirals of the Free Captains and only if their ship isn't engaged in active combat. This captain uses the void mode of her cutlass by default, the hundreds of shimmering stars in the blade representing the lives taken in her countless engagements.

The Free Captains have been a scourge of interstellar shipping across the Pact Worlds for generations, but since the adoption of Drift Lanes, the outlaws have expanded their reach and scale by targeting ships across the galaxy using the new standardized interstellar shipping routes.

5TtSi0PiNmNJGIj1.description: The Free Captain telepathically orders their crew to mercilessly slaughter one target. All allied creatures of equal or lower level within 60 feet of the Free Captain gain a +1 status bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls against one creature until the end of the Free Captain's next turn.
5TtSi0PiNmNJGIj1.name: Give 'Em No Quarter!

YKphA9q7R8akTvGU.description: This piece of wood or silver is emblazoned with an image representing a deity. Some divine spellcasters, such as clerics, can use a religious symbol of their deity to use certain abilities and cast some spells. A religious symbol can be worn on the body on a chain or pin, or can be held.
YKphA9q7R8akTvGU.name: Seashell Religious Symbol of Besmara

ly3Jm5e6LmCSYR7o.description: The Free Captain uses Area Fire with their starfall pistol split by their phase cutlass, causing the starry darkness to spread. The pistol's Area Fire uses a @Template[type:cone|distance:10] that deals @Damage[2d6[void]|options:area-damage] damage. Creatures that fail their save against the Area Fire become @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 1} (or @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 2} on a critical failure).
ly3Jm5e6LmCSYR7o.name: Stardust Storm

vVqDQPvu63YdR6xO.description: The stars of the Free Captain's cutlass seem to empower their starfall pistol, which deals an additional @Damage[2d6[void]] damage as long as the Free Captain is holding both weapons.
vVqDQPvu63YdR6xO.name: Soul Squall

Free Captain.name: Free Captain

Free Captain Gunner.description:
Leading the assault with an explosion of cannon fire, the gunner's role in a boarding party is to incite a rout while protecting their fellow crew by suppressing a ship's defenses.

The Free Captains have been a scourge of interstellar shipping across the Pact Worlds for generations, but since the adoption of Drift Lanes, the outlaws have expanded their reach and scale by targeting ships across the galaxy using the new standardized interstellar shipping routes.

CugYZrkH97K53L9W.description: A special payload gives the breaching gun the area (@Template[type:cone|distance:15]) and unwieldy traits until the end of the gunner's turn. The gunner makes an attack using Area Fire (@Check[reflex|dc:19|basic] save) that uses 3 projectiles. Enemies in the affected area who fail their save against the attack become @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.enA7BxAjBb7ns1iF]{Suppressed} until the start of the gunner's next turn.
CugYZrkH97K53L9W.name: Fire in the Hole!

FqiswOY4E4rW3pgV.description: The Free Captain gunner Switches Hands, then Raises a Shield or Reloads, in any order.
FqiswOY4E4rW3pgV.name: Raid Ready

l9grgMnh2mblvZ9H.description: A creature damaged by the gunner's breaching gun can't reduce its frightened condition until the gunner's next turn.
l9grgMnh2mblvZ9H.name: Shiver Your Timbers

lwsqV5dcFiHdvpPk.description: @Localize[PF2E.NPC.Abilities.Glossary.ShieldBlock] In addition to the normal use of Shield Block, a Free Captain gunner can use Shield Block to prevent damage from an area attack and also prevent damage that would be dealt to an adjacent ally instead of themself.
lwsqV5dcFiHdvpPk.name: Shield Block

ycFuNAqdi2DuZugE.description: You have four arms, which allows you to wield and hold up to four hands' worth of weapons and equipment. At any time, one pair of hands is designated as your active hands. You can change this designation from one pair of hands to another by taking the Switch Hands action, which is a single action. You can wield items only with your active hands.
ycFuNAqdi2DuZugE.name: Four-Armed

Free Captain Gunner.name: Free Captain Gunner

Free Captain Knave.description:
The Free Captains aren't picky employers and will take almost anyone they believe capable of following the Pirate Code. Most Free Captain ships carry a handful of fresh recruits each trip, some of whom will actually return for a second voyage. While usually relegated to the most demeaning and mundane jobs on board, these sailors take every opportunity to prove themselves to the rest of the crew once combat starts.

The Free Captains have been a scourge of interstellar shipping across the Pact Worlds for generations, but since the adoption of Drift Lanes, the outlaws have expanded their reach and scale by targeting ships across the galaxy using the new standardized interstellar shipping routes.

UWObj4d1vJHCtNQ8.description: A Free Captain knave's melee attacks gain the trip trait and @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.bestiary-ability-glossary-srd.Item.BCLvAx4Pz4MLa2pu]{Knockdown} ability against @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.AJh5ex99aV6VTggg]{Off-Guard} creatures.
UWObj4d1vJHCtNQ8.name: Blow the Man Down

Ywv2tkS4QqaDYnlW.description:
Trigger A creature within melee reach is hit by a ranged weapon or rolls a failure or critical failure against an area attack

Effect The Free Captain knave makes a melee Strike against the triggering creature.
Ywv2tkS4QqaDYnlW.name: Free Swing

l432s6vv0vYkuYqJ.description: Any creature that has the frightened condition is @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.AJh5ex99aV6VTggg]{Off-Guard} against the Free Captain knave's attacks.
l432s6vv0vYkuYqJ.name: Capitalize on Fear

Free Captain Knave.name: Free Captain Knave

Garaggakal.description:
Most garaggakals are around 8 feet tall, weighing 400 pounds, with a 20-foot wingspan. Always on the move, they might find a temporary lair on a broken starship or floating chunk of terrain but are soon off again, in search of a new creature to be their next meal. While one rarely encounters garaggakals in the Universe, it can happen, particularly if their temporary lair exits in the Drift.

The Drift is a strange place, and the creatures native to it are stranger still. Garaggakals prove no exception. Shaped vaguely like humanoids, they have arms and legs but also sallow, rubbery skin with long, scaly tails and gauzelike wings. Most horrifyingly, their faces are almost entirely taken up by their enormous, funnel-like mouth, lined with sharp teeth. While they use these mouths for the obvious purpose of biting, they can also use its powerful suction to draw actual life force from their prey.

Also known as "Drift wraiths," garaggakals hunt down any living creatures that linger too long in the Drift. For garaggakals, anything that isn't a fellow garaggakal is prey. However, they're no mere mindless hunters. Garaggakals are surprisingly intelligent and prefer to dissect victims, learning all about them before eating them. Often, garaggakals take their victims apart while they're still alive. Xenobiologists have determined that garaggakals don't even technically need to eat to survive, so their relentless hunger is seemingly psychological. They do require the energy of the Drift to survive in the absence of food, however, and further need the energy of the Drift to reproduce, seeking out areas of intense radiation to absorb and then build a new offspring from their own cells. Their children are fully grown at creation.

Garaggakals surprise their prey. They are quite stealthy and can even phase through solid matter, suddenly appearing on the inside of a starship—bad news for whatever living creatures happen to be inside. Con artists sell garaggakal repelling devices for travelers to use while in the Drift to prevent such visits.

8MfQP3Ag8pyj14uP.description: A creature that takes damage from a garaggakal's spit Strike must attempt a @Check[fortitude|dc:20] save. On a failure, it's @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.4D2KBtexWXa6oUMR]{Drained 1} (or @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.4D2KBtexWXa6oUMR]{Drained 2} on a critical failure).
8MfQP3Ag8pyj14uP.name: Draining Saliva

LUgsjx0QA0n5Dz1t.description:
Requirements A living creature within 30 feet of the garaggakal has the drained condition

Effect The garaggakal amplifies the drain on the required creature's essential life force, dealing @Damage[5d6[void]] damage (@Check[fortitude|dc:20|basic] save). The garaggakal gains temporary Hit Points equal to half the damage dealt that last 1 minute. Regardless of the result of the save, the garaggakal then Flies up to 15 feet closer to the required creature, and the required creature becomes temporarily immune to Leech Life for 24 hours.
LUgsjx0QA0n5Dz1t.name: Leech Life

VpqYdBDp2rPZb0Qe.description: The garaggakal senses all creatures that are under emotion effects as an imprecise sense at the listed range.
VpqYdBDp2rPZb0Qe.name: Emotion Sense

r3wLwM9pVsFu32OJ.description: The garaggakal's imprecise senses function through most materials and walls. The senses are blocked by energy fields (such as force fields and force effects) and sufficiently dense material: 10 feet of wood or plastic, 5 feet of stone, 1 foot of common metal, or 6 inches of lead or any starmetal.
r3wLwM9pVsFu32OJ.name: Sense Through

ufK1vEfwRqWHXQNk.description: A garaggakal can shift out of phase with reality and thus can't be held by walls or cages. The garaggakal moves through up to 15 feet of solid matter. They must end their turn outside of the solid matter or take @Damage[5d6[bludgeoning]] damage. A garaggakal can't phase through force effects.
ufK1vEfwRqWHXQNk.name: Phase Through

Garaggakal Polymath.description:
These garaggakals have lived for centuries and reached sizes greater than 15 feet tall and 1,000 pounds. Garaggakal polymaths have spent their many years tormenting and tearing apart all the creatures they've encountered, and they have extensive recollection of anatomy of a wide variety of living things. They're even crueler than younger garaggakals, taking great delight in causing excruciating pain to their victims before stealing their life force. They travel much further through the Drift than their younger counterparts, driven by their insatiable desire to find and dissect new creatures.

They do require the energy of the Drift to survive in the absence of food, however, and further need the energy of the Drift to reproduce, seeking out areas of intense radiation to absorb and then build a new offspring from their own cells. Effect The garaggakal uses their extensive knowledge of anatomy to dig into the wound, causing agonizing pain to the target. The garaggakal attempts a jaws Strike against the required creature, using the same multiple attack penalty as the previous Strike. On a hit, the target is also @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.fesd1n5eVhpCSS18]{Sickened 1} (or @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.fesd1n5eVhpCSS18]{Sickened 2} on a critical hit).
