Glass Serpent.description:
The great glass serpents of the barren planet of Eox are one of the Pact Worlds' most notorious apex predators. With an average length of almost 60 feet and a weight of about 5,000 pounds, the size and grace of glass serpents are only part of what makes them such efficient killers. Thanks to an innate invisibility provided by their unique scales, glass serpents remain outside of the visual spectrum of most creatures, allowing them to silently approach unsuspecting prey. Having evolved through Eox's numerous cataclysms, these serpents find sustenance from the rare bands of living creatures who visit the world, and in an odd turn, while they're consuming the living is when glass serpents are at their most vulnerable. The combination of acids and digestive fluids used in consuming a living creature also deprives the serpents of their invisibility, and canny glass serpent hunters actively tempt their quarry with animals to consume before attacking in force.

Glass serpents have made their way well beyond the confines of Eox, and some have even found an accepting ecosystem in the Diaspora's strange waterway, the River Between. The local sarcesians blame Eox for intentionally polluting their waterways with predators, though Eox denies all accusations of intentional meddling. Such debates have only intensified since the Diaspora was granted provisional Pact World status under the sarcesians' stewardship.

1GNbrbSYPpOG1Dqf.description:
Requirements The glass serpent's last action was a successful tail whip Strike

Effect The creature the glass serpent hit is @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.DmAIPqOBomZ7H95W]{Concealed} from all creatures except the glass serpent until that creature moves out of the glass serpent's reach or until the start of the glass serpent's next turn.
1GNbrbSYPpOG1Dqf.name: Concealing Coil

ADo0WO3FwECDw7oR.description: The glass serpent is naturally invisible. When a glass serpent takes a hostile action of any kind, it is hidden instead of undetected until the start of its next turn, as parts of its body become momentarily tangible. A glass serpent that has swallowed a creature becomes visible for the next day as its meal is being digested. If the swallowed creature escapes or is otherwise removed, the glass serpent immediately returns to being invisible.
ADo0WO3FwECDw7oR.name: Ravenous Invisibility

DVuH2SVNP0ZrlitJ.description:
Trigger A creature passes within 20 feet of the glass serpent and hasn't detected it

Effect The glass serpent lunges out of hiding. It Strides directly toward the triggering creature and makes a jaws Strike against it. The target creature is @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.AJh5ex99aV6VTggg]{Off-Guard} to this attack.
DVuH2SVNP0ZrlitJ.name: Ambush

Glass Serpent.name: Glass Serpent

Gnackle.description:
Many poor souls who encounter a gnackle don't realize until it's too late. These gremlins relish watching other creatures suffer humiliating failure and often spend weeks or longer selecting and grooming a victim into bringing out their own downfall. After reading their target's mind to learn what they want most, gnackles then magically disguise themselves, presenting to their target as a fairy godmother or similar granter of wishes and convincing their victims of some great destiny. They offer a magical "gift" and encourage the target toward acts of greater and greater ambition. However, once gnackles deem their victims in a suitably embarrassing or dangerous situation, they twist the gift into a terrible curse.

Gremlins have plagued the Universe with cruel tricks since long before the Gap, and they've fully adapted to a galaxy filled with technology. Whether meddling with a comm unit, a starship, or an entire space station, gremlins delight in ruination and chaos.

gCBofQcc17WnXjPJ.description:
A gnackle can imbue a willing creature with a magical gift of talent for 24 hours, imparting a +2 status bonus to checks with a specific skill, chosen when this ability is used. The gnackle always knows when the creature attempts checks with the chosen skill and, at any time, can choose to invert the gift to instead immediately impart a –4 status penalty to all checks attempted with that skill for 1 minute, after which the creature is no longer affected by this ability.

@UUID[Compendium.sf2e.bestiary-effects.Item.1uk1rvqSP0S2HfVG]{Effect: Gremlin's Gift}

@UUID[Compendium.sf2e.bestiary-effects.Item.LdbqPPiSg5gn5Kqp]{Effect: Gremlin's Inverted Gift}
gCBofQcc17WnXjPJ.name: Gremlin's Gift

v3mW5tciW4Q6n8PI.description: 30 feet. Non-gremlin creatures that enter the aura must attempt a @Check[will|dc:18] save. On a failure, the creature gains a +1 status bonus to attack rolls and skill checks while in the aura, but if it misses an attack roll or fails a skill check while in the aura, it loses that bonus and instead takes a –2 status penalty to all attack rolls and skill checks for 1 minute. After 1 minute has elapsed, or if a creature succeeds at its save, the creature becomes temporarily immune to that gnackle's aura for 24 hours.
v3mW5tciW4Q6n8PI.name: False Confidence Aura

Gnackle.name: Gnackle

Gubbin.description:
Gubbins—also known as data gremlins—are spontaneously born from corrupted data, especially as a result of errors in artificial intelligence programs. While gubbins aren't particularly powerful, they're notoriously hard to hit due to the way their bodies flicker and jolt through space as if slightly out of sync with the rest of the world. Gubbins are most easily set apart from other gremlins by their fingers, which vary in number from moment to moment and sprout from illogical locations on their hands, such as the backs or palms. While lacking in fine mobility, their warped hands are disturbing to observe in motion, a fact they delightfully use to their advantage.

Due to being weaponized in corporate espionage efforts and later multiplying out of control, gubbins are one of the most ubiquitous types of gremlin on heavily computerized planets. While not as malevolent as other gremlins, gubbins delight in irrevocably corrupting computer data, which they do for their own amusement as well as to create more gubbins. Gubbins are often found where large amounts of data are stored, accompanied by corrupted technological constructs such as hardlight life-forms or robots.

Gremlins have plagued the Universe with cruel tricks since long before the Gap, and they've fully adapted to a galaxy filled with technology. Whether meddling with a comm unit, a starship, or an entire space station, gremlins delight in ruination and chaos.

7TlxPjLrlROi4iKw.description: Gubbins can spread their glitchiness to others. Creatures damaged by the gubbin's claw or glitchy beam Strikes must succeed at a @Check[fortitude|dc:17] save or become @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.fesd1n5eVhpCSS18]{Sickened 1} (@UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.fesd1n5eVhpCSS18]{Sickened 2} on a critical hit). If the target has the tech trait, it becomes glitching instead of sickened.
7TlxPjLrlROi4iKw.name: Scramble

J3OsW8fLW5IATM8F.description:
You delete data from a device or object with a flamboyant magical gesture. This data might be handwritten, printed, or digital. You delete up to 1,500 words' worth of text, one page of content, or one display screen worth of text or other visual information. Non-magical writing in or on an unattended or held object is automatically deleted. Attempt a counteract check to delete digital or magical writing. If you fail to delete writing that's part of a hazard, you trigger the hazard. This can't be used to delete the contents of a spellbook or similar means of storing magical formulas or spells.

If you target an attended tech item with the tracking trait, attempt a counteract check. On a success, the item becomes glitching 1. A creature holding the item can Interact to restart the software, reducing the glitching value by 1.

Heightened (7th) You can delete all the data stored locally on a single device or book, or all the data on a device or book related to a specific name, topic, or category.
J3OsW8fLW5IATM8F.name: Delete (at will)

qAWBwvDaBKGuSLWV.description:
Trigger A creature targets the gubbin with an attack or area effect, and the gubbin is aware of the attacker

Effect The gubbin teleports 10 feet. If this puts the gubbin out of the range or area of the attack, the attack misses. If not, the gubbin gains a +2 circumstance bonus to AC and Reflex saves against the attack.
qAWBwvDaBKGuSLWV.name: Not Really There

rH9r1JoFstg0qvtF.description: 20 feet. A non-gremlin creature that enters the aura must succeed at a @Check[will|dc:17] save or become @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 1} (or @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 2} on a critical failure) and is then temporarily immune to unsettling appearance for 1 minute. If the gubbin used any action with the manipulate trait, an Interact action, or a claw Strike since the start of their last turn, creatures take a –4 status penalty to their saves against this effect.
rH9r1JoFstg0qvtF.name: Unsettling Appearance

Gubbin.name: Gubbin

Gwereiad.description:
Gwereiads are aloof and enigmatic nymphs who keep to themselves, nestling deep inside the phenomena known as black holes. Whether their solitary nature is an active preference or simply a consequence of their homes is up for debate, as few creatures can brave the gravitational forces of a black hole long enough to make contact with gwereiads. They're rarely hostile unless provoked and occasionally even rescue starships at risk of being devoured by their homes.

Gwereiads adore art and music, though their tastes tend toward the strange and avant-garde. While most nymphs aren't overtly religious, gwereiads devote themselves to esoteric spirituality focused on space-time.

Nymphs are beautiful fey who appear as humanoids with elven features. They generally take female forms, but nymphs of all genders and presentations exist. While many nymphs live on planets and act as protectors of natural ponds, forests, caves, and cliffsides, other nymphs—often called space nymphs—are known for their association with celestial bodies. Like their planet-bound kin, space nymphs guard their bonded territories from exploitation or harm.

As admirers of the arts, nymphs are especially friendly toward creatives, and offering to depict a nymph in story, picture, or song is a sure way to win their favor—unless the nymph doesn't like the final result and lashes out at the artist for insulting them with a mediocre product. Vidcasting and livestreaming are popular pastimes among more sociable nymphs, whether to show off their remote environments or find audiences for performances. Some nymphs entice movie crews to film in their territories, with two provisos: first, that the production not damage the environment, and second, that the nymph receive a prominent role in the film.

Unless their territories are threatened, most space nymphs are friendly or indifferent to mortals, but they have long memories. Anyone visiting a space nymph's territory would be wise to research that nymph's grudges, past encounters with mortals, or any recent events in the area that might color the nymph's perspective of those traveling near their home.

A mortal who demonstrates the right attitude and abilities, such as by protecting a stellar body from destruction or creating an especially beautiful work of art, might draw a space nymph's attention. From time to time, space nymphs will offer their services as mentors to solarians or mystics, though they seldom seek pupils on their own. Space nymphs rarely enter into more than one such arrangement at a time and typically only make commitments that promise to last decades or centuries, so they're extremely selective in their choice of mentee.

FpJNCPwS9CJl5YUb.description:
The gwereiad summons a gravitational collapse around a creature within 30 feet, dealing @Damage[6d6[bludgeoning]] damage. The affected creature must attempt a @Check[fortitude|dc:29] save.

Critical Success The creature is unaffected.

Success The creature's body crumples under the gravity, and it takes half damage.

Failure The creature takes full damage and is @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.eIcWbB5o3pP6OIMe]{Immobilized} by the gravitational collapse. It takes @Damage[2d6[persistent,bludgeoning]] damage until it [[/act escape dc=29]]{Escapes}.

Critical Failure As failure, but the creature takes double damage and the persistent damage is 4d6.
FpJNCPwS9CJl5YUb.name: Gravitic Crush

Uiipad3fyQ9dcPCk.description: 30 feet. The area around a gwereiad inexorably draws things toward its center. Creatures entering or starting their turns inside the aura must succeed at a @Check[reflex|dc:29] save or be pulled 5 feet toward the gwereiad (10 feet on a critical failure).
Uiipad3fyQ9dcPCk.name: Singularity Field

bh40NA5UrV45vCHu.description: A gwereiad is mystically bonded to a single black hole. If they're away from their bonded black hole for more than 24 hours, they become @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.4D2KBtexWXa6oUMR]{Drained 1} and must succeed at a @Check[fortitude|dc:29] save each additional 24 hours or increase their drained value by 1. A gwereiad can perform a 24-hour ritual to bond themself to a new black hole.
bh40NA5UrV45vCHu.name: Black Hole-Dependent

qIzCfjW9FXxHe2VN.description: While on their bonded celestial body, a nymph can sense approaching starships within a day's travel from the celestial body. This doesn't give them any information about the ship, its occupants, or its exact position. The nymph can send a message to the ship as if using a personal comm unit.
qIzCfjW9FXxHe2VN.name: Sense Transponder

wQy9ojr4tNVUfWrC.description: You alter gravity's effects on you. You treat gravity as if it were your choice of one step higher or lower (for example, if you were in an area of low gravity, you could choose either standard gravity or zero-g). While the spell is active, you reduce the distance of any forced movement that would affect you by 5 feet (minimum 0 feet), and you ignore being clumsy and untethered because of gravity effects on you. You can Dismiss the spell.
wQy9ojr4tNVUfWrC.name: Personal Gravity (Constant)

Gwereiad.name: Gwereiad

Gwereiad Queen.description:
The rarest of nymphs, gwereiad queens form within supermassive black holes, either from a weaker gwereiad's ascension or created spontaneously amid the black hole's powerful energies. They tend to be even more detached than the typical gwereiad, speaking only in peculiar metaphors blending science and mysticism.

Nymphs are beautiful fey who appear as humanoids with elven features. They generally take female forms, but nymphs of all genders and presentations exist. While many nymphs live on planets and act as protectors of natural ponds, forests, caves, and cliffsides, other nymphs—often called space nymphs—are known for their association with celestial bodies. Like their planet-bound kin, space nymphs guard their bonded territories from exploitation or harm.

As admirers of the arts, nymphs are especially friendly toward creatives, and offering to depict a nymph in story, picture, or song is a sure way to win their favor—unless the nymph doesn't like the final result and lashes out at the artist for insulting them with a mediocre product. Vidcasting and livestreaming are popular pastimes among more sociable nymphs, whether to show off their remote environments or find audiences for performances. Some nymphs entice movie crews to film in their territories, with two provisos: first, that the production not damage the environment, and second, that the nymph receive a prominent role in the film.

Unless their territories are threatened, most space nymphs are friendly or indifferent to mortals, but they have long memories. Anyone visiting a space nymph's territory would be wise to research that nymph's grudges, past encounters with mortals, or any recent events in the area that might color the nymph's perspective of those traveling near their home.

A mortal who demonstrates the right attitude and abilities, such as by protecting a stellar body from destruction or creating an especially beautiful work of art, might draw a space nymph's attention. From time to time, space nymphs will offer their services as mentors to solarians or mystics, though they seldom seek pupils on their own. Space nymphs rarely enter into more than one such arrangement at a time and typically only make commitments that promise to last decades or centuries, so they're extremely selective in their choice of mentee.

3Q5AfLoYI4g0KrPk.description:
A nymph queen can inspire a single intelligent creature by sending them a motivational video or text message. As long as the creature keeps the message saved and remains in good standing with the nymph queen, they gain a +1 status bonus to all Crafting, Performance, and Lore checks related to art or performance.

As a 1-action Interact action, the creature can play or view the message to bolster their spirits. Doing so allows the creature to attempt a [[/r 1d20+26 #Counteract]] counteract check against a single emotion effect affecting them.

When the nymph queen's message is used in this way, it becomes a mundane video or text afterward.
3Q5AfLoYI4g0KrPk.name: Fan Mail

Em1L3vIGiBRawgLG.description: Nymph queens can transform between their original form, which looks much like a typical nymph of their kind, and any Small or Medium humanoid form, typically choosing a version of their natural form with the appearance of the chosen species.
Em1L3vIGiBRawgLG.name: Change Shape

bfrXuZFAFF95bnwg.description: A nymph queen can traverse her celestial body near-instantaneously. A nymph queen can use Celestial Step to teleport to any area on or within her territory, vanishing into its surface and reemerging at her intended destination.
bfrXuZFAFF95bnwg.name: Celestial Step

eqBRDqwFrMrEskH6.description:
The gwereiad summons a gravitational collapse around a creature within 30 feet, dealing @Damage[5d12[bludgeoning]] damage. The affected creature must attempt a @Check[fortitude|dc:40] save.

Critical Success The creature is unaffected.

Success The creature's body crumples under the gravity, and it takes half damage.

Failure The creature takes full damage and is @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.eIcWbB5o3pP6OIMe]{Immobilized} by the gravitational collapse. It takes @Damage[2d6[persistent,bludgeoning]] damage until it [[/act escape dc=40]]{Escapes}.

Critical Failure As failure, but the creature takes double damage and the persistent damage is 4d6.
eqBRDqwFrMrEskH6.name: Gravitic Crush

mPnMtydRl5BnfXrE.description:
The nymph queen magically superimposes her image on all technological items capable of displaying it, such as datapads or comm units, within planetary range. Alternatively, she can send this image to any comm address or addresses that she knows.

Each creature that can see the image must succeed at a @Check[will|dc:40] or have their attitude toward her improve by one step (two steps on a critical failure).

Affected creatures' attitudes revert to their previous level if the nymph queen uses a hostile action against them or their allies.
mPnMtydRl5BnfXrE.name: Broadcast Allure

sJfeR4Txvzzba4Ux.description:
A nymph queen is intrinsically tied to a specific celestial body, such as a supergiant star for a heliad queen.

As long as the queen is healthy, her territory thrives, and she can attempt to [[/r 1d20+32 #Counteract]] counteract spells and rituals that alter its physical properties with a counteract rank of 10.

If a nymph queen is injured or unhealthy, however, her celestial body also weakens: asteroids wobble out of orbit, stars dim, and the gravity of black holes diminishes. Restoring the nymph queen returns her celestial body to its equilibrium.
sJfeR4Txvzzba4Ux.name: Astronomical Ties

yIMu1ZyoStZPETE7.description:
A globe of freezing darkness explodes in the area, dealing 8d10 cold damage to creatures in the area, plus an additional 8d4 void damage to living creatures. Each creature in the area must attempt a Reflex save.

If the globe overlaps with an area of magical light or affects a creature affected by magical light, eclipse burst attempts to counteract the light effect.

Critical Success The creature is unaffected.

Success The creature takes half damage.

Failure The creature takes full damage.

Critical Failure The creature takes double damage and becomes @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.XgEqL1kFApUbl5Z2]{Blinded} by the darkness for an unlimited duration.

Heightened (+1) The cold damage increases by 1d10 and the void damage against the living increases by 1d4.
yIMu1ZyoStZPETE7.name: Eclipse Burst

Gwereiad Queen.name: Gwereiad Queen

Haeshi-Shaa (Haeshi Form).description:
A haeshi-shaa in their haeshi form is aggressive and persistent, unlikely to back down from an argument or a fight unless their life is in danger. While aggressive, haeshis are far from foolish; they prepare carefully for any encounter and often have dozens of nested contingencies to fall back on should any situation evolve beyond their control.

Haeshi-shaas are relatively new members of the Dominion of the Black. These long-lived creatures shift unpredictably between a liquid and a gaseous form in a mysterious cycle that lasts their entire lives. In their liquid haeshi form, they're a churning, chunky fluid, while in their vaporous shaa form, they're more akin to hazy brown fog. Regardless of their form, they hum with atonal harmonies that cause great discomfort in others.

Haeshi-shaas serve as a sort of priest caste for the Dominion of the Black, each form preaching a doctrine of entropy and annihilation, though with slightly different nuances between each form. Haeshis tend toward assertive, aggressive practices, while shaas are meditative, often spending many months or years in contemplation. Haeshi-shaas believe that the most perfect and divine state of any object or being is complete separation into its most basic, individual particles. They claim (dubiously) that they can see, even predict, the journey of all things as they travel toward this ultimate entropic end.

In truth, haeshi-shaas can't even predict when they'll shift into their alternate form. Some have tried to catalyze the change by seeking out specific types of life experience or knowledge, but despite the many claims to the contrary, there are no verified instances of a haeshi-shaa forcing the change. Most choose to simply await their next transformation, during which time they have many centuries to spread the Dominion's disturbing doctrines and pursue their inscrutable agendas.

7FNjUjp4jHxdhAV4.description: A haeshi can move through a gap at least 2 feet wide without Squeezing and can Squeeze through a gap at least 1 foot wide.
7FNjUjp4jHxdhAV4.name: Compression

JIKYqGjjxpvxslsi.description:
Saving Throw @Check[fortitude|dc:32]

Stage 1 carrier (1 day)

Stage 2 the creature becomes partially vaporous and treats all other creatures as @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.DmAIPqOBomZ7H95W]{Concealed} (1 day)

Stage 3 the creature is incorporeal and @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.fBnFDH2MTzgFijKf]{Unconscious} (1 day)

Stage 4 the creature dies, and its body dissipates into fine particles
JIKYqGjjxpvxslsi.name: Viral Vapor

U19URI7ZSi7OKpcB.description:
You fire a shard of solidified magic toward a creature that you can see. It automatically hits and deals 1d4+1 force damage. For each additional action you use when Casting the Spell, increase the number of shards you shoot by one, to a maximum of three shards for 3 actions. You choose the target for each shard individually. If you shoot more than one shard at the same target, combine the damage before applying bonuses or penalties to damage, resistances, weaknesses, and so forth.

Heightened (+2) You fire one additional shard with each action you spend.
U19URI7ZSi7OKpcB.name: Force Barrage (at will)

c260f1dgR0yU9hFH.description: When killed, a haeshi explodes in a wave of psychic energy, dealing @Damage[13d6[mental]|options:area-damage] damage to all creatures in a @Template[type:burst|distance:20] (@Check[will|dc:29|basic] save).
c260f1dgR0yU9hFH.name: Frenetic Death

hCyAd6Cn6N4I5EAC.name: +1 Status to All Saves vs. Magic

QAV7aK1PSQ8v040L.description: The shaa agitates their molecules and becomes semitransparent and virtually impenetrable for 1 minute. In this form, the shaa isn't incorporeal, gains resistance 25 to all damage, and gains 150 temporary Hit Points for 1 minute. They can take no actions and are immovable. The shaa reverts to their natural form at the end of the duration.
QAV7aK1PSQ8v040L.name: Thicken

gChixndA8SOlM5KO.name: +1 Status to All Saves vs. Magic

hyAu17FEMDtJteGR.description:
You plant fear in the target; it must attempt a Will save.

Critical Success The target is unaffected.

Success The target is @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 1}.

Failure The target is @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 2}.

Critical Failure The target is @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 3} and @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.sDPxOjQ9kx2RZE8D]{Fleeing} for 1 round.

Heightened (3rd) You can target up to five creatures.
hyAu17FEMDtJteGR.name: Fear (at will)

jpODDybpYqSH4erj.description:
You cast your thoughts through a creature's mind, sifting for information. You access the target's memories and knowledge unless it fends you off with a Will save.

Success The target is unaffected.

Failure Each round of the spell's duration, you can Sustain the spell to ask a different question and attempt to uncover the answer. For each question, the target can attempt a Deception check against your spell DC; if the target succeeds, you don't learn the answer, and on a critical success, the target gives you a false answer that you believe is truthful Once you've asked the target a given question, asking it again, even with a separate casting of mind probe, produces the same result.

Critical Failure As failure, and the target takes a –4 circumstance penalty to Deception checks against your questions.
jpODDybpYqSH4erj.name: Mind Probe (at will)

kxH6Bx5LuZMx4ima.description: The shaa spreads their matter thin, becoming Gargantuan and gaining a space and reach of 20 feet. The shaa can take only purely mental actions or use Thicken while in this state. A shaa can return to their normal size by spending a single action, which has the concentrate trait.
kxH6Bx5LuZMx4ima.name: Expand

Haeshi-Shaa (Shaa Form).name: Haeshi-Shaa (Shaa Form)

Hardlight Havoc.description:
This hardlight life-form is unstable, displaying stuck frames and erratic movements.

Unlike normal holograms, hardlight life-forms are tangible, living entities.

A hardlight life-form reduced to 0 HP vanishes, though its projector reconstructs it in [[/gmr 1d4 #hours]]{1d4 hours}. The only way to permanently destroy a hardlight life-form is to find its projector and either repair or destroy it.

Change Character The hardlight havoc regains @Damage[2d8[healing]|options:area-damage] Hit Points.

Pixelation The hardlight havoc is @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.DmAIPqOBomZ7H95W]{Concealed} from all creatures.

Power Leak The hardlight havoc is @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.dfCMdR4wnpbYNTix]{Stunned 1}. At the end of its turn, it deals @Damage[4d6[electricity]|options:area-damage] damage to creatures in a @Template[type:emanation|distance:10] (@Check[reflex|dc:22|basic] save).

Surge The hardlight havoc is @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.nlCjDvLMf2EkV2dl]{Quickened} until the end of its turn and can use the extra action to Stride or Strike.
cognXh33XPilRvjB.name: Error State

dXeXugw7BwsAa5Jl.description: The hardlight havoc teleports up to 40 feet. If the destination is within melee reach of an enemy, it can make a melee Strike against that enemy. If it teleports to a square without a surface to stand on, it falls after attempting a Strike and takes no damage from falling.
dXeXugw7BwsAa5Jl.name: Flicker

Hardlight Havoc.name: Hardlight Havoc

733vwV9zYuaN0Y9w.description: The hardlight mascot can make a special Leap up to 15 feet vertically and up to 20 feet horizontally without a check.
733vwV9zYuaN0Y9w.name: Arcade Leap

BQ5k6rieS1WyDPdy.description: The hardlight mascot sings a jingle to a creature within 60 feet, dealing @Damage[4d6[mental]] damage (@Check[will|dc:19|basic] save).
BQ5k6rieS1WyDPdy.name: Taunt

I5EEmXduat96ZQrL.description: The hardlight mascot Leaps adjacent to a Medium or smaller creature, then makes a kick Strike against it. I5EEmXduat96ZQrL.name: Stomp

Hardlight Scamp.description:
These creatures typically resemble the ad or media they were born from, though they often also resemble bat-like elemental scamps, thus earning their name.

Unlike normal holograms, hardlight life-forms are tangible, living entities.

PLJ2sk0qq5ZffBIn.description: The hardlight scamp holds perfectly still so it appears as a normal hologram and becomes hidden. A hardlight scamp can Freeze even while being observed and counts as being @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.DmAIPqOBomZ7H95W]{Concealed}.
PLJ2sk0qq5ZffBIn.name: Freeze

yhioblIlvX9bT33j.description: The hardlight scamp shoots sparks at a creature within 60 feet. The target must succeed at a @Check[fortitude|dc:17] save or be @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.TkIyaNPgTZFBCCuh]{Dazzled} for 1 round (1 minute on a critical failure).
yhioblIlvX9bT33j.name: Holospark

a4VbrboOsQ6TB5M6.name: Virtual Roadblocks

Anyone visiting a space nymph's territory would be wise to research that nymph's grudges, past encounters with mortals, or any recent events in the area that might color the nymph's perspective of those traveling near their home.

A mortal who demonstrates the right attitude and abilities, such as by protecting a stellar body from destruction or creating an especially beautiful work of art, might draw a space nymph's attention. From time to time, space nymphs will offer their services as mentors to solarians or mystics, though they seldom seek pupils on their own. Space nymphs rarely enter into more than one such arrangement at a time and typically only make commitments that promise to last decades or centuries, so they're extremely selective in their choice of mentee.

PDkHtAiJ6LpAnwQu.description: A nymph queen can traverse her celestial body near-instantaneously. A nymph queen can use Celestial Step to teleport to any area on or within her territory, vanishing into its surface and reemerging at her intended destination.
PDkHtAiJ6LpAnwQu.name: Celestial Step

ZbpDAxnEsIOCAtez.description: While on their bonded celestial body, a nymph can sense approaching starships within a day's travel from the celestial body. This doesn't give them any information about the ship, its occupants, or its exact position. The nymph can send a message to the ship as if using a personal comm unit.
ZbpDAxnEsIOCAtez.name: Sense Transponder

aNtEgRACAiCNHXVu.description:
A nymph queen is intrinsically tied to a specific celestial body, such as a supergiant star for a heliad queen.

As long as the queen is healthy, her territory thrives, and she can attempt to [[/r 1d20+26 #Counteract]] counteract spells and rituals that alter its physical properties with a counteract rank of 7.

If a nymph queen is injured or unhealthy, however, her celestial body also weakens: asteroids wobble out of orbit, stars dim, and the gravity of black holes diminishes. Restoring the nymph queen returns her celestial body to its equilibrium.
aNtEgRACAiCNHXVu.name: Astronomical Ties

dKrmnxMOcFSnyKjK.description:
60 feet. A heliad's eyes blaze like a sun. When a creature enters or starts its turn in the aura, it must attempt a @Check[fortitude|dc:34] save. The heliad can deactivate or activate this aura by using a single action, which has the concentrate trait.

Success The creature is unaffected.

Failure The creature is @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.TkIyaNPgTZFBCCuh]{Dazzled} until the start of its next turn.

Critical Failure The creature is @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.XgEqL1kFApUbl5Z2]{Blinded} until the start of its next turn.
dKrmnxMOcFSnyKjK.name: Radiant Gaze

ii7zqpYP6kwHPsVa.description: Nymph queens can transform between their original form, which looks much like a typical nymph of their kind, and any Small or Medium humanoid form, typically choosing a version of their natural form with the appearance of the chosen species.
ii7zqpYP6kwHPsVa.name: Change Shape

pvcJnlNSkZsiCA5N.description:
The nymph queen magically superimposes her image on all technological items capable of displaying it, such as datapads or comm units, within planetary range. Alternatively, she can send this image to any comm address or addresses that she knows.

Each creature that can see the image must succeed at a @Check[will|dc:34] or have their attitude toward her improve by one step (two steps on a critical failure).

Affected creatures' attitudes revert to their previous level if the nymph queen uses a hostile action against them or their allies.
pvcJnlNSkZsiCA5N.name: Broadcast Allure

pwsz6NnCv8buuxKC.description:
A nymph queen can inspire a single intelligent creature by sending them a motivational video or text message. As long as the creature keeps the message saved and remains in good standing with the nymph queen, they gain a +1 status bonus to all Crafting, Performance, and Lore checks related to art or performance.

As a 1-action Interact action, the creature can play or view the message to bolster their spirits. Doing so allows the creature to attempt a [[/r 1d20+26 #Counteract]] counteract check against a single emotion effect affecting them.

When the nymph queen's message is used in this way, it becomes a mundane video or text afterward.
pwsz6NnCv8buuxKC.name: Fan Mail

qU2eXzHQlXr9NPQd.description:
Trigger The heliad queen dies

Effect The heliad's body explodes into brilliant, luminous flame. Each creature in a @Template[type:emanation|distance:10] takes @Damage[12d8[fire]|options:area-damage] damage (@Check[reflex|dc:34|basic] save). Creatures that critically fail are @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.XgEqL1kFApUbl5Z2]{Blinded} for 1 minute.
qU2eXzHQlXr9NPQd.name: Supernova

Heliad Queen.name: Heliad Queen

Hellknight Armiger.description:
Hellknight armigers are the lowest-ranked Hellknights, though attaining this rank requires them to spend six years as an initiate and then pass the Hellknight Test, during which they must summon, combat, and defeat a fiend of Hell.

Hellknights are infernal knights, and while they once ruled entire nations on Lost Golarion, the Hellknights of the Pact Worlds enforce law and order more holistically, traveling in massive citadel starships to spread their influence rather than remaining in any one place. In battle, Hellknights are orderly, unrelenting, and deadly.

hDm1f5ddw7r1E9Yf.description: You have four arms, which allows you to wield and hold up to four hands' worth of weapons and equipment. At any time, one pair of hands is designated as your active hands. You can change this designation from one pair of hands to another by taking the Switch Hands action, which is a single action. You can wield items only with your active hands.
hDm1f5ddw7r1E9Yf.name: Four-Armed

hUnTlogdAD8zA7aL.description:
Trigger The armiger takes fire damage

Effect The armiger absorbs a fraction of the fire to empower their attacks. Until the end of their next turn, their Strikes deal an additional @Damage[1d6[fire]] damage.
hUnTlogdAD8zA7aL.name: Forged in Hellfire

hX1ZJpFiodBORSA0.description: The armiger draws two grenades, then Area Fires both grenades. Creatures in the area of both grenades take a –1 circumstance penalty to their saving throws against both grenades.
hX1ZJpFiodBORSA0.name: Rapid Bombardment

Hellknight Armiger.name: Hellknight Armiger

Hellknight Degradant.description:
Hellknights most often study the forces of Hell to inspire their fighting styles and magic, but they might also learn to attune to the forces of the cosmos to become solarians.

Hellknights are infernal knights, and while they once ruled entire nations on Lost Golarion, the Hellknights of the Pact Worlds enforce law and order more holistically, traveling in massive citadel starships to spread their influence rather than remaining in any one place. In battle, Hellknights are orderly, unrelenting, and deadly.

DDfzxUupGvhC59pZ.description: A degradant wields a solar glaive formed of solidified gravitons. They can conjure and dismiss this weapon as a single action that has the concentrate trait. Whenever they successfully Strike a creature using their graviton glaive, the creature treats all squares adjacent to the square in which it was struck as difficult terrain until the end of the creature's next turn.
DDfzxUupGvhC59pZ.name: Graviton Glaive

ZVgajmKaVG73XBTM.description: The degradant uses gravity to crush an enemy within 100 feet, dealing @Damage[4d6[bludgeoning]] damage (@Check[fortitude|dc:26|basic] save); on a critical failure, the creature takes an additional @Damage[1d6[persistent,bleed]] damage.
ZVgajmKaVG73XBTM.name: Crush

fvCCAdEqWNrnOHG2.description:
The degradant deals @Damage[9d6[bludgeoning]] damage to each enemy creature within 30 feet with a @Check[fortitude|dc:26] save. The degradant can't use Black Hole again for [[/gmr 1d4 #Recharge Black Hole]]{1d4 rounds}.

Critical Success The creature is unaffected.

Success The creature takes half damage and is pulled 5 feet toward the degradant.

Failure The creature takes full damage and is pulled 10 feet toward the degradant.

Critical Failure The creature takes double damage, is pulled 30 feet toward the degradant, and is knocked @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.j91X7x0XSomq8d60]{Prone}.
fvCCAdEqWNrnOHG2.name: Black Hole

j0XKbPXtZEzbSDZR.description: The degradant Strides twice, gaining a +10-foot circumstance bonus to their Speed during these moves. When they complete these Strides, all enemies within 15 feet of the degradant are pulled 15 feet closer to the degradant unless they succeed at a @Check[fortitude|dc:26] save.
j0XKbPXtZEzbSDZR.name: Stellar Rush

Hellknight Degradant.name: Hellknight Degradant

Hellknight Signifer.description:
A Hellknight who displays prowess, scholarly discipline, and magical acumen might attain the rank of signifer.

Hellknights are infernal knights, and while they once ruled entire nations on Lost Golarion, the Hellknights of the Pact Worlds enforce law and order more holistically, traveling in massive citadel starships to spread their influence rather than remaining in any one place. In battle, Hellknights are orderly, unrelenting, and deadly.

SZ0CK5fqJfCQAYAQ.description:
You make an appeal to a powerful devil, asking them to bind some of their subordinates to your service. If you succeed, the devil sends you their choice of one devil of level 2 or lower, two devils of level 0 or lower, or three devils of level –1 or lower.

Critical Success The devils are sent to you and serve you for [[/gmr 1d4 #Weeks]]{1d4 weeks}.

Success The devils are sent to you and serve you for [[/gmr 1d4 #Days]]{1d4 days}.

Failure Your request is denied.

Critical Failure Not only is your request denied, but the powerful devil sends word of its displeasure to your master.

Heightened (+1) Increase the level of devil sent to you by 2 for each option.
SZ0CK5fqJfCQAYAQ.name: Diabolic Pact (DC 22, Doesn't Require Secondary Casters)

fhbAiWGpDfd8fOhE.description: 10 feet. Magical wards cause a signifer's surrounding foes to catch flame. An enemy creature that starts its turn in the area must succeed at a @Check[fortitude|dc:19] save or take @Damage[1d4[persistent,fire]] damage. A signifer can activate and deactivate this aura as a single action that has the concentrate trait. Regardless of the result of the save, the creature is immune to the aura for 1 minute.
fhbAiWGpDfd8fOhE.name: Burn the Unworthy

lGpoPTGxcGtUiwNn.description:
Frequency once per round

Effect The signifer accuses a target within 60 feet of misdeeds, then attempts an Intimidation check to [[/act demoralize]] them. As long as the target is frightened due to Proclamation of Guilt, it's also @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.enA7BxAjBb7ns1iF]{Suppressed}.
lGpoPTGxcGtUiwNn.name: Proclamation of Guilt

usbkdFRjmHA7dqdo.description: If the next action the signifer uses is to Cast a Spell that has a range, increase that spell's range by 30 feet.
usbkdFRjmHA7dqdo.name: Reach Spell

Hellknight Signifer.name: Hellknight Signifer

Hesper.description: These nuclear fey make their homes in reactors and embody the rapidly changing nature of their radioactive homes. They shift colors to reflect their moods, which can sometimes be used to predict their dangerous bouts of boredom. Hespers never intend malice, but they rarely consider the consequences of their actions.

TLohaBo6PxqfdIN5.description:
A hesper can deliver an enormous, mutating dose of radiation with a touch. Creatures struck by a hesper's fist Strike must attempt a @Check[fortitude|dc:18] save. On a failure, the creature gains a random mutation from the table below for 1 hour (or 24 hours on a critical failure).

[[/r 1d8]]Mutation
1Extra eyes: Target is dazzled in bright light and gains a +2 status bonus to sight-based Perception checks.
2Bioelectric cells: Tech items held by the target regain all spent charges at the end of the creature's turn. Tech items are glitching 1 for as long as the target holds them. If the target is a creature with the tech trait, it becomes glitching 1, and its melee Strikes deal an additional @Damage[1d6[electricity]] damage.
3Spikes: Target gains an unarmed melee attack that deals @Damage[1d4[piercing]] damage. It takes a –2 status penalty to attack rolls with two-handed weapons.
4Glowing Tumors: Target sheds light as a flashlight and takes a –2 status penalty to Stealth checks.
5Gills: Target gains the amphibious trait and takes a –1 status penalty to Fortitude saves.
6Musk gland: Target gains a 30-foot stench aura with a DC equal to their class DC.
7Protective growths: Target gains a +1 status bonus to AC and takes a –2 status penalty to Dexterity-based checks.
8Cellular alteration: The target is @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.fesd1n5eVhpCSS18]{Sickened} for the duration and gains @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.bestiary-ability-glossary-srd.Item.fJSNOw4zHGbIm4bZ]{Fast Healing} with a value equal to half its level (rounded up).
TLohaBo6PxqfdIN5.name: Mutating Touch

hknftzcCPHfGauT6.description:
Requirements The hesper has spent at least 1 hour in contact with a reactor or other large power source

Effect The hesper Strides into the reactor, passing through its exterior and gaining fast healing 5 while inside. The hesper is aware of but can't physically interact with their surroundings and is protected from those outside. If the reactor is broken, the hesper takes @Damage[2d10[force]] damage and is immediately expelled from it. If the reactor is destroyed while the hesper is inside, the hesper must succeed at a @Check[fortitude|dc:15] save or be slain instantly.
hknftzcCPHfGauT6.name: Merge

qpt7EVgZkAzVa9DX.description: A hesper can sense radiation sources, such as reactors and power cores, as an imprecise sense at the listed range.
qpt7EVgZkAzVa9DX.name: Radiation Sense

sGavOZIHTZG0i8lR.description: A hesper can change the damage type of its energy ray as a free action.
sGavOZIHTZG0i8lR.name: Energy Ray

Hesper.name: Hesper

Host Dragon (Adult).description: Innumerable insects follow these lumbering, ravenous dragons wherever they roam, swarming around them and living in the countless orifices along the host dragon's body. The dragon is both a part of the swarm itself and a part of the swarm's ecosystem—the swarm feeds on their body, and the dragon feeds on the swarm in a grotesque, centuries-long cycle that somehow results in the host dragon growing larger and more powerful even if they feed on no other substance in their lifetime. Host dragons draw their power from the primal instincts of insects and, despite their intelligence, often behave like the insects they gather to them. Host dragons despise answering questions and violently defy all attempts others make to understand their nature.

Iirg1MEAtdtiIeBe.description:
Trigger The dragon critically fails a saving throw

Effect Swarming insects interfere with the effect, sacrificing themselves to protect their host's body and mind. The dragon attempts a @Check[flat|dc:17]. On a success, the dragon fails the saving throw instead of critically failing.
Iirg1MEAtdtiIeBe.name: Covered in Bugs

PIWNVL4bNDzMtvjX.description: The dragon makes two claw Strikes and one tail Strike in any order.
PIWNVL4bNDzMtvjX.name: Draconic Frenzy

eIVOyIMb6eydRywB.description: The dragon transforms into an insect swarm. They drop all held, worn, and carried items. While in this form, they can't use attack actions (except Swarming Bites and Swarm Breath) and can't cast spells, but they can move through areas small enough for their individual insects to fit without having to Squeeze. They can use the same action to coalesce back into their normal form.
eIVOyIMb6eydRywB.name: Swarm Shape

enSboo96fqQMk6pL.name: +2 status to all saves vs. mental

iBiBaO2kPuQJut07.description:
Requirements The dragon is a swarm

Effect Each enemy in the swarm's space takes @Damage[8d6[piercing]] damage (@Check[fortitude|dc:30|basic] save). A creature that fails its save is also @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.MIRkyAjyBeXivMa7]{Enfeebled 1} for 1 round.
iBiBaO2kPuQJut07.name: Swarming Bites

j2VahQANZRoy87zO.description: The host dragon is immune to any attack made by a swarm of insects or similar creature (at the GM's discretion).
j2VahQANZRoy87zO.name: One with Swarms

nFjwpY6DJ3GighJQ.description: The dragon recharges their Swarm Breath whenever they score a critical hit with a Strike.
nFjwpY6DJ3GighJQ.name: Draconic Momentum

xCKxNit5WWVs9p8f.description: The dragon disgorges a swarm of biting insects that deals @Damage[9d8[piercing]|options:area-damage] damage in a @Template[type:cone|distance:40] (@Check[reflex|dc:30|basic] save). They can't use Swarm Breath again for [[/gmr 1d4 #Recharge Swarm Breath]]{1d4 rounds}.
xCKxNit5WWVs9p8f.name: Swarm Breath

xTqOhhPRqhJmqars.description: A creature that takes damage from a host dragon's jaws Strike or is swallowed by the dragon is also bitten by hundreds of tiny insects; the creature must succeed at a @Check[fortitude|dc:28] save or be @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.MIRkyAjyBeXivMa7]{Enfeebled 2} for 1 round.
xTqOhhPRqhJmqars.name: Excruciating Bites

Host Dragon (Adult).name: Host Dragon (Adult)

Host Dragon (Young, Spellcaster).description: Innumerable insects follow these lumbering, ravenous dragons wherever they roam, swarming around them and living in the countless orifices along the host dragon's body. The dragon is both a part of the swarm itself and a part of the swarm's ecosystem—the swarm feeds on their body, and the dragon feeds on the swarm in a grotesque, centuries-long cycle that somehow results in the host dragon growing larger and more powerful even if they feed on no other substance in their lifetime. Host dragons draw their power from the primal instincts of insects and, despite their intelligence, often behave like the insects they gather to them. Host dragons despise answering questions and violently defy all attempts others make to understand their nature.

Iirg1MEAtdtiIeBe.description:
Trigger The dragon critically fails a saving throw

Effect Swarming insects interfere with the effect, sacrificing themselves to protect their host's body and mind. The dragon attempts a @Check[flat|dc:17]. On a success, the dragon fails the saving throw instead of critically failing.

Ichor Lord.description:
Orocoran ichor lords are blessed by the Newborn—ichor flows through their veins, and they can conjure short-lived fonts of ichor. Most gather desperate orocorans around them, controlling their brethren through access to ichor.

Native to the now-destroyed planet of Aucturn, orocorans are foul and desperate creatures, cast adrift in space as they yearn to consume once more the essence of the Newborn god or fragments of the womb it gestated within. They're irritable, violent, and utterly anguished.

While some orocorans have broken free of their addiction and regained their clarity of mind and sense of self, the orocorans presented here are those who still rely on Aucturn's eldritch fluids.

IAWVrxRgSO9ox2VU.description:
An orocoran's stomach fluids are laced with hallucinogens due to their consumption of the ichor-like birthing fluids expelled by Aucturn during the hatching of the Newborn.

A creature hit with the projectile vomit must succeed at a @Check[will|dc:28] save or be @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.yblD8fOR1J8rDwEQ]{Confused} for 1 round (1d4 rounds on a critical failure).
IAWVrxRgSO9ox2VU.name: Hallucinate

eWnCfjQO87fg7Lc8.description:
Frequency once per round

Requirements A creature within reach of the orocoran's proboscis is taking persistent bleed damage

Effect The orocoran flicks out their proboscis and sups on the flowing blood of their enemy. The orocoran regains Hit Points equal to the target's persistent bleed value.
eWnCfjQO87fg7Lc8.name: Lick Wounds

npkNvy8QeLPktGgI.description:
Trigger The ichor lord is dealt piercing or slashing damage

Effect Hallucinogenic ichor spurts from the ichor lord's wound, dealing @Damage[1d6[mental]|options:area-damage] damage to non-orocoran creatures in a @Template[type:emanation|distance:10] centered on the ichor lord (@Check[will|dc:28|basic] save).
npkNvy8QeLPktGgI.name: Ichor Spray

oB748thJIyEXmzE5.description:
Your gaze pierces through illusions and finds @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.zJxUflt9np0q4yML]{Invisible} creatures and spirits. You can see invisible creatures as though they weren't invisible, although their features are blurred, making them @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.DmAIPqOBomZ7H95W]{Concealed} and difficult to identify. You can also see incorporeal creatures, like ghosts, phased through an object from within 10 feet of an object's surface as blurry shapes seen through those objects. Subtler clues also grant you a +2 status bonus to checks you make to disbelieve illusions.

Heightened (5th) This spell has a duration of 8 hours.

@UUID[Compendium.sf2e.spell-effects.Item.T5bk6UH7yuYog1Fp]{Spell Effect: See the Unseen}
oB748thJIyEXmzE5.name: See the Unseen (Constant)

sleA9O90zepppciQ.description:
Requirements The ichor lord is touching solid ground

Frequency once per hour

Effect With a psychic cry to the Newborn, the ichor lord tears open the earth, causing a geyser of hallucinogenic ichor to burst from the ground within 100 feet. This geyser occupies a 50-foot-tall cylinder with a 10-foot radius base. The base of this geyser must be on the ground or a similar solid surface, and the geyser must be oriented vertically. Each creature in the area takes @Damage[4d6[bludgeoning],4d6[mental]|options:area-damage]{4d6 bludgeoning damage and 4d6 mental damage}, with a @Check[reflex|dc:28] save. A creature pushed into the air by the geyser can't be pushed beyond the top of the geyser. After being pushed into the air, a creature falls unless it's flying, is in zero gravity, or has some other means of staying aloft in its current environment, taking falling damage as normal.

Critical Success The creature is unaffected.

Success The creature takes half damage and isn't pushed into the air.

Failure The creature takes full damage and is pushed 20 feet into the air.

Critical Failure The creature takes double damage and is pushed 40 feet into the air. The geyser continues to flow for 1 minute, gently raining ichor in a @Template[type:emanation|distance:30] centered on the geyser's base. An orocoran in the area of this rain can drink the ichor once per round as a single action with the manipulate trait; if they do, they become invigorated, gaining a +2 circumstance bonus to damage rolls and resistance 5 to physical damage until the beginning of their next turn.
sleA9O90zepppciQ.name: Ichor Wellspring

Ichor Lord.name: Ichor Lord

Ignurso.description:
Adventurers exploring active geothermal areas might encounter one of the extreme habitat's most unique creatures: ignursos. These ursine burrowers are partially armored with scales and a fearsome horn. They're sedentary by nature, but when disturbed, their rage combines the ferocity of a bear mauling with the heat of a pyroclastic flow.

Ignursos are specially adapted to survive in extremely hot climates but thrive anywhere warm. Those that inhabit less hospitable planets tend to stay underground and hibernate during the coldest parts of the year.

Scavengers by nature, ignursos can't take their next meal for granted. However, these clever creatures can manipulate their environment to trap prey. Ignursos have been observed creating large networks of burrows right before volcanic eruptions, seemingly because they understand lava flows will follow this path of least resistance. These tunnels turn to rivers of red-hot lava perfectly positioned to strand fleeing wildlife. Ignursos then return for their spoils after the worst of the eruption has passed.

Ignursos have a significant impact on volcanic ecosystems. Burrowing ignursos break up solid rock—often freshly deposited after an eruption—kick-starting the process of soil formation that's necessary for the return of plants. Some dig too close to underground magma chambers, turning their tunnels into volcanic vents that release lava and gases. In this way, they make explosive, damaging eruptions much less likely and provide a moderating force on a harsh environment.

1FTodvEiwg3AIx9w.description: The ignurso ignores the @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.DmAIPqOBomZ7H95W]{Concealed} condition from smoke.
1FTodvEiwg3AIx9w.name: Smoke Vision

C9IhS5S4lZZ1R5cX.description: The ignurso expels lava in a @Template[type:cone|distance:30], dealing @Damage[6d6[fire]|options:area-damage] damage (@Check[reflex|dc:20|basic] save). A creature that fails its save also takes @Damage[1d6[persistent,fire]|options:area-damage] damage. The ignurso can't Spew Lava again for [[/gmr 1d4 #Recharge Spew Lava]]{1d4 rounds}.
C9IhS5S4lZZ1R5cX.name: Spew Lava

ILSFqrOHGohABQik.description: The ignurso gains a +3 circumstance bonus to damage rolls against creatures it has @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.kWc1fhmv9LBiTuei]{Grabbed} or @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.VcDeM8A5oI6VqhbM]{Restrained}.
ILSFqrOHGohABQik.name: Mauler

ZaLMqfnQO3EZe7cS.description: The ignurso is immune environmental fire damage and fatigue from to heat and lava
ZaLMqfnQO3EZe7cS.name: Lavaproof

rOqVyQ4dVgG3MgCb.description: 20 feet. The ignurso is shrouded in a cloud of smoke and ash. Creatures within the aura are @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.DmAIPqOBomZ7H95W]{Concealed}, and creatures outside it are concealed to creatures within. The ignurso can deactivate or activate this aura as a single action, which has the concentrate trait.
rOqVyQ4dVgG3MgCb.name: Thermal Venting

Ignurso.name: Ignurso

Illumantula.description:
Though it only recently appeared in the shattered red deserts of the planet Akiton, the so-called illumantula has already become the stuff of local legend and folklore. Emerging shortly after the crash of the mysterious First Ones vessel now only known as the Wreck of the Returned, the illumantula was so named by the shobhad desert guides who first encountered the creature and compared it to the deadly spiders of the Akitonian glaciers. Other Pact Worlds citizens have taken to the name, as the closest descriptive title for the being has simply been "a spider made of light."

Content—for now—to spend its days wandering the Wreck of the Returned and the immediately surrounding area, the illumantula has only had a handful of meaningful engagements since its appearance. The first was against a group of Hellknights of the Order of the Eclipse, where the illumantula systematically unmade 80 of their best-trained troops in under two minutes. Only weeks after the engagement, a group of Stewards attempting to enter the Wreck of the Returned were discovered and engaged at the periphery of the illumantula's patrol path. Only two of 12 commandos managed to escape, and their accounts of the illumantula and its powers are contradictory, leaving the Stewards unable to make effective plans for further encounters.

A strict quarantine has been set up to match the illumantula's patrol path, as calculated by the meticulous anacites of Investigation Site A01. The Aballonian constructs know the being to be related to the First Ones and dedicate their time to finding a means of communicating with the swarm of technological bits that patrol the outer wastes of the crashed starship. So far, they've had no success, and they've sent out an urgent call for linguistics and computers experts from across the Pact Worlds to travel to Akiton and aid their research.

Where the anacites continue their experiments, scholars of Eloritu have uncovered a disturbing connection between the illumantula and the concept of alternate realities. Somehow, the actions of the illumantula produce fixed points in reality, where the unique powers of creatures with greater connections to the multiverse are somehow stymied or forced to adhere to the illumantula's will. The reason for this phenomenon remains a mystery, though one the anacites seem blissfully ignorant to explore.

The appearance of the illumantula has led to the belief that it's a protector for the ancient technology of the mysterious First Ones. Similarities between the illumantula's technological bits and extracted data from Aballon have all but confirmed this theory. However, the association begs the question: is there just one illumantula, or is it merely one of many such highly advanced guardian constructs for the First Ones, a species who might be beyond anything the Pact Worlds could contend with?

0RiO21w4ism4aB4e.description:
Trigger A creature moves within the illumantula's space or uses a manipulate action, move action, or ranged attack within 100 feet of the illumantula

Effect The illumantula attempts a ranged Strike against the triggering creature. If the attack is a critical hit and the trigger was a manipulate action, the illumantula disrupts that action. This Strike doesn't count toward the illumantula's multiple attack penalty, and its multiple attack penalty doesn't apply to this Strike.
0RiO21w4ism4aB4e.name: Reactive Unmaking

7my0vfkO4aJKvOTp.description: You see things within 60 feet as they actually are. The GM rolls a secret counteract check against any illusion, morph or polymorph effect in the area, but only for the purpose of determining whether you see through it (for instance, if the check succeeds against a polymorph spell, you can see the creature's true form, but you don't end the polymorph spell).
7my0vfkO4aJKvOTp.name: Truesight (constant)

AMKI2JGgwjzTbREQ.description:
You slice through reality, forming a chasm of life-draining entropy in a straight line 20 feet high, 120 feet long, and 2 inches thick. The chasm provides cover. The chasm deals 7d8 void damage to each creature that's in the chasm's space when it's created, that attempts to pass through the chasm, or that ends its turn inside the chasm, with a basic Reflex save. A creature that succeeds at this save when the chasm is created is pushed to the nearest space on the side of its choice. Creatures trying to move through the chasm fail to do so if they critically fail the save, ending their movement next to the chasm.

Heightened (+1) The damage increases by 1d8.
AMKI2JGgwjzTbREQ.name: Slice Reality (at will)

CO1yXx0XqzaftZvN.description:
You take control of a technological creature or object and command it telepathically. If you issue an obviously self-destructive order to a sapient target, the target doesn't act until you issue a new order. The effect depends on its Will save.

Critical Success The target is unaffected.

Success The target is @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.dfCMdR4wnpbYNTix]{Stunned 1} as it fights off your commands.

Failure You control the target. It gains the controlled condition, but it can attempt a Will save at the end of each of its turns. On a success, the spell ends.

Critical Failure As a failure, but the target receives a new save only if it's sapient and you give it a new order that's against its nature, such as killing its allies.

Heightened (10th) The duration is unlimited.
CO1yXx0XqzaftZvN.name: Control Machine (at will)

FnTn2qdV7dLwdPhe.description:
You repel effects that would hinder a creature or slow its movement. While under this spell's effect, the target ignores effects that would give them a circumstance penalty to Speed. When they attempt to @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.actions.Item.SkZAQRkLLkmBQNB9]{Escape} an effect that has them @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.eIcWbB5o3pP6OIMe]{Immobilized}, @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.kWc1fhmv9LBiTuei]{Grabbed}, or @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.VcDeM8A5oI6VqhbM]{Restrained}, they automatically succeed unless the effect is magical and of a higher rank than the unfettered movement spell.

@UUID[Compendium.sf2e.spell-effects.Item.CdAyAiMGESvgNQtz]{Spell Effect: Unfettered Movement}
FnTn2qdV7dLwdPhe.name: Unfettered Movement (constant)

OX485P0OHSZfmsd0.description: The illumantula is a grouping of tiny tech bits that project energy between themselves, though the illumantula functions as single creature. The illumantula's size gives its space while being fully dispersed, though it can take actions to change its size. The illumantula can occupy the same space as other creatures and must do so to use some of its actions.
OX485P0OHSZfmsd0.name: Mutable Form

PC9qlt290mwC5zVw.description: Creatures sharing a space with the illumantula can't use any actions or abilities with the fortune trait. A creature beginning its turn within the illumantula's space can't use actions or ability with the fortune trait until the end of their turn. The illumantula has weakness 10 against any ability or action affected by the fortune trait that successfully damages it.
PC9qlt290mwC5zVw.name: Relativity Field

V0foA0vY04Zk66on.description: The illumantula releases coordinated blasts from each of its constituent bits at creatures within its form. Each enemy in the illumantula's space takes @Damage[12d8[electricity]] damage (@Check[reflex|dc:49|basic] save). A creature that fails its save is also @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.XgEqL1kFApUbl5Z2]{Blinded} for 1 round (or 1 minute on a critical failure). The blinding is a visual effect.
V0foA0vY04Zk66on.name: Energy Bombardment

VX9q6P0T0eqhOhuX.description: When the illumantula scores a critical hit with a transreality beam Strike, the target becomes @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.3uh1r86TzbQvosxv]{Doomed 1}, or increases its doomed value by 1 if it was already doomed.
VX9q6P0T0eqhOhuX.name: Unreality Engine

WWLKxSSA4iziqI4E.description:
Frequency once per round

Effect The illumantula changes its size to either Huge, Large or Medium as desired. When changing size in this manner, the illumantula can determine what direction its new space takes up or what portion of its existing space is removed. This movement doesn't trigger reactions.
WWLKxSSA4iziqI4E.name: Reform

ip3uDaHTkBN1uY0U.description:
You flash freeze a target then send subsonic waves through it, potentially reducing it into fine powder. Make a spell attack against the target. If you hit a target, the target takes 6d8 cold damage and must attempt a Fortitude save. If you critically hit, the target gets a result one degree of success worse than it rolled on its Fortitude save. A creature reduced to 0 Hit Points is blasted to fine powder; its gear remains.

Critical Success The target is unaffected by further damage.

Success The target takes an additional @Damage[((@item.level -3)d8)[sonic]] damage.

Failure The target takes an additional @Damage[((@item.level)d8)[sonic]] damage.

Critical Failure The target takes an additional @Damage[((@item.level +6)d8)[sonic]] damage.

Heightened (+1) The cold and sonic damage each increase by 1d8.
ip3uDaHTkBN1uY0U.name: Promession (at will)

y75ZVtBLrVMtL3od.description:
You supercharge the targets' electromagnetism and pull them with a tether of lightning. Make a ranged spell attack against each target. If you attack two targets, both attacks count toward your multiple attack penalty, but it doesn't increase until after both attacks. The targets each take 4d8 electricity damage and are pulled 5 feet closer to you, or 10 feet closer on a critical hit. If both attacks hit, you can choose to move the creatures closer to one another instead of closer to you. Moving a target into a barrier, creature, or obstacle causes the target to stop before entering that space.

Heightened (+1) The damage increases by 1d8.
y75ZVtBLrVMtL3od.name: Electrotether (at will)

yIgeS31f6c5ZaBCl.description: You unravel the magic behind a spell or effect. Attempt a counteract check against the target. If you successfully counteract a magic item, the item becomes a mundane item of its type for 10 minutes. This doesn't change the item's non-magical properties. If the target is an artifact or similar item, you automatically fail.
yIgeS31f6c5ZaBCl.name: Dispel Magic (at will)

Illumantula.name: Illumantula

Iridia.description:
When mortals encounter spectra outside the drift, that encounter is usually with an iridia. These opalescent, bipedal ambassadors travel the cosmos as messengers and agents of the Drift, extolling the benefits of new and emergent technologies. They champion growth and improvement in all aspects of life but especially focus on the advancement of new technologies. Their goals often put them at odds with those who forswear controversial and dangerous tech or who approach new and untested discoveries with caution.

Iridias are known to visit remote worlds in the Vast, far away from Absalom Station and the Drift lanes where Triune's original signal and the secrets of Drift travel were suppressed, lost, or misunderstood. They bring the people of these isolated worlds instructions to achieve interstellar travel and a second chance to join the galactic community.

In the Great Beyond, time is measured not in hundreds, thousands, or millions of years, but rather in eons—in iterations of reality itself. Only rising to prominence within the last three centuries alongside the advent and proliferation of Drift technology, spectra have thrived in a burgeoning niche of the otherwise stagnant zeitgeist of the Great Beyond.

Though their origins and objectives remain shrouded in mystery, encounters with spectra revolve around new technological discoveries, sharing the knowledge of faster-than-light travel, and protecting the Drift. No one knows if spectra existed before the Drift, but their connection to the hyperspace plane is indisputable. Prominent metaphysicians believe spectra were created as amalgams of raw quintessence pulled into the Drift, just as the Drift itself grows from pieces of the Multiverse. If this is true, spectra's interest in the proliferation of Drift technology takes a subtle sinister turn, as each new Drift engine serves to harvest the Great Beyond and all its denizens for the growth of the Drift and spectra themselves.

1ZoyzWJuCNJTinkV.description:
The target can understand all words regardless of language and also speak the languages of other creatures. When in a mixed group of creatures, each time the target speaks, it can choose a creature and speak in a language that creature understands, even if the target doesn't know what language that is.

Heightened (7th) The duration is 8 hours.
1ZoyzWJuCNJTinkV.name: Truespeech (constant)

7ZUimWQC9ALb1KJy.description: 100 feet. An iridia can communicate telepathically with any item or creature with the tech trait within their aura as well as with other technologically telepathic creatures (such as those with shortwave and similar abilities). This ability also allows the spectra to remotely attempt Computers checks within their aura.
7ZUimWQC9ALb1KJy.name: Digital Telepathy

LnJPfnLpCGgAgwec.description: An iridia has an internal biomechanical Drift engine, allowing them to function as a Drift engine for a starship or vehicle they pilot as a 1-minute activity. An excuba can enter or exit the Drift themself as a 1-minute activity. When an excuba gets a critical failure on a Piloting check to Navigate or Plot a Course through the Drift, they get a failure instead.
LnJPfnLpCGgAgwec.name: Slip Drive

Lxb0AMTemjqyB943.description:
The excuba can take on the appearance of any Small or Medium humanoid.

@Localize[PF2E.NPC.Abilities.Glossary.ChangeShape]
Lxb0AMTemjqyB943.name: Change Shape

XhW8w8OzWBzB2V00.description: The iridia senses creatures and objects with the tech trait as a precise sense within the listed range.
XhW8w8OzWBzB2V00.name: Techsense

jFS4QBQR119XoGeP.description:
You touch one object and concentrate on a dataset contained within it, such as a story, message, file, infosphere site, audio recording, or video. You understand the gist of the dataset and can quickly locate the most relevant pages or sections to your search. If the dataset is written or otherwise communicated in a language you don't know, or you attempt to gain information from a computer you don't have access to (such as one with a password you don't know), the spell fails.

If you Cast this Spell as part of a @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.actions.Item.t5nBkpjroaq7QBGK]{Research} activity, you treat a critical failure as a failure instead.
jFS4QBQR119XoGeP.name: Skim Data (at will)

nqLYHgFAjGoflAEX.description:
Frequency once per round

Trigger The iridia is targeted by a ranged Strike

Effect A rainbow of visual distortion cascades across the iridia. They desynchronize from reality and are briefly replaced by a two-dimensional rendering, gaining concealment against the triggering Strike.
nqLYHgFAjGoflAEX.name: Shift Dimensionality

ogyjglxXLyTtMt6q.description:
You instantly transport yourself and any items you're wearing and holding from your current space to an unoccupied space within range you can see. If this would bring another creature with you—even if you're carrying it in an extradimensional container—the spell is lost.

Heightened (5th) The range increases to 1 mile. You don't need to be able to see your destination, as long as you have been there in the past and know its relative location and distance from you. You are then temporarily immune for 1 hour.
ogyjglxXLyTtMt6q.name: Translocate (at will)

sC24htf1m2EuSJeb.description: The iridia can communicate through items and creatures with the tech trait, projecting sound from and speaking through the item or creature's voice, speakers, or other audio output. In addition, the excuba can use any item or creature with the tech trait within their digital telepathy aura as the point of origin for their spells and abilities when calculating range, distance, line of effect, and area of effect.
sC24htf1m2EuSJeb.name: Arc Network

Iridia.name: Iridia

Irradiated Undead Charger.description:
Chargers, known by as many different names as their planets of origin, usually spawn from the irradiated corpses of beasts slain by natural or manufactured nuclear disasters. These quadrupedal, animalistic undead are so named for their mighty charge attack.

To survive in the unforgiving expanse of space, creatures must be naturally adapted or take protective measures. While the dead rarely need such precautions against these threats, sometimes radiation can animate a corpse (or several) to a state of undeath!

Scientists and religious scholars alike debate whether a specific type of radiation is to blame for this phenomenon that spontaneously triggers unlife, but all agree on the dangers such irradiated creatures pose. Many types of radiation could be the cause: intense bursts of cosmic radiation emitted by the stars, magically enhanced radioactive isotopes found in a planet's or moon's crust, or even the advent of new energy sources in a society (or its radioactive waste) contaminating the land. Regardless of their specific origin, irradiated undead all pose the same threat—they emit ionizing radiation that ravages everything around them.

8hc5iw5TzJvu2DfW.description: 20 feet. A creature entering or starting its turn inside the aura is exposed to extreme radiation.
8hc5iw5TzJvu2DfW.name: Radioactive Remains

BRrRxYCnAV4mgZaQ.description:
Trigger The irradiated undead plant is reduced to 0 Hit Points by energy damage of any kind

Effect The energy acts as a catalyst for a nuclear reaction, causing the plant to explode and dealing @Damage[9d6[poison]|options:area-damage] damage to all creatures in a @Template[type:emanation|distance:20] with a @Check[reflex|dc:24|basic] save.
BRrRxYCnAV4mgZaQ.name: Meltdown

X1WkxvaHxiwy44bb.description: The irradiated charger triggers a localized radioactive reaction as it charges. It Strides once and then Strikes. A creature damaged by this attack takes 1 additional point of void damage for every space the charger moved prior to making its Strike. On a critical hit, the creature is also knocked @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.j91X7x0XSomq8d60]{Prone}.
X1WkxvaHxiwy44bb.name: Charged Burst

Irradiated Undead Charger.name: Irradiated Undead Charger

Irradiated Undead Flyer.description:
Flyer is a general term referring to winged creatures such as drakes, gigantic dragonflies, raptors, and other flying beasts that have been reanimated by severe radiation.

To survive in the unforgiving expanse of space, creatures must be naturally adapted or take protective measures. While the dead rarely need such precautions against these threats, sometimes radiation can animate a corpse (or several) to a state of undeath!

Scientists and religious scholars alike debate whether a specific type of radiation is to blame for this phenomenon that spontaneously triggers unlife, but all agree on the dangers such irradiated creatures pose. Many types of radiation could be the cause: intense bursts of cosmic radiation emitted by the stars, magically enhanced radioactive isotopes found in a planet's or moon's crust, or even the advent of new energy sources in a society (or its radioactive waste) contaminating the land. Regardless of their specific origin, irradiated undead all pose the same threat—they emit ionizing radiation that ravages everything around them.

31AxZ6tSCPadNmUq.description: 20 feet. A creature entering or starting its turn inside the aura is exposed to severe radiation.
31AxZ6tSCPadNmUq.name: Radioactive Remains

icN5D1ZMt4AN26mv.description:

Effect The energy acts as a catalyst for a nuclear reaction, causing the plant to explode and dealing @Damage[5d6[poison]|options:area-damage] damage to all creatures in a @Template[type:emanation|distance:20] with a @Check[reflex|dc:19|basic] save.
icN5D1ZMt4AN26mv.name: Meltdown

tqfCvpmkBPx2e7UE.description: The irradiated undead flyer Strides twice up to its Speed in a straight line, making a single wing slash Strike against all creatures whose spaces it flies adjacent to. All creatures damaged by the Strafing Snap are considered to be within the flyer's aura at the start of their next turn. The flyer can't use Strafing Snap again for [[/gmr 1d4 #Recharge Strafing Snap]]{1d4 rounds}.
tqfCvpmkBPx2e7UE.name: Strafing Snap

wqVqkJMZ8InToMCg.description:

Effect The irradiated undead flyer channels energy into its wings, forcing all creatures in a @Template[type:emanation|distance:10] to attempt a @Check[fortitude|dc:19] save.

Critical Success No effect.

Success The creature takes @Damage[1d8[void]|options:area-damage] damage.

Failure The creature takes @Damage[2d8[void]|options:area-damage] damage and is pushed back 5 feet.

Critical Failure The creature takes @Damage[4d8[void]|options:area-damage] damage and is pushed back 10 feet.

Irradiated Undead Flyer.name: Irradiated Undead Flyer

Irradiated Undead Plant.description:
Flora are often the first victims of industrialization, dying petal by petal and blade of grass at a time before anybody even notices a loss of habitat. When nuclear fallout corrupts the hardiest species of vegetation, sometimes their irradiated seeds inexplicably bloom into new, unliving specimens.

To survive in the unforgiving expanse of space, creatures must be naturally adapted or take protective measures. While the dead rarely need such precautions against these threats, sometimes radiation can animate a corpse (or several) to a state of undeath!

Scientists and religious scholars alike debate whether a specific type of radiation is to blame for this phenomenon that spontaneously triggers unlife, but all agree on the dangers such irradiated creatures pose. Many types of radiation could be the cause: intense bursts of cosmic radiation emitted by the stars, magically enhanced radioactive isotopes found in a planet's or moon's crust, or even the advent of new energy sources in a society (or its radioactive waste) contaminating the land. Regardless of their specific origin, irradiated undead all pose the same threat—they emit ionizing radiation that ravages everything around them.

3cvcaY3fjj6IksFa.description: When a irradiated undead plant Strikes a creature, some of its contaminated seeds stick to the target. The irradiated undead plant gains the Sprout action. An affected creature can remove this seedpod as an Interact action.
3cvcaY3fjj6IksFa.name: Seedpod

8ybxr7W3iWIi4E7q.description: 20 feet. A creature entering or starting its turn inside the aura is exposed to mild radiation.
8ybxr7W3iWIi4E7q.name: Radioactive Remains

Effect The energy acts as a catalyst for a nuclear reaction, causing the plant to explode and dealing @Damage[3d6[poison]|options:area-damage] damage to all creatures in a @Template[type:emanation|distance:20] with a @Check[reflex|dc:16|basic] save.

HImtTWRGnHStmZnL.description:

Success The creature takes @Damage[1d6[piercing]|options:area-damage] damage.
