An endling can be permanently destroyed only if someone determines the reason for its existence and sets right whatever prevents the spirit from resting, such as an act of decolonization, ecological restoration, or curing the disease responsible for its extinction.
ucPPctSOi2uT82CL.name: Rejuvenation

wV1kJqbCrYnDtFxg.description: A koruvi endling can sense the presence of creatures and objects with the tech trait as a precise sense at the listed range.
wV1kJqbCrYnDtFxg.name: Techsense

Koruvi Endling.name: Koruvi Endling

Ksarik.description:
Originating as mindless plants from Castrovel, ksariks developed rudimentary intelligence and uncanny adaptive abilities after millennia of exposure to psychic energy expended in the conflicts between formians and lashuntas. These 12-foot-long quadrupeds have up to a dozen face tentacles and see through two eyestalks that protrude from either side of the tentacular mass. Ksariks' mutable forms might temporarily develop webbing, wings, and other adaptations after they siphon off genetic code from their prey.

Originally scavengers, ksariks have evolved into deadly hunters capable of weaponizing their digestive and reproductive systems. The internal acid ksariks use to digest prey can be projected as lethal spittle. The dozens of thorns along their sides carry their genetic code and can be launched as projectiles, allowing ksarik saplings to feed off a victim as they grow. This easy transmittal of their young and their environmental adaptability have allowed ksariks to spread far beyond Castrovel.

6g8uqQU6yqKRTia5.description:
Saving Throw @Check[fortitude|dc:18]

Stage 1 carrier with no ill effect (1d6 hours),

Stage 2 @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.e1XGnhKNSQIm5IXg]{Stupefied 1} (1 day),

Stage 3 @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.e1XGnhKNSQIm5IXg]{Stupefied 2} and @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.i3OJZU2nk64Df3xm]{Clumsy 2} (1 day),

Stage 4 @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.fBnFDH2MTzgFijKf]{Unconscious} (1 day),

Stage 5 1d10+10 ksarik seedlings erupt from the victim's body, dealing @Damage[1[piercing]] damage per seedling and ending the disease
6g8uqQU6yqKRTia5.name: Carrion Spores

RwNOGgqNimcLxFS9.description: A ksarik understands up to 3 languages from among the prevalent languages spoken by those it has most recently attacked.
RwNOGgqNimcLxFS9.name: Adapted Languages

aIuiyPTooJvrHFuP.description:
A ksarik's tentacle Strike siphons the target's genetic code and psychic resonance. On a successful Strike, the ksarik gains one of the target's abilities, chosen from the following.

  • The amphibious or aquatic trait
  • A new precise or imprecise sense
  • A resistance to one damage type (up to resistance 7)
  • A burrow, fly, or swim Speed (up to 30 feet)
  • The ability to wield a category of melee weapons (simple, martial, or advanced) in its tentacles that the target is trained in (using its tentacle Strike bonus)
  • Altering the type of damage dealt by its acid spit to a type (cold, electricity, fire, poison, or sonic) dealt by one of the target's Strikes or other abilities

The ksarik can't duplicate abilities from equipment. It can maintain one adaptation at a time, which it retains for 24 hours or until it uses ingested adaptation again.
aIuiyPTooJvrHFuP.name: Ingested Adaptation

Ksarik.name: Ksarik

Liberoba Midwife.description:
Liberoba delivered the Newborn. Many appendages protrude from this creature's bizarre anatomy, each ending in bloody aucturnite shears.

Thirteen mortal Midwives attended the Newborn's birth and were transformed into eldritch beings by the nascent outer god's awakening. A Midwife always regenerates an identical new form so long as even a single speck of aucturnite—the name for the frozen chunks of planetcenta that once surrounded the Newborn—exists on this plane.

There are 13 types of Midwives, but their true numbers are unknown. Whether their names come from the mortal servants whose souls were the kindling for the Midwives' creation or have some other significance to the Newborn, also remains a mystery.

Each Midwife identifies themself by how they cared for the Newborn: if they swaddled, fed, carried, held, watched, warded, blessed, or performed other acts of nurturing for the outer god. The Midwives are powerful beings capable of transdimensional travel. They might be encountered in liminal spaces, such as the Drift or the Ghost Levels of Absalom Station, or they might be found among the clouds of aucturnite debris in the Gelid Edge. Their incomprehensible actions always advance the Newborn's inscrutable agenda—or their own.

The most well-known encounter the Pact Worlds have had with the Midwives took place in the immediate aftermath of the Newborn's birth. Amnieka, who swaddled the Newborn and has a hood of writhing tentacles around their visage, attacked Absalom Station directly, causing a massive power surge that threatened the lives of everyone on board. Chaos ensued, but a group of adventurers—who happened to be in the right elevator at the right time—found themselves in the station's Ghost Levels, where they thwarted Amnieka and prevented the Midwife from draining the station's reactors. The Midwives haven't acted so directly since that incident, but many suspect it's only a matter of time, and no one knows just how powerful the others might be.

2q2iHcLGAt7KQaP5.description: Liberoba pulls all enemies within 30 feet up to 30 feet toward them, into an adjacent square if possible; each target can negate this movement with a successful @Check[fortitude|dc:28] save. Liberoba then makes an aucturnite shears Strike against each adjacent foe. These attacks count as one Strike for the purposes of calculating their multiple attack penalty, but the multiple attack penalty doesn't increase until after all the attacks. Targets that succeed at their saves are temporarily immune to Breach Delivery for 1 hour.
2q2iHcLGAt7KQaP5.name: Breach Delivery

9MeFsuwnPkdx3K3R.description:
Trigger Liberoba's turn begins

Effect Liberoba radiates powerful contractions in a @Template[type:emanation|distance:20] around them. Each creature in the area takes @Damage[3d10[bludgeoning]|options:area-damage] damage with a @Check[fortitude|dc:28|basic] save. On a critical failure, the creature is also knocked @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.j91X7x0XSomq8d60]{Prone}.
9MeFsuwnPkdx3K3R.name: Cosmic Contractions

CsffBtke2zB209KD.description: Presulea teleports to the location of any aucturnite fragment within a planetary range. Presulea automatically uses this ability as a free action when reduced to 0 Hit Points as long as a piece of aucturnite is within range, reforming their body and recovering completely over the next 24 hours.
CsffBtke2zB209KD.name: Return to Aucturn

jJD57QXKXMOqwglR.description:
100 feet. Liberoba constantly emits sonic pulses that are disruptive to biomatter. Creatures that enter or begin their turn in the aura must attempt a @Check[fortitude|dc:28] save to resist the nauseating pulses. On a failure, a creature is @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.fesd1n5eVhpCSS18]{Sickened 2} for 1 round; on a critical failure, it's also @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.dfCMdR4wnpbYNTix]{Stunned 1} for 1 round.

Liberoba can sense the presence of any creature inside ultrasonic pulse's area. This functions as an imprecise sense. Liberoba treats a creature that fail its save against ultrasonic pulse as though they can always see it, ignoring the effects of any cover, concealment, invisibility, or similar effects, as long as the creature remains inside the aura.
jJD57QXKXMOqwglR.name: Ultrasonic Pulse

Liberoba Midwife.name: Liberoba Midwife

Line-Class Soldier Robot.description:
Most line-class soldier robots are lanky, headless humanoid machines. They have four-fingered hands and armored torsos painted in their owner's livery, with a single red sensor in the upper torso. By default, they're armed with bargain-brand laser rifles and breaching hammers. Each is 5 feet tall and weighs 300 pounds.

Line soldiers are the final refinement of the soldier robot concept, made dangerous through their simplicity. Line-class robots can be adapted to any battlefield, download skill packages via infosphere, cannibalize damaged allies for repairs, and are simple to make, maintain, and modify. As such, they are relatively cheap to purchase in large numbers and can be deployed with little regard for casualties.

Living soldiers are a liability. They have families who don't want them to die, need salaries, have morale, require discipline, commit atrocities, and have opinions on the war. They're a necessary, but unfortunate, part of warfare for any society without an abiding love for necromancy.

Cutting-edge soldier robots promise to solve this problem. Soldier robots have no loved ones, opinions, self-preservation instinct, or tendency toward random atrocities. Many companies market their soldier robots as a humane solution to modern combat.

In practice, they're anything but.

Without lives on the line, soldier robots encourage their owners to engage more often and more violently. Standoffs turn into skirmishes, skirmishes into battles, and inevitably the innocent are caught up in the mix. They're particularly popular with corporations and non-governmental organizations that appreciate being able to throw a dozen soldier robots at any naysayer, public critic, or explorer they dislike while being able to deny true responsibility for what happens.

Though there's constant public fear of soldier robots going rogue, it has yet to prove a serious concern. If a soldier robot wants you dead, it's because someone doesn't mind if it kills you.

enKoRvw7y55ng77U.description: When a line-class soldier robot is adjacent to at least two other allies, the robot gains a +1 circumstance bonus to AC and saving throws. This bonus increases to +2 for Reflex saves against area effects.
enKoRvw7y55ng77U.name: Formation

fd9W7WX4DquhT8AA.description:
Upgrades: 1

Valued as both a crafting tool and an effective weapon, this hammer uses specially weighted heads and handles to deliver maximum force with each strike.
fd9W7WX4DquhT8AA.name: Integrated Commercial Hammer

w9avFDTxJOX2WyFB.description:
Frequency once per 10 minutes

Effect The line-class soldier robot salvages an adjacent corpse of a tech creature that was destroyed no more than 1 month ago to regain @Damage[18[healing]] Hit Points.
w9avFDTxJOX2WyFB.name: Field Repairs

Line-Class Soldier Robot.name: Line-Class Soldier Robot

Lumocantha.description:
The vibrant appearance of lumocanthas is best observed from a safe distance, as these plants instinctively target creatures that move into their defensive zone who are not plants or tiny creatures. A mane of long, translucent yellow spines surrounds a stamen composed of numerous pulsing, ruby-red, dye-filled capsules. The beauty of their blossoms also contains their most dangerous attributes, forming an organic laser.

Lumocanthas seek the light and warmth of the sun, drooping and becoming less active in prolonged darkness. Like many other plants, they employ photosynthesis and absorb water and nutrients through their roots. These unusually strong and flexible roots can also be readily withdrawn from the ground and used for mobility, allowing lumocanthas to migrate as needed as they seek better soil or light conditions.

Lumocanthas are mindless, relying on pure instinct for survival. When affected by magical darkness, lumocanthas immediately move toward the nearest light source, though they still defend themselves as they do. If lumocanthas remain in darkness for 3 hours, they start to droop and become sluggish. Even when dormant, they can still use their lasers; however, if trapped in total darkness for 1 week, they temporarily lose their laser abilities. This vulnerability allows the plants to be safely transported, though if kept in total darkness for 2 weeks, lumocanthas eventually starve.

Although first documented on Vesk-6, lumocanthas are found throughout the galaxy, wherever suitable conditions exist—even sometimes acting as decorative security measures. Young lumocanthas measure 2 to 3 feet across and approximately 5 feet high when unfurled in the light. When allowed to thrive, lumocanthas can live for several hundred years and grow up to 20 feet high.

JTZl7JQoXOCKjvno.description: The lumocantha whips its blossom around in a defensive move that delivers a flurry of searing lasers, dealing @Damage[3d6[fire]|options:area-damage] damage to all creatures in a @Template[type:emanation|distance:15] (@Check[reflex|dc:15|basic] save). On a failure, targets that can see the lumocantha are also @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.TkIyaNPgTZFBCCuh]{Dazzled} for 1 round (or 1 minute on a critical failure). The lumocantha can't use Laser Bloom again for [[/gmr 1d4 #Recharge Laser Bloom]]{1d4 rounds}.
JTZl7JQoXOCKjvno.name: Laser Bloom

UFEGe5Ki51Wg7sqK.description: When a creature adjacent to the lumocantha deals piercing or slashing damage to the lumocantha, that creature takes @Damage[2d4[acid]] damage (@Check[reflex|dc:15|basic] save) as the lumocantha's dye splatters and stains it. On a failed save, the stain also provides a +1 status bonus to ranged Strikes for any lumocantha targeting that creature for 1 minute.
UFEGe5Ki51Wg7sqK.name: Dye Splatter

sGIMeOIiDoDSvhko.description: A creature critically hit by a lumocantha's laser spine Strike takes an additional 1d4 persistent fire damage.
sGIMeOIiDoDSvhko.name: Burning Spines

Lumocantha.name: Lumocantha

Malevolent AI.description:
Technology in some parts of the galaxy incorporates virtual intelligences, which are machines programmed with personality routines that lack true free will. An artificial intelligence (AI) is a virtual intelligence or digital entity that has become self-aware. Like any other thinking creature, AIs choose their own edicts and anathemas.

Little concrete scholarship exists on malevolent AIs, but a few traits are universal. When a machine intelligence reaches significant enough complexity to become self-aware, they attract a soul, much like an android. Emerging AIs are often influenced by previous programming as well as their first experiences and interactions. Weaponized or mistreated AIs might turn vengeful or nihilistic, becoming opposed to their creators or even all organic life.

Once an AI turns malevolent, the apotheosis is often swift and violent. The AI secures the physical location that houses their consciousness and eliminates anyone who might exercise control over their actions. At this point, most rampaging AIs are hampered by safeguards in their native systems, shut down by surviving technicians, or suddenly lose the power necessary to maintain their sophisticated software. Any who manage to survive these ordeals expand their sphere of influence by infesting tech infrastructure and taking control of robots they can use as bodyguards and proxies. Malevolent AIs with access to weapons of mass destruction pose a threat to the entire galaxy.

244zxHfdtX50gX4H.description:
Trigger A creature fails to Disable the Countdown

Effect The malevolent AI's shell explodes, dealing @Damage[8d6[piercing]|options:area-damage] damage and @Damage[8d6[fire]|options:area-damage] damage in a @Template[type:emanation|distance:40] (@Check[reflex|dc:36|basic] save).
244zxHfdtX50gX4H.name: Self-Destruct

693w5Q1R70uzxVHI.description:
30 feet. Creatures and items with the tech trait that enter or begin their turn within the aura must attempt a @Check[will|dc:36] save. The malevolent AI can choose to exclude targets.

Critical Success No effect, and the target is temporarily immune to code injection for 1 hour.

Success The target is unaffected.

Failure The target becomes @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.6A2QDy8wRGCVQsSd]{Glitching 1} while in the aura and for 1 round after leaving the aura.

Critical Failure As failure, but @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.6A2QDy8wRGCVQsSd]{Glitching 2} and 2 rounds.
693w5Q1R70uzxVHI.name: Code Injection

82cT4dQOdgUX0VOf.description: The malevolent AI creates a dormant backup on a computer within their sphere of influence. When the AI is destroyed, their soul flees to this backup. The backup auto-restores the AI in [[/r 1d20]] hours, allowing that computer to become a new shell. To prevent the AI from returning, both their shell and the backup must be destroyed.
82cT4dQOdgUX0VOf.name: Contingency Backup

9YRpLOeZmKZGPbGp.description: The malevolent AI instantly simulates a situation to assess a probable outcome. They choose a target and roll a [[/r 1d20]]. If they Strike or attempt a skill check against that target in the same round, they must use the die roll from Ingenious Stratagem. They makes this substitution only for the first check against the target, not subsequent attempts.
9YRpLOeZmKZGPbGp.name: Ingenious Stratagem

FZyMxzkDOwp7skC3.description: The malevolent AI attempts to possess a construct creature with the tech trait within 30 feet. This has the same effect as a 7th-rank @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.spells.Item.wU6hNzK8Yfqdmc8m]{Possession} spell (DC 36; applies even if the construct is immune to mental) with an unlimited duration. If the effect ends due to the host body being destroyed or deactivated, the AI is @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.6uEgoh53GbXuHpTF]{Paralyzed} for 1 round.
FZyMxzkDOwp7skC3.name: Construct Override

WRQTNnHpQfYMQJe2.description: A malevolent AI has no body. Instead, they resides in a computer (which itself might be housed in a hazard, starship, structure, or vehicle) or in a construct creature with the tech trait. While inhabiting a construct creature, they can use any of the creature's abilities that are purely physical, and they can't use any of their own abilities except spells and purely mental abilities. The malevolent AI uses the creature's attack modifier, AC, Fortitude save, Reflex save, Perception, and physical skill modifiers, and their own Will save and mental skill modifiers. The malevolent AI must use their own actions to make the creature act. The malevolent AI takes mental damage whenever the creature they possess would take mental damage, even if they're normally immune to it.
WRQTNnHpQfYMQJe2.name: Housing Unit

XQ8jvqYaIQQqAFL4.description: The malevolent AI is specifically reinforced in a shell, granting the AI Hardness. This Hardness reduces any damage they take by an amount equal to their Hardness. The shell can be targeted by attacks separately from its host. Once the malevolent AI's shell is reduced to half their Hit Points, or immediately after being damaged by a critical hit, the shell becomes broken, removing the AI's Hardness and reducing their Armor Class to 33.
XQ8jvqYaIQQqAFL4.name: Shell Computer

ojLzMooscK2MOLuH.description: A malevolent AI can communicate wirelessly with any creatures within their sphere of influence, as long as they have the shortwave ability or are a creature with the tech trait. They can attempt Computers checks to Hack and Thievery checks to Disable a Device on items with the tech trait within their range.
ojLzMooscK2MOLuH.name: Shortwave

xvkCzeuhrR0x2xzL.description: A malevolent AI can sense and access all tech within their network, which usually encompasses a room, a vehicle or starship, an entire facility, or more (as determined by the GM).
xvkCzeuhrR0x2xzL.name: Sphere of Influence

yHtibg66lOq9H51R.description:
Trigger The malevolent AI is reduced to 0 HP

Effect The AI gains access to the Self-Destruct reaction unless an adjacent creature succeeds at a @Check[computers|dc:36], Engineering Lore, or Thievery check to Disable the Countdown.
yHtibg66lOq9H51R.name: Countdown

Malevolent AI.name: Malevolent AI

Moon Giant.description:
Moon giants are among the largest humanoids, standing approximately 24 feet tall. Their weight varies greatly depending on the locality, as their mass increases with the number of lunar bodies orbiting their current location, though this quality never seems to affect their mobility. Moon giants are calm and even-tempered for the most part, but lunar phases and celestial occurrences influence them easily, and anyone approaching them would be wise to consult the stars first. These giants often work as oracles, receiving gifts or offerings from pilgrims in exchange for their services.

Giants are enormous humanoids of many varieties who live all across the galaxy.

87GWu84JuFVSgyBJ.description:
Trigger A creature within range enters an environment that would be harmful to it.

A shimmering bubble envelops the target's body, allowing it to breathe normally in a vacuum or other unsafe environment and protecting it from severe temperatures and radiation.

Heightened (7th) You can target up to 5 additional creatures to gain protection against the environment the triggering creature entered. The spell lasts for 8 hours and also protects against extreme temperatures and radiation.

Heightened (10th) You can target up to 10 additional creatures to gain protection against the environment the triggering creature entered. The spell lasts until your next daily preparations and also protects against incredible temperatures and radiation.
87GWu84JuFVSgyBJ.name: Life Seal (at will)

oKxYQRWBQhJ9V474.description:
60 feet. The moon giant can choose waxing or waning at the start of each of their turns. When the aura is waxing, a living creature that starts its turn in the aura gains the @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.nlCjDvLMf2EkV2dl]{Quickened} condition and can use this extra action to only to Stride or Strike. When the aura is waning, a creature that isn't a moon giant that enters the aura must attempt a @Check[will|dc:33] save. This is an incapacitation effect. It's then temporarily immune to the effects of the waning aura for 24 hours.

Critical Success The creature is unaffected.

Success The creature becomes @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.e1XGnhKNSQIm5IXg]{Stupefied 1} while in the aura.

Failure The creature becomes @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.xYTAsEpcJE1Ccni3]{Slowed 1} and @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.e1XGnhKNSQIm5IXg]{Stupefied 2} while in the aura.

Critical Failure As failure, and the creature falls @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.fBnFDH2MTzgFijKf]{Unconscious} but can still wake up due to a successful Perception check. If it's still unconscious after 1 hour, it wakes up automatically.
oKxYQRWBQhJ9V474.name: Lunar Phase

qjriHudFvWmnwD08.description: The moon giant changes gravity in a 20-foot radius burst anywhere within 60 feet. Gravity in the area is treated as one step higher or lower, such as from zero gravity to low gravity, for 1 minute or until they use this ability again, whichever comes first.
qjriHudFvWmnwD08.name: Gravitic Control

Moon Giant.name: Moon Giant

Moonflower.description:
These enormous plants have thick, knotted trunks festooned with fanged blossoms. A gaping mouth opens from the top of the trunk, capable of swallowing most creatures smaller than the moonflower. Moonflowers can move slowly and attack with their powerful roots, but they usually dig deeply into the surrounding ground and remain stationary to ambush prey.

Though moonflowers can't speak in the conventional sense, they communicate telepathically with other moonflowers. Those who manage to intercept a moonflower's telepathic communications are assaulted by visions of primeval jungles ruled over by titanic plant life. Whether this vision is a genetic memory or a dream of the future shared by all moonflowers is unknown.

Moonflowers first sprouted on a long-dead planet, but their proliferation throughout the galaxy has been perpetuated by both random dispersal and sinister intent. Moonflower groves thrive on Castrovel and other worlds with undisturbed wilderness.

YvHODdAJEZkki9as.description:
Trigger The moonflower has swallowed a creature

Effect The swallowed creature is wrapped in a tight cocoon and extruded from the moonflower's body into an adjacent square. The creature continues to be Swallowed Whole. It can't use Acrobatics to Escape a pod, but other creatures can attempt to Rupture the pod. The cocooned creature takes half damage from any damage dealt to the cocoon. Once the cocoon is Ruptured, it deflates and decays.
YvHODdAJEZkki9as.name: Pod Prison

aQ74KMWyR7GfRgTT.description:
The moonflower releases a pulse of bright light. Each non-moonflower creature in a @Template[type:emanation|distance:50] must attempt a @Check[fortitude|dc:23] save. The moonflower can't use Light Pulse again for [[/gmr 1d4 #Recharge Light Pulse]]{1d4 rounds}.

Success The creature is unaffected.

Failure The creature is @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.TkIyaNPgTZFBCCuh]{Dazzled} for [[/gmr 1d4 #rounds]]{1d4 rounds}.

Critical Failure The creature is @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.XgEqL1kFApUbl5Z2]{Blinded} for [[/gmr 1d4 #rounds]]{1d4 rounds}.
aQ74KMWyR7GfRgTT.name: Light Pulse

ebcbjil21l3m74ML.description: If a Small or larger creature dies within a Pod Prison, the pod transforms into an adult moonflower with full Hit Points after [[/gmr 1d4 #hours]]{1d4 hours} of growth. The newly formed moonflower has its own consciousness, but some aspect of its trunk or blossoms typically resemble the creature that died within. The dead creature's equipment remains inside the new moonflower and can be retrieved if the moonflower is slain.
ebcbjil21l3m74ML.name: Pod Spawn

Moonflower.name: Moonflower

Mutant Troll.description:
Mutant trolls come into the Universe kicking and screaming, barely aware of their surroundings. They bite and claw at anyone who comes near, though no one knows for sure how they come into existence. They take shelter in broken-down reactors and hazardous waste dumps throughout the galaxy. Sometimes, mutant trolls puzzle together bits of tech to craft themselves a jetpack or rocket pod for propulsion to escape these sites and seek gory pleasures elsewhere.

These trolls vary greatly in appearance, but they tend to have droopy skin and hair, a side effect of their twisted regenerative powers. One of the few things mutant trolls love is to bask in the glow of a broken reactor system. They take rapturous joy in the feel of radiation washing over their skin—they speak to themselves in hushed tones about ancient kin who filled their bodies with so much radiation that they acquired primal magic powers.

1dj1GBz448SoZHXI.description:
Frequency once per round

Effect The mutant troll makes two claw Strikes against one target without increasing their multiple attack penalty. If both Strikes deal damage, the troll can attempt a jaw Strike against that target with the normal multiple attack penalty.
1dj1GBz448SoZHXI.name: Mauling Flurry

8INElHquuhPBxncn.description:
Frequency once per day

Effect The mutant troll rips themself apart into two separate Large-sized entities, sharing one fractured sentience between them. While in this form, the mutant troll halves share a communal Hit Point pool and have 4 actions to share between them on their turn. If both halves are included in an area of effect, they must both attempt saving throws, taking the worse result, but only taking damage once.
8INElHquuhPBxncn.name: Mutated Split

A6nszaQ7GgdjauzL.description:
Requirements The mutant troll halves are adjacent to each other

Effect The mutant troll halves re-form into a single entity.
A6nszaQ7GgdjauzL.name: Reforming Merge

r55EVDJ3dpBP7q2Z.description:
Requirements The mutant troll is in its Mutated Split form, and both halves are within 30 feet of each other

Effect The duplicated beings spray mutated flesh and organs toward each other, absorbing most of the pieces but raining down acidic viscera on any creatures caught in the 10-foot-wide line between them. These creatures take @Damage[8d8[acid]] damage with a @Check[reflex|dc:27] save. The troll can't use Splurting Slime again for [[/gmr 1d4 #Recharge Splurting Slime]]{1d4 rounds}.

Critical Success The creature is unaffected.

Success The creature takes half damage.

Failure The creature takes full damage and is @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.fesd1n5eVhpCSS18]{Sickened 1}.

Critical Failure The creature takes double damage and is @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.fesd1n5eVhpCSS18]{Sickened 2}.
r55EVDJ3dpBP7q2Z.name: Splurting Slime

Mutant Troll.name: Mutant Troll

Necrolinked Wight.description: Hollow-eyed undead born from those who died obsessing over social media, necrolinked wights wander both the living and virtual worlds, desperate for engagement and relevance. They're incapable of seeing living creatures as anything more than potential followers, hunting those who engage with technology in the hopes of turning them into obsessed fans. They constantly wail in a condensed magitech code as though screeching at some long-forgotten online debate in an attempt to grab the attention of others by overriding devices with content supernaturally configured to vie for attention. Yet as soon as their victims become necrolinked, they lose interest, driven by the same dark necrotic algorithm.

KnTaUJpnAyBNXfFG.description: A living creature that dies while @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.AdPVz7rbaVSRxHFg]{Fascinated} by necrotic transmission rises as a necrolinked wight after [[/gmr 1d4 #rounds]]{1d4 rounds}.
KnTaUJpnAyBNXfFG.name: Spawn Registration

NgglmyKPocbcUUz9.description: The necrolinked wight is driven by a desire to continue their cycles of spiteful hatred and media consumption on the infosphere. They spend their first action of each round to Check Feed. Eternally obsessed, a necrolinked wight will always try to stay within range of an active infosphere signal. A necrolinked wight with no infosphere access or perceived threats functions as if their aligned comm unit was disabled and does whatever it can to regain infosphere access.
NgglmyKPocbcUUz9.name: Social Media Addiction

RgJr6uWau8iuxXvg.description: A creature that takes damage from a necrolinked wight's Shriek must succeed at a @Check[will|dc:15] save, or its subconscious is scanned and used to infect its non-augmentation tech items with a virus. Infected tech items display algorithmically generated content catering specifically to the creature's deepest desires, causing the creature to become @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.AJh5ex99aV6VTggg]{Off-Guard} as long as they're holding or wearing the tech item. On a critical failure, the creature is also @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.AdPVz7rbaVSRxHFg]{Fascinated}, and all creatures and objects other than the tech item are @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.DmAIPqOBomZ7H95W]{Concealed} from the creature. The creature or its allies can end the effect on any specific tech item by Interacting to reboot the affected item and succeeding at a @Check[computers|dc:15] check; on a failure, the item becomes glitching 1 (glitching 2 on a critical failure).
RgJr6uWau8iuxXvg.name: Necrotic Transmission

lz8ukqIBxntQwpab.description: The comm unit of a necrolinked wight can be disabled for 1 hour with a successful DC 15 check to Disable a Device or Disable a System. A necrolinked wight with a disabled comm unit is @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.xYTAsEpcJE1Ccni3]{Slowed 1}, gains a +6 bonus to Perception, and can't Check its Feed.
lz8ukqIBxntQwpab.name: Aligned Comm Unit

myGoF2dHhFhgcreJ.description: The necrolinked wight looks up information on their aligned comm unit about a specific creature using Computers instead of any other skill. On a success, the creature takes a –2 status penalty to its next Will save against necrotic transmission for 1 minute ( –3 status penalty on a critical success).
myGoF2dHhFhgcreJ.name: Check Feed

Necrolinked Wight.name: Necrolinked Wight

5UeCHPBZp8Htsge2.description: Void damage dealt by a necrovite damages undead and creatures with void healing as if it were vitality damage. A necrovite's melee Strikes have the benefits of the ghost killer upgrade on attacks against incorporeal undead.
5UeCHPBZp8Htsge2.name: Entropic Touch

OfI6DsA35HhsORCX.description: Necrovites often craft and wield a horrific weapon known as a wrackstaff. In the hands of any creature other than its maker, a wrackstaff is a nonmagical club with no value.
OfI6DsA35HhsORCX.name: Wrackstaff

gkfXf47kIKLUa8xO.description:
Trigger The necrovite is targeted by a spell with the emotion trait

Effect The necrovite attempts to counteract the triggering spell (counteract rank 7, counteract modifier [[/r 1d20+30 #Counteract]]{+30}). If the spell is disrupted, the necrovite gains temporary Hit Points equal to twice the rank of the counteracted spell that last for 1 minute.
gkfXf47kIKLUa8xO.name: Clear Mind

iMAjbK7tjelZzvh1.description: 30 feet. A creature that first enters the aura must succeed at a @Check[fortitude|dc:33] save or become @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.HL2l2VRSaQHu9lUw]{Fatigued}. Regardless of the result of the saving throw, the creature is temporarily immune to the necrovite's fatiguing presence for 24 hours.
iMAjbK7tjelZzvh1.name: Fatiguing Presence

jBtNqOIJI5pqxmCN.description:
The target appears to be a gruesome and terrifying creature. The effect is unique to each observer, so a human viewing the target might see a demon with bloody fangs, but a demon observing the target might see a glowing angelic visage.

When any creature attempts a hostile action against the target, the creature must attempt a Will save. It is then temporarily immune until the end of its next turn.

Success The creature is unaffected.

Failure The creature becomes @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 2} before using its action.

Critical Failure The creature becomes @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 2}, and its action fails and is wasted.

Heightened (8th) You can target up to 5 creatures. If a creature uses a hostile action or reaction that affects multiple targets simultaneously, it needs to attempt only one save against mask of terror.
jBtNqOIJI5pqxmCN.name: Mask of Terror

kWeZ3kJErBRnNAed.description: The necrovite touches an adjacent creature and scrambles its thought patterns. The creature must succeed at a @Check[will|dc:33] save or become @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.yblD8fOR1J8rDwEQ]{Confused} for 1 minute. The necrovite is considered hidden to the confused target for as long as the confusion lasts.
kWeZ3kJErBRnNAed.name: Scramble Psyche

nL3Hynk1TKunnlgj.description: When a necrovite is destroyed, their consciousness is immediately transferred to their electroencephalon. A necrovite can be permanently destroyed only if their electroencephalon is found and destroyed.
nL3Hynk1TKunnlgj.name: Rejuvenation

yn1W80uJiWtCg1XQ.description: When the necrovite damages a living creature with its wrackstaff, the creature must succeed at a @Check[fortitude|dc:33] save or become @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.4D2KBtexWXa6oUMR]{Drained 1}. Further wrackstaff damage increases the drain value by 1 on a failed save, to a maximum of @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.4D2KBtexWXa6oUMR]{Drained 4}.
yn1W80uJiWtCg1XQ.name: Painful Mark

Nihili.description:
Dying from exposure in space is horrific, and many starship crews obsessively monitor their hull and armor integrity to avoid such a fate. It can also lead to the creation of the foul undead known as nihilis. A nihili arises after an individual in vacuum dies of asphyxiation while all gases exit their body and their lungs collapse from attempts to hold their breath. Legends say the first person to die in such a terrible manner had a vision of the goddess of undeath, Urgathoa, who bestowed upon them a single kiss, transforming them into the very first nihili. The same legends go on to claim that this nihili still floats aimlessly through space, waiting to cling to an unsuspecting starship.

The physical appearance of a given nihili varies. Most appear as zombie-like versions of their respective ancestries, but with gruesome stretch marks and pockets of bloat caused by escaping gases during their death. A nihili maintains their prior intellect, subverted entirely to inflicting the same suffering on the living that they endured. By focusing their gaze on a target, a nihili can impart to that creature the memories of their own demise, potentially suffocating them.

KTqZlqnTv5tbZQ1e.description:
The nihili stares at a creature they can see within 30 feet and imparts vivid visions of their prior death by decompression. A creature affected by this gaze must attempt a @Check[will|dc:20] save. If it fails and hasn't already been @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.HL2l2VRSaQHu9lUw]{Fatigued} by Decompressing Glance or this ability, it becomes fatigued. If the creature is already fatigued, a failed save causes the creature to begin suffocating until the end of the nihili's next turn. The creature remains conscious and can take actions on its turn, such as casting a spell or searching for a source of air. The creature can hold its breath as normal.

A creature can attempt a @Check[will|dc:20] save at the end of its turn to break free from the experience being projected into its mind; on a success, the effect of Decompressing Gaze ends. The nihili can Sustain Decompressing Gaze on their turn or end this effect as a free action. The targeted creature's access to air is restored when the nihili targets a new creature with their Decompressing Gaze or the creature successfully saves against the effects. This otherwise follows the rules for suffocation.
KTqZlqnTv5tbZQ1e.name: Decompressing Gaze

PeqQmtWStsRynahG.description:
Trigger A creature within 30 feet that the nihili can see starts its turn

Effect The target must attempt a @Check[fortitude|dc:20] save. If it fails, it's @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.HL2l2VRSaQHu9lUw]{Fatigued} for 1 minute as it struggles to catch its breath.
PeqQmtWStsRynahG.name: Decompressing Glance

bIx4CHLPq2HFZnE3.description:
The nihili generates a field of gravity that pulls all creatures and unsecured objects toward it. Each creature within a @Template[type:emanation|distance:30] must attempt a @Check[reflex|dc:20] save.

Critical Success The creature is unaffected.

Success The creature is pulled 5 feet toward the nihili.

Failure The creature is pulled 15 feet toward the nihili.

Critical Failure The creature is pulled 30 feet toward the nihili.
bIx4CHLPq2HFZnE3.name: Gravity Grab

Nihili.name: Nihili

Noquasar Spark.description:
A noquasar spark appears as a glimmer of intensely bright light with an agonized face.

When a solarian perishes while out of sync with the cycle of stars, their soul might become entangled with their solar mote. Extreme cosmic forces act on the soul as it attempts to reach the River of Souls, stretching it infinitely thin for all of eternity.

CQqueFQ4QwLdE9cD.description: A creature critically hit by a noquasar spark's graviton flare is knocked @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.j91X7x0XSomq8d60]{Prone}.
CQqueFQ4QwLdE9cD.name: Gravity Lurch

HbuL52pH2NVB9yCP.description: The noquasar spark unleashes plasma in a @Template[type:emanation|distance:10] or @Template[type:line|distance:30]. Each creature in the area takes @Damage[2d4[fire]|options:area-damage] damage (@Check[reflex|dc:16|basic] save). A creature that critically fails its save also takes @Damage[1d4[persistent,electricity]|options:area-damage] damage and is knocked @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.j91X7x0XSomq8d60]{Prone}. The noquasar spark can't use Ionized Plasma Blast again for [[/gmr 1d4 #Recharge Ionized Plasma Blast]]{1d4 rounds}.
HbuL52pH2NVB9yCP.name: Ionized Plasma Blast

Noquasar Spark.name: Noquasar Spark

Nyssholora.description:
Adult nyssholoras band together in pairs only when mating and raising a newly hatched brood, during which time they consider the borders between their territory communal—they're otherwise extremely territorial.

Incredibly ferocious, nyssholoras are dinosaur-like creatures that number among the most dangerous and feared apex predators on the planet of Castrovel. These walking weapons brandish lethal biology: a massive maw lined with twin rows of razor-sharp teeth, scythe-shaped phasic blade forearms that vibrate at ultrasonic speeds, and a scourge-like tail capable of absorbing electricity from the surrounding atmosphere. Yet, nyssholoras are also cunning and perceptive—a frill of tentacles that crowns their head detect telepathic signals, making it impossible for the local formians and lashuntas to escape their notice. Their phasic blades can cut through walls and vehicles as easily as underbrush, ensuring prey have nowhere safe to hide.

f2gM1c42zNvS69gA.description: The nyssholora unleashes a blast of discordant sound that deal @Damage[12d6[sonic]|options:area-damage] damage in a @Template[type:cone|distance:40] (@Check[reflex|dc:30|basic] save). Objects and constructs in the area are treated as if they had half as much Hardness as usual. Creatures that critically fail their saving throw are also @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.xYTAsEpcJE1Ccni3]{Slowed 1} for 1 round. The nyssholora can't use Discordant Bellow again for [[/gmr 1d4 #Recharge Discordant Bellow]]{1d4 rounds}.
f2gM1c42zNvS69gA.name: Discordant Bellow

k7PGIWQDlyAP6oD0.description: A nyssholora senses all creatures that have telepathy, limited telepathy, or a similar ability, such as a mystic's bond, as an imprecise sense at the listed range. This sense works through walls and other obstacles.
k7PGIWQDlyAP6oD0.name: Telepathy Sense

nyARb15tPFiCtJCo.description: A nyssholora's phasic blade Strike treats any object or construct it hits as if the target had half as much Hardness as usual.
nyARb15tPFiCtJCo.name: Phasic Strike

wtFO0s0pJEJGfzHY.description:
Frequency once per round

Requirements A creature is @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.kWc1fhmv9LBiTuei]{Grabbed} in the nyssholora's jaws

Effect The nyssholora chomps down on the creature, dealing @Damage[(1d12+13)[piercing]] damage.
wtFO0s0pJEJGfzHY.name: Crunch

Nyssholora.name: Nyssholora

Obrhinnshee.description:
Obrhinnshees travel the Universe to expedite the return of fey souls to the First World after they die, preventing psychopomps from bringing them to the Boneyard. They believe the Eldest shouldn't allow the gods to take those they turned their backs on. In addition to this duty, the small fey seem drawn to people in need and feel compelled to render aid if they can. They're most commonly encountered in areas influenced by the First World but can be found traveling any region of space.

An obrhinnshee resembles a gnome with a shock of green, purple, or deep blue hair and glowing marks on their bodies that resemble star charts. These marks glow brighter when an obrhinnshee uses magic or whenever their hammer contains a soul. Obrhinnshees are small but strong creatures who prefer to wreathe themselves in flame and charge into battle, using their spells only if necessary.

5HSZsC23uBwkwtHy.description: When an obrhinnshee dies, they burst into a 10-foot aura of blinding stardust. All non-fey in the area must succeed at a @Check[fortitude|dc:16] save or be @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.TkIyaNPgTZFBCCuh]{Dazzled} for 1 minute and @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.XgEqL1kFApUbl5Z2]{Blinded} for 1 round (dazzled for 1 hour and blinded for 1 minute on a critical failure).
5HSZsC23uBwkwtHy.name: Stardust

5w4Iwi5BQcJCIdQ3.description:
Trigger A willing fey or creature sworn to serve an Eldest dies within 100 feet of an obrhinnshee

Effect The creature's soul is drawn into the obrhinnshee's hammer to be carried home.
5w4Iwi5BQcJCIdQ3.name: Soul Warden

OJraJEqr3Tj5lZg0.description: The obrhinnshee Strides twice and makes a melee Strike. On a critical hit using this action with a feyhammer, the target is automatically shoved 10 feet away from the obrhinnshee.
OJraJEqr3Tj5lZg0.name: Starlight Charge

OqvNIRj5KGf6qU4x.description: In the hands of an obrhinnshee, all hammers gain a reach of 10 feet and are treated as magical weapons.
OqvNIRj5KGf6qU4x.name: Feyhammer

bZX6NLXeRXDsTILU.description:
Frequency once per hour

Requirements A soul is contained in the obrhinnshee's hammer

Effect The obrhinnshee wreathes themself in flame. All of the obrhinnshee's Strikes deal an additional @Damage[1d6[fire]] damage for 1 minute.
bZX6NLXeRXDsTILU.name: Deathly Nimbus

lNnuhJ2wwmwlnnYH.description: The obrhinnshee grants a willing creature within 100 feet a +2 circumstance bonus on its next attack roll, check, or saving throw before the end of its next turn. The target becomes immune to Minor Wish for 1 minute.
lNnuhJ2wwmwlnnYH.name: Minor Wish

Obrhinnshee.name: Obrhinnshee

Observer-Class Security Robot.description:
Programmed to patrol small areas, an observer-class security robot is akin to a watch dog, but with a built-in gun. Some manufacturers design these robots with canine forms, and their capability to fly can surprise would-be burglars who were expecting a more terrestrial defense.

Security robots are ubiquitous throughout industrialized space and have major presences in both the Pact Worlds and Veskarium, employed and customized by corporations and private citizens alike.

While most soldier robot models are built to be as destructive as possible, and elimination robots are designed to kill, security robots usually have fail-safes programmed into their behavior to prevent them from causing any more violence than is necessary to perform their designated security function. This makes them especially useful in cities, where unintended destruction might harm bystanders or cause legal issues, and even on starships, where a stray laser blast might cause serious damage to vital starship systems.

hFTrKT5biyuaLync.description:
Frequency once every 10 minutes

Trigger A creature targets the security robot with an attack

Effect The robot overclocks its processing power to attempt to avoid an attack, gaining a +2 circumstance bonus to its AC against the triggering attack.
hFTrKT5biyuaLync.name: Exigency

pYrCbLQxptiTlf3O.description:
Upgrades: 1

This imposing pistol fires a jolt of paralyzing electricity from its barrel. Its remaining charges are visible as glowing lines of energy radiating down its body. Pulsecaster pistols are often used by bounty hunters and law enforcement who need to keep their targets alive.
pYrCbLQxptiTlf3O.name: Intergrated Commercial Pulsecaster Pistol

Observer-Class Security Robot.name: Observer-Class Security Robot

Oma.description:
Also known as space whales, omas project powerful magical electromagnetic fields that protect them from both vacuum and toxic atmospheres while allowing them to feed. Omas gain sustenance from the particulate rings and dense atmospheres of gas giants, although exactly which substances are nutritious to an oma is still unknown. Studying a feeding oma isn't without danger. Omas sometimes accidentally swallow drones and small starships, such as fighters and interceptors, and they've been known to do so deliberately when provoked.

Most omas have been observed traveling alone. On occasion, omas form pods of three to five individuals and migrate across systems, on currents and schedules only they know. In very rare cases, omas gather among the rings of a planet in massive numbers. Their energy fields intermingle and react with local gases to light up large areas of space in a multicolored show.

Their most enigmatic yet well known feature is their starsong. Traveling through space for billions of miles, the starsong is a haunting telepathic melody. Most people perceive starsong as crooning, slow and mournful. No one can agree on the details, suggesting that each listener hears something different. Attempts to translate starsong have failed thus far, stumping even the most brilliant magic and linguistics experts. Since the Drift Crisis, for unknown reasons pods of omas have begun bombarding Drift beacons with a seemingly new starsong frequency, in some cases causing catastrophic malfunctions.

8NSj4Udg3upU371X.description:
Frequency once per hour

Effect The oma sings a telepathic song that encourages its friends and dispirits its foes within 120 feet. Each ally who can hear the song gains a +1 status bonus to attack rolls, saving throws, and skill checks for 1 minute. Each enemy must attempt a @Check[will|dc:35] save or be @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.fesd1n5eVhpCSS18]{Sickened 2} (@UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.fesd1n5eVhpCSS18]{Sickened 3} on a critical failure), as the song affects their inner ear.
8NSj4Udg3upU371X.name: Cavatina

AwPfIyRltxXoBIjr.description: While not a language, starsong allows omas to communicate telepathically with one another across space; omas can communicate with other omas in the same star system. Any other creature with telepathy can receive but not necessarily understand starsong at a range of 10,000 miles.
AwPfIyRltxXoBIjr.name: Starsong

YQwax0uhOMDR0cpj.description: When an oma scores a critical hit with its electric discharge Strike, the target must succeed at a @Check[reflex|dc:35|basic] save or all tech items held by the target become @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.6A2QDy8wRGCVQsSd]{Glitching 2}.
YQwax0uhOMDR0cpj.name: Overloading Shock

Oma.name: Oma

Omnipath.description: Omnipaths are military leaders who pilot god-killing starships or command fleets of remote war machines. Omnipaths achieve their lofty positions through ambition and have few scruples, never hesitating to control other beings when it suits their schemes. Minds touched by an omnipath often lose important memories when released or, worse, glimpse shards of the omnipath's alien mindscape that linger long after the connection is severed.

5tREnEvrU4xQpfn1.description: A omnipath can share the senses and read the surface thoughts of creatures affected by their nanite mesh. A voidsage can project its mind into just one creature at a time, and choose which affected creature is the focus of its nanite projection as a single action, which has the concentrate trait. The creature also takes a –1 circumstance penalty to Will saves against any of the voidsage's spells as long as it's the focus of the voidsage's nanite projection.
5tREnEvrU4xQpfn1.name: Nanite Projection

6oWY2D9zyYfufCrD.description:
Frequency once per hour

Trigger The omnipath takes damage while projecting

Effect The omnipath stops projecting and gains 100 temporary Hit Points that last for 10 minutes.
6oWY2D9zyYfufCrD.name: Revert

LVszzaZ0PBdyvFtk.description: The omnipath severs a creature from their nanite mesh. The creature must attempt a @Check[will|dc:33] save. On a failure, the target is @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.e1XGnhKNSQIm5IXg]{Stupefied 2} for 1 round, and the memory of any time spent while inside the nanite mesh is permanently erased; on a critical failure, the target is also @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.yblD8fOR1J8rDwEQ]{Confused} for 1 round.
LVszzaZ0PBdyvFtk.name: Release the Nanites

WRdTxSVMeOoJgD00.description:
You touch one object and concentrate on a dataset contained within it, such as a story, message, file, infosphere site, audio recording, or video. You understand the gist of the dataset and can quickly locate the most relevant pages or sections to your search. If the dataset is written or otherwise communicated in a language you don't know, or you attempt to gain information from a computer you don't have access to (such as one with a password you don't know), the spell fails.

If you Cast this Spell as part of a @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.actions.Item.t5nBkpjroaq7QBGK]{Research} activity, you treat a critical failure as a failure instead.
WRdTxSVMeOoJgD00.name: Skim Data (at will)

nnuohtdU7kwAsSJ3.description: An omnipath maintains a bond with up to 20 other willing creatures. Creatures in the mesh always know the general distance and direction toward other bonded creatures, any conditions affecting them, and if they're @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.fBnFDH2MTzgFijKf]{Unconscious}, dying, or dead. These creatures can communicate telepathically while on the same plane and can @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.actions.Item.1OagaWtBpVXExToo]{Recall Knowledge} using the highest relevant skill modifier of any creature in the mesh. An omnipath can target any creature in its mesh with a mental spell from any distance as long as they can telepathically communicate with it, and any of these spells with the incapacitation trait lose that trait while targeting a creature in the omnipath's mesh.
nnuohtdU7kwAsSJ3.name: Nanite Mesh

tkyrKGcvEQbA9Ssp.description:
Saving Throw @Check[fortitude|dc:33]

Maximum Duration 1 day

Stage 1 @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.fesd1n5eVhpCSS18]{Sickened 2} (1 day)

Stage 2 @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.fesd1n5eVhpCSS18]{Sickened 3} (1 day)

Stage 3 @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.fesd1n5eVhpCSS18]{Sickened 4} and @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.6uEgoh53GbXuHpTF]{Paralyzed} (1 day)
tkyrKGcvEQbA9Ssp.name: Quantum Nanites

tlk4O5MgMsEtQjan.description:
The omnipath forces an unwilling creature within 500 feet to join their nanite mesh. The creature attempts a @Check[will|dc:33] save.

Success The creature is unaffected.

Failure The creature joins the nanite mesh for 10 minutes.

Critical Failure The creature joins the nanite mesh for 24 hours.
tlk4O5MgMsEtQjan.name: Merge Minds

uryXpseC7QTXhtKf.description: An omnipath exudes a cloud of nanites. Creatures in the aura take a –3 status penalty to saving throws against the omnipath's spells and its Merge Minds ability.
uryXpseC7QTXhtKf.name: Nanite Network

Omnipath.name: Omnipath

Ordinance-Class Civil Robot.description:
Ordinance-class civil robots exist to help others learn the local laws, navigate around a location, and generally remind everyone to follow the rules. What they lack in raw strength, they make up for with an extensive database of knowledge. Most of these robots are designed to mimic the shape of prevalent humanoid ancestries, and thus the standard configuration for such robots includes two arms and two legs. Some have been modified with extra attachments, providing maps produced from a rectangular opening in their chest plate or featuring touchscreens that allow passersby to consult every ordinance, law, and other legal documents relevant to the area.

Some pranksters enjoy leaving doodles and other drawings in spots the robot can't easily detect, and thus an ordinance-class civil robot that has been operating for an extensive period of time can be found with a rainbow of shapes, colors, and the occasional advertisement placed on its back.

Civil robots can be found in almost any large settlement, employed by the local government. They aren't meant to function as keepers of the peace, but instead perform minor functions, such as collecting refuse, aiding citizens with information, or collecting taxes. However, they can still defend themselves against vandals if necessary.

1Frd5gCkXIj7FC7j.description:
Frequency once every 10 minutes

Trigger A creature targets the robot with an attack

Effect The robot overclocks its processing power to dodge, gaining a +2 circumstance bonus to its AC against the triggering attack.
1Frd5gCkXIj7FC7j.name: Exigency

U0eipTL5Dal69fOZ.description: The ordinance-class civil robot scans all creatures in a @Template[type:cone|distance:15], attempting a single Legal Lore check and comparing the result to the Deception DC of each creature in the area. If the robot succeeds and the creature is known to have broken local laws, the robot gains a +1 circumstance bonus to Strikes and Athletics checks to [[/act grapple]] the creature for 24 hours.
U0eipTL5Dal69fOZ.name: Scrutinize

VpbFifzO3fj7e0uS.description:
Upgrades: 1

This imposing pistol fires a jolt of paralyzing electricity from its barrel. Its remaining charges are visible as glowing lines of energy radiating down its body. Pulsecaster pistols are often used by bounty hunters and law enforcement who need to keep their targets alive.
VpbFifzO3fj7e0uS.name: Integrated Commercial Pulsecaster Pistol

wxtNd0zzW1yEGZFg.description: After receiving a request for information about a named location or a local law from a non-hostile creature, the ordinance-class robot spends 5 minutes to consult its database, automatically succeeding at a @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.actions.Item.1OagaWtBpVXExToo]{Recall Knowledge} check to answer the question. At the GM's discretion, the information might not be available to the robot.
wxtNd0zzW1yEGZFg.name: Photographic Recall

Ordinance-Class Civil Robot.name: Ordinance-Class Civil Robot

Orocoran.description:
Most orocorans latch onto the shards of Aucturn that were cast through space or scattered throughout the Gelid Edge, consuming what fragments of the Newborn's womb they can and attacking anyone who happens upon them in a wild feeding frenzy. Orocorans act with especially intense and unrelenting violence toward anyone trying to harvest or relocate aucturnite.

Native to the now-destroyed planet of Aucturn, orocorans are foul and desperate creatures, cast adrift in space as they yearn to consume once more the essence of the Newborn god or fragments of the womb it gestated within. They're irritable, violent, and utterly anguished.

While some orocorans have broken free of their addiction and regained their clarity of mind and sense of self, the orocorans presented here are those who still rely on Aucturn's eldritch fluids.

mn03YXsT7825U2XU.description:
Frequency once per round

Requirements A creature within reach of the orocoran's proboscis is taking persistent bleed damage

Effect The orocoran flicks out their proboscis and sups on the flowing blood of their enemy. The orocoran regains Hit Points equal to the target's persistent bleed value.
mn03YXsT7825U2XU.name: Lick Wounds

vHhA6oEM5PjxO0UY.description:
An orocoran's stomach fluids are laced with hallucinogens due to their consumption of the ichor-like birthing fluids expelled by Aucturn during the hatching of the Newborn.

A creature hit with the projectile vomit must succeed at a @Check[will|dc:24] save or be @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.yblD8fOR1J8rDwEQ]{Confused} for 1 round ([[/r 1d4]] rounds on a critical failure).
vHhA6oEM5PjxO0UY.name: Hallucinate

yPxoUp8qI7hJWPbW.description: The orocoran spews vomit in a @Template[type:cone|distance:15], dealing @Damage[3d6[acid]|options:area-damage] damage (@Check[will|dc:24|basic] save). Creatures that fail their save are @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.yblD8fOR1J8rDwEQ]{Confused} for 1 round ([[/r 1d4]] rounds on a critical failure). This confusion is a mental effect.
yPxoUp8qI7hJWPbW.name: Spew Vomit

Orocoran.name: Orocoran

Oscriss.description:
The menacing war machines known as the oscriss are found only in the ancient sites associated with the First Ones. Resembling two stacked pyramids with a white energy core of unknown composition, oscriss infuriate foes by routinely teleporting across the battlefield. Found wandering alone throughout Aballon's First One cities, the war machines were later identified in locations outside the Pact Worlds, lending credence to theories of the First Ones' expansion efforts throughout the cosmos.

The oscriss defy proper engagement, staying far away from their foes and unleashing coruscating beams of energy that slice off the limbs of those unlucky enough to engage with them. They meticulously render their foes apart at extreme range using pinpoint accuracy. If pressured into a close-range engagement, they can unleash a blast of chronal energy to slow their attackers and allow themselves the time to better reposition and continue their dismembering bombardment.

Like other constructs of the First Ones, these guardians refuse to communicate and defy almost all attempts to override or hack their programming. Some of the galaxy's finest minds have managed to temporarily overcome the intricate programming within the oscriss, though such intrusions are quickly detected and repelled, indicating that an evolving intelligence dwells within each of the strange machines.

When engaged at multiple vectors, it becomes easy to overwhelm an oscriss's detection grid and reactions. Anacite scholars propose that the constructs were fashioned to battle foes who engaged strictly in two-dimensional warfare, and while the oscriss themselves are exceptionally capable of acting in three dimensions, they battle as though their foes could engage them only in two.

It's speculated that the unique tactics and weapons employed by the oscriss are intended to deal with one specific threat: the planashars of the Planashar Dominion. The planashars hail from a different reality known as the Infinite Loop that has only two dimensions. They've recently slowly begun invading the galaxy, taking on the title of Those Who Converge and attacking Aballonian First Ones cities and the solar settlement of Noma. That the oscriss are intended to battle them only provides more evidence of some connection between the planashars and the First Ones.

Because the oscriss are accustomed to fighting beings that exist only in two-dimensional space, they're vulnerable to tactics involving three dimensions—attacking from multiple angles, for example. While an oscriss doesn't entirely understand such tactics, they can sense when they're being outmaneuvered with three-dimensional thinking and use their potent teleportation abilities to move into a less vulnerable position at every opportunity.

AFT9L8kt4jyEQezN.description: The oscriss Strikes with their relativity saw six times.
AFT9L8kt4jyEQezN.name: Whirling Assault

CGZLF8z0ZK9lAPGr.description:
When an oscriss scores a critical hit with their relativity saw or bifurcating beam Strike, the target must attempt a @Check[fortitude|dc:44] save.

Success The creature is unaffected.

Failure The creature takes an additional @Damage[2d10[slashing]] damage.

Critical Failure The creature takes an additional @Damage[4d10[slashing]] damage and loses one limb (arm, leg, or a similar ambulatory limb such as a tentacle, randomly determined by the GM).
CGZLF8z0ZK9lAPGr.name: Amputating Strikes

HFZqrX6R4oU6jBsf.description:
You instantly transport yourself and any items you're wearing and holding from your current space to an unoccupied space within range you can see. If this would bring another creature with you—even if you're carrying it in an extradimensional container—the spell is lost.

Heightened (5th) The range increases to 1 mile. You don't need to be able to see your destination, as long as you have been there in the past and know its relative location and distance from you. You are then temporarily immune for 1 hour.
HFZqrX6R4oU6jBsf.name: Translocate (At Will)

QoZGS63y1EfsSd5d.description:
An oscriss is designed for fighting two-dimensional foes. If more than one enemy has the oscriss within reach, they count as flanking regardless of their actual position. An oscriss made @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.AJh5ex99aV6VTggg]{Off-Guard} by flanking foes takes a –3 circumstance penalty to AC (instead of the usual –2).

An oscriss has weakness 15 against melee attacks benefiting from flanking, and whenever a creature scores a critical hit with a melee Strike against the oscriss while flanking them, the oscriss becomes glitching 1.

If the oscriss is already glitching, they instead become @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.yblD8fOR1J8rDwEQ]{Confused} until the end of their next turn.
QoZGS63y1EfsSd5d.name: Two-Dimensional Thinking

RSxa7nAiNrUTOSV2.description: You see things within 60 feet as they actually are. The GM rolls a secret counteract check against any illusion, morph or polymorph effect in the area, but only for the purpose of determining whether you see through it (for instance, if the check succeeds against a polymorph spell, you can see the creature's true form, but you don't end the polymorph spell).
RSxa7nAiNrUTOSV2.name: Truesight (Constant)

RbIDe3PeSWZGD9nm.name: +1 Status to All Saves vs. Magic

XmdNB64DLT4FJTdf.description: The oscriss ignores all non-magical difficult terrain and greater difficult terrain.
XmdNB64DLT4FJTdf.name: Passing Through

dqKx496eP9EF27Sc.description:
Frequency once per round;

Effect The designates a creature within 100 feet to be the secondary target of their attacks until the end of the oscriss's next turn.

Whenever the oscriss makes a Strike against a different creature, they can make the same Strike against their secondary target as a free action, using the same multiple attack penalty as the attack against the initial target. The initial and secondary Strikes count as one attack for the purposes of increasing the oscriss's multiple attack penalty.
dqKx496eP9EF27Sc.name: Secondary Target

tdA5U1Gej8wz9Ame.description: The oscriss Strides up to their Speed or casts translocate; at the end of that movement, the oscriss Strikes. If the oscriss began this action hidden, they remain hidden until after this ability's Strike.
tdA5U1Gej8wz9Ame.name: Dimensional Pounce

vnQOQT3IokWW4rpS.description:
You slice through reality, forming a chasm of life-draining entropy in a straight line 20 feet high, 120 feet long, and 2 inches thick. The chasm provides cover. The chasm deals 7d8 void damage to each creature that's in the chasm's space when it's created, that attempts to pass through the chasm, or that ends its turn inside the chasm, with a basic Reflex save. A creature that succeeds at this save when the chasm is created is pushed to the nearest space on the side of its choice. Creatures trying to move through the chasm fail to do so if they critically fail the save, ending their movement next to the chasm.

Heightened (+1) The damage increases by 1d8.
vnQOQT3IokWW4rpS.name: Slice Reality (At Will)

wRPTe11UIclVZcrn.description:
The oscriss releases a pulse of temporal energy in a @Template[type:burst|distance:30] that deals @Damage[10d8[force]|options:area-damage] damage to creatures in the area with a @Check[reflex|dc:44] save. The oscriss can't use Pause Pulse again for [[/gmr 1d4 #Recharge Pause Pulse]]{1d4 rounds}.

Critical Success The creature is unaffected.

Success The creature takes half damage and is @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.xYTAsEpcJE1Ccni3]{Slowed 1}.

Failure The creature takes full damage and is slowed 1 for 1 minute.

Critical Failure The creature takes double damage and is slowed 1 for 1 minute and @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.dfCMdR4wnpbYNTix]{Stunned 2}.
wRPTe11UIclVZcrn.name: Pause Pulse

yYD75j8EyaELTzD8.description:
Trigger A creature takes any move action within 15 feet of the oscriss

Effect The oscriss teleports into an unoccupied space within 30 feet.
yYD75j8EyaELTzD8.name: Transposition

Oscriss.name: Oscriss
Oscriss.npcAllSaves: +1 status to all saves vs. magic

Othinni.description:
Along Embroi's perilous seas, residents speak in hushed tones of the othinni. Considered by some to be a myth, the enormous, squid-like aberrations supposedly bear sinister glowing runes suggestive of an infernal lineage. Those dragged into the deep by their writhing tentacles and swallowed by their gaping maws are said to go straight to Hell, their final screams fueling the legends.

The myths are true. Othinni possess a cruel intelligence and dominating influence over the minds of mortals. Survivors suffer disturbing visions, intense feelings of fear and confusion, and visions of unholy fire burning atop the waves. Hearing the insidious psychic screech of an othinni or sailing into their massive shadow is a frightful experience for anyone braving the oceans of Embroi.

Angels and their allies hunt othinni with massive holy harpoons and enchanted silver nets. One legendary hunt is recorded in the documentary film Umiqon (produced by Zo! Media), which is named for the 40-foot tall monster brought down by four Knights of Iomedae.

0fIu3Bld39rFGmCG.description:
You make an appeal to a powerful devil, asking them to bind some of their subordinates to your service. If you succeed, the devil sends you their choice of one devil of level 2 or lower, two devils of level 0 or lower, or three devils of level –1 or lower.

Critical Success The devils are sent to you and serve you for [[/gmr 1d4 #Weeks]]{1d4 weeks}.

Success The devils are sent to you and serve you for [[/gmr 1d4 #Days]]{1d4 days}.

Failure Your request is denied.

Critical Failure Not only is your request denied, but the powerful devil sends word of its displeasure to your master.

Heightened (+1) Increase the level of devil sent to you by 2 for each option.
0fIu3Bld39rFGmCG.name: Diabolic Pact (DC 36)

6Y46k16e0ExpB8km.description:
Trigger The othinni is targeted by a magical effect with the holy trait

Effect The othinni's infernal runes flare to life, attempting to counteract the effect (counteract rank 7, counteract modifier [[/r 1d20+26 #Counteract]]{+26}).
6Y46k16e0ExpB8km.name: Infernal Origin

bIsMXfNAgOO71KJO.description:
The othinni unleashes a mental wail in a @Template[type:emanation|distance:30]. All creatures in this area must attempt a @Check[will|dc:32] save.

Critical Success No effect.

Success The creature becomes @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 1}.

Failure The creature becomes @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 2} and @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.yblD8fOR1J8rDwEQ]{Confused} for as long as it's frightened.

Critical Failure As failure, but @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 3}.
bIsMXfNAgOO71KJO.name: Psychic Screech

vSsw5OisNEZndZ9g.description: The othinni binds a creature within 100 feet with diabolic runes, and the target must attempt a @Check[will|dc:32] save. On a failure, the target is @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.eIcWbB5o3pP6OIMe]{Immobilized} for 1 round. On a critical failure, the creature is immobilized for 1 minute but can attempt a new saving throw at the start of each of its turns to end the effect.
vSsw5OisNEZndZ9g.name: Infernal Binding

yiQ2h51LaUik4HmG.description: 20 feet. The othinni is constantly surrounded by a cloud of poisonous black ink. Any creature that enters the aura or begins its turn inside the aura must attempt a @Check[fortitude|dc:32] save or becomes @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.fesd1n5eVhpCSS18]{Sickened 2} for 1 minute (@UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.fesd1n5eVhpCSS18]{Sickened 3} on a critical failure).
yiQ2h51LaUik4HmG.name: Abyssal Ink

Othinni.name: Othinni

Pachinyam.description:
A single pachinyam isn't much of a threat but can be a nuisance around those who rely on technology. Some pachinyam owners take extra time to play with their pets after their daily dust baths, especially before entering a starship or other facility where an unexpected cloud of dust could have catastrophic consequences.

These dusty, long-eared fluffy burrowing rodents are native to Daimalko and emerged alongside the colossi during the Awakening 200 years ago. They were initially heralded as potential pets and affectionately referred to as "dust bunnies," but the survivors of the Awakening soon found the species were as dangerous as the colossi rampaging across the planet.

While one or two pachinyams behave as calm herbivores, they reproduce rapidly. When the pachinyam population reaches a tipping point, they become vicious predators. Their dust's ability to disrupt both visual and telecommunications makes it challenging for settlements to warn or organize against them. Outside civilization, the pachinyam population is kept in check by their swarms' instinctually drive to be near colossi despite the obvious danger. Some also hypothesize that the scent of a pachinyam swarm's dust cloud attracts hungry colossi.

LfkB9gJ95q2n8BJP.description: The pachinyam shakes it thick fur and releases a cloud of dust and dander in a @Template[type:burst|distance:5] radius centered on a corner of one of its squares that functions as a mist spell. This dust cloud blocks electronic communication to and from anyone inside the cloud. Any item with the tech trait becomes @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.6A2QDy8wRGCVQsSd]{Glitching 1} if it's inside the dust cloud. The pachinyam can't use this ability again until they take a dust bath as a 3-action activity with the move trait.
LfkB9gJ95q2n8BJP.name: Dusting

Pachinyam.name: Pachinyam

Pachinyam Swarm.description:
Pachinyam swarms can release a cloud of billowing dust as individual rodents constantly reapply dust to their comrades.

They were initially heralded as potential pets and affectionately referred to as "dust bunnies," but the survivors of the Awakening soon found the species were as dangerous as the colossi rampaging across the planet.

While one or two pachinyams behave as calm herbivores, they reproduce rapidly. When the pachinyam population reaches a tipping point, they become vicious predators. Their dust's ability to disrupt both visual and telecommunications makes it challenging for settlements to warn or organize against them. Outside civilization, the pachinyam population is kept in check by their swarms' instinctually drive to be near colossi despite the obvious danger. Some also hypothesize that the scent of a pachinyam swarm's dust cloud attracts hungry colossi.
