The pachinyam swarm shakes it thick fur and releases a cloud of dust and dander in a 30-foot radius burst centered on a corner of one of its squares that functions as a mist spell. This dust cloud blocks electronic communication to and from anyone inside the cloud. Any item with the tech trait becomes @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.6A2QDy8wRGCVQsSd]{Glitching 1} if it's inside the dust cloud.
Lxk4eawD7m2HMFxs.name: Dust

UkMVH1zSNaLheHow.description: Each enemy in the swarm's space takes @Damage[2d8[piercing]] damage (@Check[reflex|dc:20|basic] save). Creatures that fail this save are @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.fesd1n5eVhpCSS18]{Sickened 1} (@UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.fesd1n5eVhpCSS18]{Sickened 2} on a critical failure). While within a pachinyam's dust cloud and sickened, the creature is also suppressed until it leaves the cloud or recovers from the sickened condition.
UkMVH1zSNaLheHow.name: Swarming Bites

Pachinyam Swarm.name: Pachinyam Swarm

Paradox 17.description:
As Paradox 17 is normally invisible, most recorded observations of it start with hearing a roar "like static from a dead signal." All reports mention a profound yet hard-to-place sense of meaningfulness. One survivor saw it illuminated by a blast of light she described as "a spiral galaxy made up of shining eyes and glass feathers." Another described it as "dozens of interleaved wings scattered with embers." The only thing consistent about Paradox 17, however, is how deadly it can be if confronted directly.

Can you ever really know that the Universe you perceive exists? That you'll never awaken one day to find it was all a dream? A planet full of philosophers sought the answers to these questions once upon a time… shortly before they all vanished en masse. They left behind confusing records stating that the light of a "whirling star" revealed that physical matter had no substance and the Universe was secretly a mental prison. These records are all that remain from the first known encounter with the being known as Paradox 17.

8ijrjLPd8OmeaLci.description:
Paradox 17 burns away the fabric of reality with intense sunlight. If no creatures are observing Paradox 17, the light fills a @Template[type:cone|distance:60]. If any creature is observing Paradox 17, the area is a @Template[type:line|distance:60]. Creatures and unattended objects in the area turn temporarily translucent. Creatures in the area take @Damage[24d6[fire]|options:area-damage] damage and must attempt a @Check[reflex|dc:45] save. Paradox 17 can't use Waking Light again for [[/gmr 1d4 #Recharge Waking Light]]{1d4 rounds}.

Critical Success The target takes no damage.

Success The target takes half damage becomes @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.3uh1r86TzbQvosxv]{Doomed 1}.

Failure The target takes full damage and becomes @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.3uh1r86TzbQvosxv]{Doomed 2}.

Critical Failure The target takes double damage and becomes @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.3uh1r86TzbQvosxv]{Doomed 3}.
8ijrjLPd8OmeaLci.name: Waking Light

FSzsGKXCpUUsIRTv.description: Paradox 17 can move through all creatures, objects, and structures as though they were incorporeal.
FSzsGKXCpUUsIRTv.name: Disregard Reality

GST4tws15IFRhwgx.description: Paradox 17 is naturally invisible. It becomes visible only when using a hostile action.
GST4tws15IFRhwgx.name: Natural Invisibility

JKwSIJZU6bgO4IG8.description:
The target can understand all words regardless of language and also speak the languages of other creatures. When in a mixed group of creatures, each time the target speaks, it can choose a creature and speak in a language that creature understands, even if the target doesn't know what language that is.

Heightened (7th) The duration is 8 hours.
JKwSIJZU6bgO4IG8.name: Truespeech (constant)

OnYBF4vIJp1THNy7.description: Paradox 17 automatically and instantly learns and can observe the exact location of any creature on any plane that succeeds at a @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.actions.Item.1OagaWtBpVXExToo]{Recall Knowledge} check to learn any information about Paradox 17 or any creature who communicates information about Paradox 17 in any way. The ability to observe the creature and its surroundings, wherever the creature goes, lasts 1 hour.
OnYBF4vIJp1THNy7.name: Interdict Definition

Pv0g8IZlNCZIQyLw.description: 100 feet. When a creature in the aura observes Paradox 17 for the first time each day, it must attempt a @Check[will|dc:42] save or Performance check. On a failure, reality rejects the creature for as long as it can observe Paradox 17. The affected creature becomes hidden from all other creatures (except Paradox 17) as though invisible itself.
Pv0g8IZlNCZIQyLw.name: Reject Reality

pPQUZQI74b2MHUvA.description:
Frequency once per round

Trigger A creature would trigger Paradox 17's Reactive Strike, but it has no reactions remaining

Effect Paradox 17 Steps or Strikes prior to resolving the triggering action.
pPQUZQI74b2MHUvA.name: Causational Moments

v8KvsEVsS4f6UnOy.description:
Requirements Another creature is observing Paradox 17 or has triggered interdict definition in the last hour

Effect Paradox 17 teleports to any location that both Paradox 17 and the required creature can observe across any distance, even to another galaxy or plane.
v8KvsEVsS4f6UnOy.name: Bridge of Perception

Paradox 17.name: Paradox 17

Paradoxical Solipsist.description:
On six recorded occasions, individuals having prolonged contact with Paradox 17 continued to display anomalous behavior afterward. Two expressed belief they were dreaming, four that they were in a hostile simulation. One of these latter individuals insisted on "finding the light again" during an interview before walking through their guards and the holding cell wall, and they haven't been seen since.

Can you ever really know that the Universe you perceive exists? That you'll never awaken one day to find it was all a dream? A planet full of philosophers sought the answers to these questions once upon a time… shortly before they all vanished en masse. They left behind confusing records stating that the light of a "whirling star" revealed that physical matter had no substance and the Universe was secretly a mental prison. These records are all that remain from the first known encounter with the being known as Paradox 17.

blfTDd9ElE4mQ0k5.description: The solipsist deals an additional 2d6 precision damage to @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.AJh5ex99aV6VTggg]{Off-Guard} creatures, and on the first successful melee Strike they make against an off-guard creature each turn, the target must succeed at a @Check[will|dc:28] save or be @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.dfCMdR4wnpbYNTix]{Stunned 1} and @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.XgEqL1kFApUbl5Z2]{Blinded} while stunned.
blfTDd9ElE4mQ0k5.name: Baffling Attack

hQV8VzGnOrABlog3.description:
Flash Grenade (@Template[type:burst|distance:10], range 70 feet, tracking +1)

Effect @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.TkIyaNPgTZFBCCuh]{Dazzled} for 2 rounds on failure (@Check[fortitude|dc:26] save)
hQV8VzGnOrABlog3.name: Area Fire (Flash Grenade)

mM5Jx07eBW0gFPIk.description:
Trigger The solipsist succeeds at a Will save, or an attack against them is a critical failure

Effect The solipsist teleports up to 25 feet in any direction of their choice. Creatures adjacent to the solipsist after they teleport are @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.AJh5ex99aV6VTggg]{Off-Guard} to them until the end of the solipsist's next turn.
mM5Jx07eBW0gFPIk.name: Elude Consequences

x4AYlpydKXojoKZg.description: The solipsist treats all creatures, objects, and structures they're observing (except for Paradox 17) as quasi-illusory, allowing the solipsist to move through them as though the solipsist were incorporeal. They can also choose to use Will for any saving throw against any non-damaging effect.
x4AYlpydKXojoKZg.name: Perceive Unreality

Paradoxical Solipsist.name: Paradoxical Solipsist

Plasma Ooze.description:
Plasma oozes pose a significant menace to seasoned spacefarers within the Pact Worlds. These entities materialize as expansive networks of crackling electromagnetic energy, assuming a captivating spherical form pulsating with luminous hues of purple and blue, with searing white-hot bursts scattered throughout.

These oozes primarily lurk near the surface of stars but are also drawn to potent electromagnetic phenomena elsewhere in the Universe. The electromagnetic fields exuded by the ooze present dangers in space, potentially even incapacitating shielded starships. Armed scions connected to the Plane of Fire, known as the Sunkillers, claim to actively hunt these enigmatic beings, armed with specialized gear and sonic weaponry.

Oozes of many types lurk in dark and abandoned places across the galaxy, emerging only to satiate their appetites and threaten adventurers, explorers, and hapless workers alike.

EdB3IDaH66xj6K6b.description:
100 feet. When an item with the tech trait is activated inside the aura, it must succeed at a @Check[reflex|dc:36] save or become @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.6A2QDy8wRGCVQsSd]{Glitching 1} (@UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.6A2QDy8wRGCVQsSd]{Glitching 2} on a critical failure).

A tech creature that starts its turn within the aura must attempt a @Check[will|dc:35] save. If it fails, it becomes @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.6A2QDy8wRGCVQsSd]{Glitching 1} (@UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.6A2QDy8wRGCVQsSd]{Glitching 2} on a critical failure).

An item or creature that succeeds at this save becomes immune to this aura for 1 hour.
EdB3IDaH66xj6K6b.name: Electromagnetic Field

FlbvmKcwLcoOAHZG.description:
Frequency once per day

Effect each creature and wielded object with the tech trait within 100 feet of the plasma ooze must attempt a @Check[fortitude|dc:36] save. For each target that fails this save, the ooze regains @Damage[15[healing]] Hit Points and the object loses half of its remaining charges (if battery-powered).
FlbvmKcwLcoOAHZG.name: Plasma Drain

JJIauijtuZFZLhEm.description: The plasma ooze can sense all non-mindless creatures within the listed range.
JJIauijtuZFZLhEm.name: Thoughtsense

rXbUcESy22pVg9UY.description: Large and smaller creatures and all unattended objects within 100 feet must succeed at a @Check[reflex|dc:36] save or be pulled 15 feet toward the plasma ooze (30 feet on a critical failure).
rXbUcESy22pVg9UY.name: Magnetic Draw

ttVDCu8lswvDVgbn.description: A creature damaged by the ooze's pseudopod must succeed at a @Check[fortitude|dc:36] save or be @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.xYTAsEpcJE1Ccni3]{Slowed 1} (@UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.xYTAsEpcJE1Ccni3]{Slowed 2} on a critical failure). A creature with the tech trait uses the outcome one degree of success worse than the result of its roll.
ttVDCu8lswvDVgbn.name: Plasma Slag

Plasma Ooze.name: Plasma Ooze

Plasmazer.description:
Plasmazers are air elementals of vivid colors and grumpy disposition who became commonly found in the Universe after the invention of neon lighting. They manifest as dangerous explosions of light and color that shut down city grids, redirecting the power into a strobing neon kaleidoscope. They often take the shape of legendary birds or other creatures from local myths. Experimental club owners have tried harnessing plasmazers to produce special effects for their dance parties, but such situations usually end with dancers dodging plasma beams. The plasma slide is the name of a line dance that went viral after a plasmazer broke free at the Neon Crypt, an all-hours club on Eox with a reputation for rowdy fetes.

Elementals are energetic intrusions from the primal planes of existence. They take many forms, from mindless eddies in the wind or water to complex entities capable of wielding primal magic. The advent of space travel and the progress of technology have allowed even more living embodiments of the elements to manifest in the Universe.

Natural events like wildfires, solar storms, and floods can unleash hordes of unruly elementals on a planet or into a region of space. Sometimes, a gathering of powerful elementals causes a natural disaster on an epic scale, like an off-the-charts solar flare that fries a planet's power grid or a ceaseless storm swirling in a gas giant's atmosphere.

Nkte35QaV3ykxkx0.description:
Trigger The plasmazer takes electricity damage

Effect The plasmazer redirects the triggering effect to a creature within 30 feet. The creature attempts a @Check[reflex|dc:21] save. On failure, the creature takes an equal amount of electricity damage as the triggering effect.
Nkte35QaV3ykxkx0.name: Redirect Arc

bXCmbFv88T7aYxf1.description: A plasmazer emits bright light of their color in a 30-foot radius and dim light in the next 30 feet.
bXCmbFv88T7aYxf1.name: Tinted Glow

vxLHMqTQ7km52Z7E.description: The plasmazer Flies twice in a straight line, ignoring any creatures in their path as if the plasmazer is incorporeal. All creatures in or adjacent to the plasmazer's path take @Damage[4d6[electricity]] damage with a @Check[reflex|dc:21|basic] save. On critical failure, a creature also takes @Damage[2d6[persistent,fire]] damage and is @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.XgEqL1kFApUbl5Z2]{Blinded} for 1 round.
vxLHMqTQ7km52Z7E.name: Flash Strike

Plasmazer.name: Plasmazer

Presulea Midwife.description:
Presulea's mortal existence ended in self-sacrifice to feed the Newborn. Presulea was remade as a quivering mound of rampant growths and pumping organs that shimmer with vital energy.

Thirteen mortal Midwives attended the Newborn's birth and were transformed into eldritch beings by the nascent outer god's awakening. A Midwife always regenerates an identical new form so long as even a single speck of aucturnite—the name for the frozen chunks of planetcenta that once surrounded the Newborn—exists on this plane.

There are 13 types of Midwives, but their true numbers are unknown. Whether their names come from the mortal servants whose souls were the kindling for the Midwives' creation or have some other significance to the Newborn, also remains a mystery.

Each Midwife identifies themself by how they cared for the Newborn: if they swaddled, fed, carried, held, watched, warded, blessed, or performed other acts of nurturing for the outer god. The Midwives are powerful beings capable of transdimensional travel. They might be encountered in liminal spaces, such as the Drift or the Ghost Levels of Absalom Station, or they might be found among the clouds of aucturnite debris in the Gelid Edge. Their incomprehensible actions always advance the Newborn's inscrutable agenda—or their own.

The most well-known encounter the Pact Worlds have had with the Midwives took place in the immediate aftermath of the Newborn's birth. Amnieka, who swaddled the Newborn and has a hood of writhing tentacles around their visage, attacked Absalom Station directly, causing a massive power surge that threatened the lives of everyone on board. Chaos ensued, but a group of adventurers—who happened to be in the right elevator at the right time—found themselves in the station's Ghost Levels, where they thwarted Amnieka and prevented the Midwife from draining the station's reactors. The Midwives haven't acted so directly since that incident, but many suspect it's only a matter of time, and no one knows just how powerful the others might be.

Presulea treats a creature that casts such a spell as though they can always see it for 1 hour following the casting, ignoring the effects of any cover, concealment, invisibility, or similar effects.

Proog.description:
Proogs, unique among oozes, are cherished pets in many Pact Worlds households. These gentle, affable creatures are considered harmless in all but the worst of circumstances. Proogs quickly adapt to domestic life, are easily trained, and seem to delight in pleasing their owners with favored or humorous transformations. Late in their life cycle, these creatures reproduce by splitting in half without warning. Owners have noted that each resultant proog must relearn any tricks the original knew, leading researchers to conclude that the original proog is lost in the reproductive process.

Oozes of many types lurk in dark and abandoned places across the galaxy, emerging only to satiate their appetites and threaten adventurers, explorers, and hapless workers alike.

Protection-Class Security Robot.description:
These security robots are often constructed out of more durable materials than other robots, granting them the ability to protect their charges. Their bulky frames can be seen guarding important individuals or valuable items

Security robots are ubiquitous throughout industrialized space and have major presences in both the Pact Worlds and Veskarium, employed and customized by corporations and private citizens alike.

While most soldier robot models are built to be as destructive as possible, and elimination robots are designed to kill, security robots usually have fail-safes programmed into their behavior to prevent them from causing any more violence than is necessary to perform their designated security function. This makes them especially useful in cities, where unintended destruction might harm bystanders or cause legal issues, and even on starships, where a stray laser blast might cause serious damage to vital starship systems.

Upgrades: 1

The universal standard Pact Worlds model is highly modifiable and designed to function with a variety of accessories and upgrades, with wielders adapting the laser rifle to their preferences and even kit-bashing it into a nearly unrecognizable weapon.

Psychic Fungus Harvester.description:
In order to grow and spread, a sufficiently stable cluster of psychic fungi dispatches harvesters to collect nutrients. While most harvesters return with decaying animal and plant matter, the fungi's preferred prey are thinking creatures that they lead back to the colony for the elders' consumption.

A menace to every sentient being, psychic fungi are an invasive species that propagate by using the minds of sapient creatures. Psychic fungi that have integrated a higher intelligence can become a regional or even planetary threat.

Quaking Footfalls.description:
The footsteps of a kyokor (or other kaiju) shake the ground, causing the earth around it to tremble as though from a powerful earthquake.

When a kyokor passes by or through a settlement—or even attacks!—it leaves a trail of destruction that can be represented by the following hazards.

Terrifying, skyscraper-sized beasts roam the wastelands of Daimalko. Called colossi by the population, these monsters erupted from deep within the earth to stomp cities into dust, decimating the population and destroying every surface civilization on the planet in a terrifying Awakening. Kyokors are among the most dreaded colossi. There's no hope of defeating one without a valko—a war machine created by Daimalko's stubborn survivors to fight the colossi.
Quaking Footfalls.hazardDisable: @Check[athletics|dc:39] (trained), @Check[civil-engineering-lore|dc:39] (trained), or @Check[crafting|dc:39] (trained) to brace a small structure or surface to cancel the effects of the quake in that area, @Check[arcana|dc:41] (legendary), @Check[occultism|dc:41] (legendary), or @Check[performance|dc:41] (legendary) to calm or divert the kyokor; three total successes are required to disable the hazard; @Check[piloting|dc:30] (trained) if in a vehicle to avoid the kyokor's path (disables the hazard only for that vehicle)
Quaking Footfalls.hazardReset: The kyokor (or other kaiju) doesn't move this way again for [[/gmr 1d4 #rounds]]{1d4 rounds}.
Quaking Footfalls.name: Quaking Footfalls

Quyu.description:
At first look, quyus appears to be a small, adorable creatures, likely resembling a pet or helpless animal. This appearance is, however, a ploy meant to lure unsuspecting creatures into their grasp. Their true form is a two-headed twisted knot of flesh with eyeless sockets and gaping maws dripping with acid—and they're far from helpless.

Quyus can live without air, food, or water indefinitely. They have a dangerous combination of bottomless curiosity and complete lack of concern for other species' well-being. They originate from a now-Diasporan asteroid, though due to their disguises, they've spread to countless planets undetected, where they hunt and dissect creatures for their sadistic pursuits.

These solitary creatures prefer to observe an area's wild and domesticated species before infiltrating the peripheries of a civilization. There, they establish quiet cover identities, often as children's pets, only to capture and vivisect unsuspecting victims.

Quyus take on whatever appearance they believe is most likely to be considered cute by whatever beings inhabit their environments, even if the creature they mimic has no place in the world's ecology. They might take on the form of an adorable, mundane cat, rabbit, or similar fluffy creature, even in the middle of an asteroid mine or in the deep sea.

They have an automatic result of 35 on Deception checks and DCs to pass as the creature. While in this form, the quyu is Tiny and can't attack, and their pathetic gaze aura is active. The quyu can Dismiss this form.
30r8iC9Oax9YNlHb.name: Facade Form

A creature that ends its turn in the aura must attempt a @Check[will|dc:24] save or it becomes @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.AdPVz7rbaVSRxHFg]{Fascinated} by the quyu for 1 minute and takes a –2 circumstance penalty to attack the quyu for 1 round, even if the quyu leaves Facade Form.

Ranonek.description:
These enormous, bearlike vampiric beasts stalk the chilly jungle environments of Triaxus. While they hibernate most of the year, ranoneks awaken before deep freezes to catch beasts, dragons, or anything else migrating with the encroaching glaciers. With muscular, lean legs like a large cat, these white-furred predators use the tree line to hide from and ambush flying prey by leaping up to snatch them from midair. Using the hunted creatures' bodies to break the fall, ranoneks slam them into the ground below to reduce their insides to pulp before feeding on their blood.

A ranonek's digestive system utilizes several highly compressive tracts that allow them to squeeze the blood from smaller prey. When another meal tries to fly away, they can hock up and shoot the dried pellets containing the remains of their desiccated meals, knocking down prey before it gets too far away. Those documenting these remains have confirmed that these huge beasts prefer dragon prey over any other; this comes as no surprise given that ranoneks can drain many young dragons in under a minute and swallow entire dragonkin whole.

eLAfnxy4JiS7MHLs.description: The ranonek can detect blood inside creatures' bodies as an imprecise sense at the listed range. This is a precise sense against actively bleeding creatures.
eLAfnxy4JiS7MHLs.name: Bloodsense

A Large or smaller creature remains grabbed or @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.VcDeM8A5oI6VqhbM]{Restrained} by the ranonek even if the ranonek moves. If a ranonek would take falling damage while it has a creature grabbed, the grabbed creature takes the falling damage instead (in addition to any falling damage it would normally take).
lzG4TRNP6gNDV2vE.name: Bear Hug

ySZKG7cquC3BTYEs.description: The Ranonek Strides, Climbs, or Leaps twice (in any combination), then makes a claw or jaws Strike at the end of the movement. If it ends this movement by Leaping, the ranonek doesn't begin to fall until the end of the ranonek's turn, but it needs a solid surface to Leap from for each Leap.
ySZKG7cquC3BTYEs.name: Soaring Rush

Effect The ranonek sucks blood from the grabbed creature. This requires an Athletics check against the creature's Fortitude DC if the victim is grabbed and is automatic if the creature is restrained or if it took 50 or more damage since the start of the ranonek's last turn. The victim is @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.4D2KBtexWXa6oUMR]{Drained 1} until it receives healing (of any kind or amount), and the ranonek regains @Damage[25[healing]] Hit Points, gaining any excess Hit Points as temporary Hit Points that last for 1 minute.

Ravenous Drake.description:
Ravenous drakes are a singular variant among drakes due to their lack of a propulsive breath weapon. They were bred into near domestication for their relatively small size and powerful inhaling maw. Frontier colonies and deep-space exploration firms often rely on ravenous drakes instead of felines or other pest-control creatures.

When found in the wild, ravenous drakes are familial and fiercely territorial, often roving in large packs. Within the structure of civilization or alongside a sentient species, a ravenous drake's territorialism and familial tendencies manifest as a true bond of loyalty to their companion.

Drakes resemble their larger draconic cousins in more than just scaled, monstrous acclaim. Ranging in size from the diminutive fey drake to the massive, ship-sized star drake, drakes share a dragons' winged reptilian form, long necks, and breath weapons. But where dragons often have forelimbs and wings, a drake typically only has one or the other. Their long, winding tails and sharp jaws more than make up for this lack, however.

Despite being more animalistic than dragons, drakes still possess a formidable cunning, and most share a dragon's ability to generate some form of breath weapon. However, their lack of intelligence makes drakes substantially easier to domesticate than other draconic creatures, and their familial nature makes them excellent pack hunters.

TT4lgmJl4fuIHaer.description:

Effect The ravenous drake draws breath into its powerful lungs to drag prey into its maw. Each creature in a @Template[type:cone|distance:15] must succeed at a @Check[fortitude|dc:16] save or be pulled up to 10 feet closer to the drake. If at least one creature ends this forced movement adjacent to the drake, the drake can make a jaws Strike against that creature. If this Strike is a critical success, the creature is also grabbed in the drake's jaws.
TT4lgmJl4fuIHaer.name: Suction Vortex

Ravenous Drake.name: Ravenous Drake

Rendworm.description: A parasitic creature from the edge of the Pact Worlds, the rendworm has a sinuous, undulating body and fine quills that run in a frill down its back. Blue gray in color, it blends in with the frigid surroundings of its home territory, making it easy to overlook when setting up campsites. The short-lived creature needs a living host for its reproductive cycle and uses a chilling neurotoxin to paralyze, infect, and spread.

Repair-Class Security Robot.description:
On many scrappy starships and remote space stations, it's hard to afford dedicated security robots, especially if you can't manage to secure a license to own them in the first place. Most such operations rely on cheap maintenance bots to step up and repel intruders—they might not get the job done against serious threats, but they might be able to take out common vermin before they can cause too much damage to the starship's circuitry. After all, sometimes the best maintenance is preventive maintenance.

Security robots are ubiquitous throughout industrialized space and have major presences in both the Pact Worlds and Veskarium, employed and customized by corporations and private citizens alike.

While most soldier robot models are built to be as destructive as possible, and elimination robots are designed to kill, security robots usually have fail-safes programmed into their behavior to prevent them from causing any more violence than is necessary to perform their designated security function. This makes them especially useful in cities, where unintended destruction might harm bystanders or cause legal issues, and even on starships, where a stray laser blast might cause serious damage to vital starship systems.

wCfkobDVQSb6oNBj.description: The robot sprays a torrent of water that functions as @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.spells.Item.jfVCuOpzC6mUrf6f]{Hydraulic Push} (1st-rank, DC 16). The robot must refill its tanks after using this ability.
wCfkobDVQSb6oNBj.name: Fire Suppressor

Trigger A creature targets the security robot with an attack

Effect The robot overclocks its processing power to attempt to avoid an attack, gaining a +2 circumstance bonus to its AC against the triggering attack.
zihVtY9YWW6WBmp4.name: Exigency

Repair-Class Security Robot.name: Repair-Class Security Robot

Rivarin Endling.description:
Rivarins were furry, flat-toothed, three-eyed quadrupedal herbivores ranched as pack beasts by a feudal society on wintry Destalon-2. Rivarins were brought to extinction alongside their fledgling society by jinsuls. The jinsuls fled soon after, reportedly following attacks by ghostly giants with jagged fangs and baleful red eyes.

Every species follows a natural arc as it emerges and evolves: rising, thriving, declining, and falling into extinction. When extremely unnatural ends to these paths occur—when unexpected predation, industrialization, or alien pathogens wipe out a population—endlings are born. These spectral members of extinct species typically develop as "answers" to their eradication. Xenobiologists differ on what creates endlings, unable to confirm whether the creatures are a species' last collective sorrow made manifest or just vengeful individual spirits—the last lights to go out.

3NMSyag7gpNokLhk.description: A rivarin endling can sense the presence of bleeding, frightened, or wounded creatures as a precise sense at the listed range.
3NMSyag7gpNokLhk.name: Warsight

Success The creature is @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 1}.

Failure The creature is @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 2} and must spend the first action of its next turn @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.sDPxOjQ9kx2RZE8D]{Fleeing}.

Robotic Advanced War Machine.description:
Strong and ferocious, code name "thermatrod" is designed to maximize carnage and destruction on a battlefield. In contrast, the "vracinea" is among the weakest of the unidentified biotech war machines observed in the Pact Worlds. Sleek and stealthy, it darts in and out of enemy defenses while transmitting data to its pilot before departing. If discovered, the vracinea consumes itself to destroy records of the data it was carrying.

The incursion began with a series of probes detected by anacites on Aballon. Strange machines with blazing sensors and articulated tentacles appeared out of nowhere, ripping through infrastructure seemingly at random and collecting intelligence all around Pact Worlds space. Panic spread fast, but since the machines always vanished without a trace, or exploded when captured, the sightings couldn't be confirmed or identified. Rumors began to circulate that the machines were a form of biotech never encountered before. Soon the Stewards became formally involved, shuttering the incidents behind the adamantine partition of top security clearance.

In Sarenith of 325 ag, after dozens of military operations failed to engage the elusive probes, a wing of fighters dispatched from the Idari finally got lucky and disabled one of the machines before it could self-destruct. Coaxed into giving up some of its secrets by top Pact Worlds scientists, the biotech vessel became the prototype for the "home grown" remote war machines that are currently being tested for use in combat. The replicas aren't alive but are built using robotic construction templates since the core of the original biotech design has proven too complicated to reverse engineer with Pact technology.

Remote war machines are proxies that can be controlled from a great distance. The original biotech war machines connect to the pilot's mind through a psychic link or unknown radio frequency. Robotic remote war machines connect to a computer via data link, allowing the pilot to control their proxy using a keyboard, virtual reality rig, or even a vidgame controller.

Sapient Green Orb.description:
Sapient green orbs only recently appeared in Pact Worlds space, and wherever they appear, purple orbs are nowhere to be found. While the history and relationship between these orbs is unclear, scholars have at least discerned they communicate using the same language and share similar physiology. Their behavior, on the other hand, is quite different from purple orbs; they shun contact with others, rarely make friends, and lie whenever possible, though they aren't especially good at deception, much in the same way purple orbs aren't especially good at diplomacy, despite their best efforts. Some scholars have begun to expect that these two types of orb are somehow enemies of one another, though no records of conflict between them exist, and no sapient orb seems eager to discuss the other type in depth. Green orbs' tendency to lie about most topics further complicates the study of sapient orbs and their apparent enmity.

Sapient green orbs are 3 feet in diameter, much like sapient purple orbs, but if asked about their size (or just about any other trait), they always state something slightly inaccurate—three-and-a-half feet, two feet and four inches—whatever they think will be more impressive or confusing for whoever they're addressing. The only trait they never lie about is their color (they all insist that every sapient green orb is exactly the same shade of green, which isn't quite true; there are slight variations). They'll gladly argue about the exact shade of green with anyone around. More than one person has theorized, after such an encounter, that sapient green orbs somehow draw sustenance from engaging others in pointless arguments, but it's more likely they don't need sustenance at all and simply enjoy such pursuits.

When a sapient green orb feels they're about to lose an argument, they typically resort to using Excandescent Flash, then fly away.

These enigmatic, orb-shaped beings seem to have no home world, organized society, traditions, or religion. Sightings of the orbs are sporadic—they briefly appear in large numbers, then vanish for a year or more, only to reappear in an entirely different region of space for a few months. Scholars and friends of the orbs have noticed that each time the orbs appear, their numbers have diminished.

Sapient orbs occasionally form permanent bonds, merging three to six orbs (always of the same type, as far as anyone knows) into a cluster called a luminant. Only sapient orbs at advanced stages of their life cycle can form such clusters, and the merge is permanent and irrevocable. Luminants are highly intelligent but far more reclusive than other sapient orbs, making it difficult to discern their motivations or purpose in sapient orb society.

Sapient Purple Orb.description:
Purple orbs are curious, social beings who unfailingly attempt to make contact with any life-form they encounter, though these attempts are frequently inept. Few other creatures understand their ancient language, so purple orbs instead use magic, telepathy, minor illusions, and flashes of light and flowing mist from their 3-foot-diameter luminous bodies.

Purple orbs are eager for cooperation and solidarity with their chosen friends and family, whether those are other sapient orbs or completely different beings, making it relatively easy to befriend them—or deceive them. Purple orbs are devout supporters and defenders of their companions, flinging themselves bodily into the fray if a friend is in danger. They become a deep dark purple as they grow more emotional in the heat of conflict (violent or otherwise), though their emotions rarely grow so intense that they're willing to take another being's life. That purple orbs seem to value their own lives less than those of their friends might be among the reasons that the number of sapient purple orbs in the universe seems to be dwindling.

Scavenger Slime.description:
For longer than anyone can remember, scavenger slimes have been found all over the galaxy. They hitch rides on starships, drift among wrecks and meteors, and lay hidden in junkyards. Their only goal: to repair everything they can get their protoplasm on. Scavenger slimes are believed to be an accidental marriage of technology and magic, built by an extremely advanced civilization as an all-purpose repair gel, only to develop rudimentary sentience and outlive their creators.

These creatures have an instinctive drive to repair and rebuild nearly any technological item they encounter. Using their extremely malleable bodies, which excrete a highly specialized resin, scavenger slimes can repair even exceedingly complex pieces of technology. They intuitively understand how to shield themselves from harm and how to operate any weapon they manage to find, aggressively using such armaments to drive any and all creatures away from their never-ending repair work.

Oozes of many types lurk in dark and abandoned places across the galaxy, emerging only to satiate their appetites and threaten adventurers, explorers, and hapless workers alike.

7edcnn43264BKjAM.description: A scavenger slime builds a shell for itself from discarded pieces of technology and a secretion of natural resin. This grants the ooze Hardness. Once the scavenger slime is reduced to half its Hit Points or immediately after being damaged by a critical hit, the scavenger shell breaks, removing its Hardness and reducing its Armor Class to 22.
7edcnn43264BKjAM.name: Scavenger Shell

9elq82zfzrv6BQw9.description: A scavenger slime can incorporate up to three weapons into its protoplasmic body, gaining proficiency with each. These weapons are treated as integrated weapons and are powered by the scavenger slime's own technomagical nature without needing to reload.

Shimmerstone sentinels are created from shimmerstone, an empathic mineral mined on the planet Vesk-8 that has a calming effect on those around it. Shimmerstone sentinels can absorb powerful emotions, which they infuse into their own bodies to empower their attacks.

Shipbreaker.description:
Shipbreakers are bullet-shaped chunks of living steel crackling with electricity from their plasma fields. Shipbreakers propel themselves through space, seeking faint electronic signals emitted by starships. After tracking a target, shipbreakers slam into the starship using a powerful breach maneuver and then rip through the hull to get at the crew inside, ingesting passengers, components, and cargo in a vicious gulp that fuels their interplanetary predation.

Shipbreakers are especially attracted to batteries and even prioritize eating a fully charged battery over a more nutritious living creature. These batteries remain a permanent component of shipbreakers, storing and retrieving excess caloric energy from the elementals. Shipbreakers that have ingested a tremendous amount of batteries over their long existences often glow from the inside or crackle with electricity.

Elementals are energetic intrusions from the primal planes of existence. They take many forms, from mindless eddies in the wind or water to complex entities capable of wielding primal magic. The advent of space travel and the progress of technology have allowed even more living embodiments of the elements to manifest in the Universe.

Natural events like wildfires, solar storms, and floods can unleash hordes of unruly elementals on a planet or into a region of space. Sometimes, a gathering of powerful elementals causes a natural disaster on an epic scale, like an off-the-charts solar flare that fries a planet's power grid or a ceaseless storm swirling in a gas giant's atmosphere.

Critical Success The creature is unaffected and becomes temporarily immune to plasmashock for 1 hour.

Success The creature becomes @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.AJh5ex99aV6VTggg]{Off-Guard} and loses its reactions until the start of its next turn. If the creature has the tech trait or the shipbreaker was attacked by a tech weapon, the creature or weapon becomes glitching 1.

Failure The creature is @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.dfCMdR4wnpbYNTix]{Stunned 1}. If the creature has the tech trait or the shipbreaker was attacked by a tech weapon, the creature or weapon becomes glitching 2.

Critical Failure As failure, but @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.dfCMdR4wnpbYNTix]{Stunned 2} and glitching 3.
HRvxjqJQJHmoCIGC.name: Plasmashock

VljJEEjjhPC12urs.description: A shipbreaker can detect creatures and items with the tech trait as an imprecise sense at the listed range.
VljJEEjjhPC12urs.name: Techsense

pjjO3F53mj0RPBTH.description: While in space, the shipbreaker can sense electronic signals from starships in the same star system. While it can't necessarily interpret starship signals, it has a vague sense of the intent or purpose of any given starship signal, such as "to scan," "to communicate," or "to warn of danger."
pjjO3F53mj0RPBTH.name: Electroreception

wMogXXyHuCkqELeD.description: The shipbreaker Flies, then Leaps vertically up to 25 feet, plus a cumulative 25 feet for each consecutive round the shipbreaker uses this ability, and makes a jaws Strike against a creature at any point during the jump. In low gravity, the shipbreaker Leaps 100 feet high the first round it jumps, cumulatively multiplied by 4 each consecutive round if trying to reach escape velocity to leave the surface of a planet (which requires 5 consecutive rounds of using Atmospheric Breach in a low-gravity environment).
wMogXXyHuCkqELeD.name: Atmospheric Breach

Shipbreaker.name: Shipbreaker

Sihedron Guard Specialist.description: While all Aeon Guards swear an oath of allegiance to the Aeon Throne, Sihedron Guard specialists are conditioned from a young age to be utterly devoted to Lissala—and thus to high priest Ishmerai Ophir. Such is their devotion that, the first time they die each year, a brilliant display of green lightning forms the Sihedron symbol in the air above them, preventing their death and allowing them to continue to fight in Lissala's name. Whether this boon is granted by Ishmerai or a direct gift from Lissala is unknown, but no one dares to question a Sihedron Guard specialist's devotion or deadly skill.

41RaYXdsM75PdZgc.description: The Sihedron Guard specialist makes a ranged Strike with their aeon rifle or a melee strike with their battleglove, then Casts a Spell requiring 2 actions or fewer against the same target. If the spell requires an attack roll, don't count the ranged or melee Strike toward the multiple attack penalty.
41RaYXdsM75PdZgc.name: Battle Casting

7Te7Z1gj1O760YFw.description:
Frequency once per year

Trigger The Sihedron Guard specialist is reduced to 0 Hit Points, but not from an effect that leaves no remains (like the promession spell)

Effect The Sihedron Guard specialist regains @Damage[5d8[healing]] Hit Points and doesn't fall @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.j91X7x0XSomq8d60]{Prone} or drop their equipment.
7Te7Z1gj1O760YFw.name: Reward of Obedience

CmzoKP5yEE8hsGVx.description:
Upgrades: 0

These decorative suits of medium armor feature exaggerated shoulder guards, stylized dragon wings, and draconic emblems across the breastplate's back and chest. Skyfire armor is often plated with gold or other attractive metals, sacrificing upgrade space for style.
CmzoKP5yEE8hsGVx.name: Advanced Sihedron Guard Armor

caMeuZclNIv2qusv.description:
Trigger The Sihedron Guard specialist is reduced to 0 Hit Points and has used their Reward of Obedience reaction in the last year. A Sihedron Guard must use this ability when the trigger is met

Effect The Sihedron Guard specialist is utterly destroyed, leaving behind only equipment. Their soul can't be restored, and no magical means can contact their soul.
caMeuZclNIv2qusv.name: Punishment For Failure

nCdUX14SmUTeJEaV.description: A Sihedron Guard specialist who makes a Strike while adjacent to another member of the Sihedron Guard gains a +4 circumstance bonus to damage rolls for that attack.
nCdUX14SmUTeJEaV.name: Virtue in Service

Sihedron Guard Specialist.name: Sihedron Guard Specialist

Sihedron Guard Thunderstriker.description: Sihedron Guard thunderstrikers, so named for one of their most common forms of attack, serve as air support for units of Aeon and Sihedron Guards. They bombard enemies with magic and explosives to force their targets out of defensive positions and into firing range for the rest of their squad. They also frequently execute extraction missions, whether getting an important asset to safety or capturing an enemy for interrogation.

7ir93Hymw6bhGj0E.description: The aeon guard Flies using their jetpack, tracing arcane sigils through the air with their motion to empower their spells. If the next action the aeon guard uses is to Cast a Spell that has a range, increase that spell's range by 30 feet. In addition, if the spell requires an attack roll or a Reflex save, any targets of the spell that have lesser cover reduce the bonuses they gain from cover by 1 against the spell.
7ir93Hymw6bhGj0E.name: Navigational Spellshape

PrwxWJhqO0NzL51o.description: undermounted frag grenade (@Template[type:burst|distance:10], consumable, range 30 feet, tech, tracking +1), Damage @Damage[2d8[piercing]|options:area-damage] damage (@Check[reflex|dc:23|basic] save; @Damage[1d4[persistent,bleed]|options:area-damage] damage on critical failure)
PrwxWJhqO0NzL51o.name: Launch

nvJrPV9p9BUel91h.description:
@UUID[Compendium.sf2e.spells.Item.zDJS8E66UI0himqV]{Thunderstrike}

These latticed gemstones are suspended in a silicon casing and encoded with the magical script necessary to cast a single, specific spell. Casting a spell from a spell gem requires holding the gem in one hand and activating it with a Cast a Spell activity using the normal number of actions for that spell. The spell must appear on your spell list. Because you're the one Casting the Spell, use your spell attack modifier and spell DC. The spell must be of your spellcasting tradition. The spell in a spell gem can be cast only once, and the spell gem is destroyed as part of the casting. Spell gems can't contain cantrips or rituals. The traits for this item vary based on the spell it contains.

Activate Cast a Spell

Effect You Cast the Spell at the indicated rank.
nvJrPV9p9BUel91h.name: Spell Gem of Thunderstrike (Rank 3)

Sihedron Guard Thunderstriker.name: Sihedron Guard Thunderstriker

Skarak.description:
The skarak is a ravenous mass of spiked chitin and teeth propelled with frightening speed by a collection of spindly, arachnid legs. It rampages across its territories, consuming everything smaller than itself and taking delight in the destruction it leaves in its wake. It's difficult to hide from a skarak, as it'll rip down fortifications and smash through concrete walls to get at prey cowering inside buildings. It's even more difficult to run from a skarak since it can spit a corrosive webbing that magically binds its prey to itself, allowing it to pull its prey across any distance to within reach of its waiting maw.

A skarak possesses a terrible cunning to complement its destructive might. It often watches a targeted settlement for days, analyzing defenses before launching a devastating offensive. It's typically a solitary creature except when training a newly hatched brood to hunt. During this period, it ranges ahead of its young, rampaging through densely populated areas and leaving wounded, weakened targets behind it. Survivors of the initial rampage soon discover they aren't the lucky ones as the skarak young come after, devouring all in their path.

5xu7Jb7MjWSvPFf8.description: A creature hit by a skarak's etheric web is @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.kWc1fhmv9LBiTuei]{Grabbed} by the skarak. The creature isn't @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.eIcWbB5o3pP6OIMe]{Immobilized}, but it can't move beyond the maximum range of the skarak's etheric web. A creature can sever the etheric web with a Strike against AC 30 that deals at least 18 fire or force damage. This deals no damage to the skarak.
5xu7Jb7MjWSvPFf8.name: Etheric Tether

6YBw1cwBcvTXqK4w.description: The skarak makes a horn Strike against each creature within reach. These attacks count toward the skarak's multiple attack penalty, but the multiple attack penalty doesn't increase until after the skarak makes all these attacks.
6YBw1cwBcvTXqK4w.name: Rampage

EMUQhPt9T9ipHaPA.description:
Requirements A creature is @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.kWc1fhmv9LBiTuei]{Grabbed} by the skarak's etheric tether

Effect The creature must succeed at a @Check[will|dc:33] save or be teleported to a space adjacent to the skarak of the skarak's choosing. This ends the grabbed condition from etheric tether unless the creature critically fails the save.
EMUQhPt9T9ipHaPA.name: Tether Pull

lYnyIKeFyKUoTm6w.description: A skarak's horn Strike bypasses the Hardness of structures made primarily of wood, stone, and metal.
lYnyIKeFyKUoTm6w.name: Destructive

Skarak.name: Skarak

Skreeling.description:
Skreelings hunt in packs and can subsist on ash, metal, wood, or near anything else.

Skreesires, and their offspring skreelings, are vicious predators who skulk and prowl in the crags and caverns of the cosmos.

6H0JByZGOcLCEOUU.description: The skreeling's melee Strikes deal 1d4 persistent bleed damage to creatures within reach of one or more other skreelings.
6H0JByZGOcLCEOUU.name: Cluster Attack

Skreeling.name: Skreeling

Skreesire.description:
Skreesires are reptilian monstrosities with a formidable will, razor-sharp teeth, and nonfunctional wings atop a mass of ambulatory tentacles.

Skreesires, and their offspring skreelings, are vicious predators who skulk and prowl in the crags and caverns of the cosmos.

WYAdhuIG9LQlklLy.description:
Requirements The skreesire is in rocky terrain

Effect Until the next time they act, the skreesire resembles rocky terrain. They have an automatic result of 29 on @Check[deception] checks and DCs to pass as rocky terrain.
WYAdhuIG9LQlklLy.name: Camouflage

lkwaX8ixjNdqvdrA.description:
Effect A target within 30 feet hears a telepathic manifestation of the skreesire's will and must attempt a @Check[will|dc:22] save.

Failure The creature must use the first action of its next turn to Stride toward the skreesire.

Critical Failure The creature must use all its actions on its next turn to Stride toward the skreesire; when it's adjacent to the skreesire, it drops @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.j91X7x0XSomq8d60]{Prone} and ends its turn.
lkwaX8ixjNdqvdrA.name: Enthrall

Skreesire.name: Skreesire

Snoop-Class Infiltrator Robot.description:
Not a front-line combatant, an infiltrator robot's primary tactic is to quietly enter a location, use its sleeping gas bombs to disable those guarding its target, and collect its payload. The leadership of the Pact Worlds found that the snoop-class infiltrator robot could have other, darker tasks during the Silent War: its reactive camouflage could help it transport deadly explosives to sabotage ships, shipyards, and other military installations.

Brought to the forefront during the war against the Veskarium, and further perfected by various corporate interests within the Pact Worlds, infiltrator robots are known for being able to get into places where no one else could. Generally small and agile, infiltrator robots sneak into enemy territory and either download precious data or record incriminating evidence.

C5rq5TeKaVAHe1sx.description: You need an infiltrator's toolkit to @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.actions.Item.2EE4aF4SZpYf0R6H]{Pick Locks} or @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.actions.Item.cYdz2grcOcRt4jk6]{Disable Devices} (of some types) using the Thievery skill.
C5rq5TeKaVAHe1sx.name: Integrated Infiltrator's Toolkit (Commercial)

GalCqJK006J7qkuu.description:
Upgrades: 1

This high-tech crossbow uses a series of pistons to propel bolts along its barrel. These quiet-firing semiautomatic weapons are popular in high-density settlements where gunfire might cause a panic.
GalCqJK006J7qkuu.name: Integrated Commercial Crossbolter

VwgERY2caHDBSzsh.description: The robot comes packaged with photosensitive reflectors on its exterior panels. It can [[/act hide]] even without cover or concealment.
VwgERY2caHDBSzsh.name: Reactive Camouflage

W0rQJlDj2c6TmE0Q.description:
The infiltrator robot fires a bomb within 30 feet that disperses sleeping gas in a @Template[type:burst|distance:10]. Each creature in the area must attempt a @Check[fortitude|dc:18] save.

Critical Success The creature is unaffected.

Success The creature takes a –1 status penalty to Perception checks for 1 round.

Failure The creature falls @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.fBnFDH2MTzgFijKf]{Unconscious}. If it's still unconscious after 1 minute, it wakes up automatically.

Critical Failure The creature falls unconscious. If it's still unconscious after 1 hour, it wakes up automatically.
W0rQJlDj2c6TmE0Q.name: Sleeping Gas Bomb

hZ3JA43iAYqjtQkh.description: A hacking toolkit is required for Computers checks to Hack computers. You can use a hacking toolkit to access a computer without using a user interface, but this requires physical contact with the computer or contact via an infosphere or a similar linked network.
hZ3JA43iAYqjtQkh.name: Integrated Hacking Toolkit (Commercial)

Snoop-Class Infiltrator Robot.name: Snoop-Class Infiltrator Robot

Spined Renkroda.description:
Thickly built and burly, spined renkrodas live on open plains, mesas, and plateaus. Unlike most renkrodas, their frill is a deadly weapon, lined with hundreds of foot-long spines that serve as an excellent defense—and a deadly weapon.

Renkrodas are a family of large dinosaur-like predators native to the planet Castrovel. They've spread beyond the jungle planet's boundaries thanks to smugglers, poachers, and ultra-wealthy big-game hunters. Bipedal and strong with long necks and decorative spines, renkrodas are best known for their terrifying roars, which they bellow frequently as a form of long-range communication and to scare away other predators and scavengers. Over a dozen species of renkrodas exist, each specially adapted to their environment or ecological niche.

R6Bycds8pbGXT6za.description: The spined renkroda makes three ranged spine Strikes.
R6Bycds8pbGXT6za.name: Spine Barrage

dP9TzUqlYBxaPGkI.description: The spined renkroda bristles its spines and adopts a defensive posture, gaining a +2 circumstance bonus to AC until it uses a move action, uses Spine Deflection, or makes any Strike other than a spine Strike. Any creature that attempts a melee attack against the spined renkroda takes @Damage[3d6[piercing]] damage, regardless of whether the attack hits.
dP9TzUqlYBxaPGkI.name: Bristle

mowMOK1bouo9yjSz.description:
Requirements The spined renkroda's spines are bristled

Trigger The spined renkroda would be hit by a ranged Strike, but the damage hasn't been rolled yet

Effect The spined renkroda twists its body, deflecting part of the attack with its spines, and gains resistance 10 to the triggering damage. Its spines are no longer bristled.
mowMOK1bouo9yjSz.name: Spine Deflection

vh8ALXaGq2XE0Pxp.description:
The spined renkroda bellows ferociously. Each non-renkroda creature within 60 feet must attempt a @Check[will|dc:32] save. The creature is then temporarily immune for 10 minutes.

Critical Success The creature is unaffected.

Success The creature is @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 1}.

Failure The creature is @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 2}.

Critical Failure The creature is @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 3}.
vh8ALXaGq2XE0Pxp.name: Terrifying Roar

Spined Renkroda.name: Spined Renkroda

Squox.description:
The tiny vulkarikis are a common animal in the Pact Worlds, originating from the planet Castrovel. Human explorers from Lost Golarion gave them the name "squox," as they interpreted the creatures as being a mix of fox and squirrel. Squoxes are cunning to the point of being devious and employ scare tactics to routinely abscond with shiny items they uncover on their travels. They exhibit complex social behaviors, including a distinct hierarchy between individuals in a skulk, and have a vast vocal repertoire used to assign signature sounds to different individual squoxes.

Having long since been exported from the Pact Worlds, squoxes are found throughout the galaxy, with many civilizations in Near Space maintaining growing communities of these tiny furry creatures, much to the growing consternation of the Xenowardens who worry that the highly adaptable squox has become an invasive species in several biomes. While some advocate for culling these populations, the popularity of the animal as a pet has made this view an incredibly unpopular stance.

Young squoxes are referred to as kits and can be purchased from the open market on most Pact Worlds. Squoxes tend to live for about 10 years. A typical squox weighs about 10 pounds and is about 3 feet long, with much of its length being its tail. Squoxes come in all colorations, and many even take on unique environmental adaptations to specific climates, such as desert-dwelling squoxes growing longer ears to help disperse heat.

yqoAwJbrV1SIXbbh.description: A squox can [[/act disarm skill=acrobatics]] and [[/act trip skill=acrobatics]] creatures with its tail using Acrobatics instead of Athletics, even if it doesn't have a free hand. A squox can attempt to Disarm or Trip @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.AJh5ex99aV6VTggg]{Off-Guard} creatures up to two sizes larger than it and gains a +2 circumstance bonus to Disarm or Trip an off-guard target
yqoAwJbrV1SIXbbh.name: Squox Tricks

Squox.name: Squox

WiOLLZ7fx5vFpMJp.description: The biotech of a biotech zombie can be disabled for 1 hour by a creature that succeeds at a @Check[medicine|dc:18] of Life Science Lore check. Attempting to do so can typically be done only while within reach of the zombie and is a 2-action activity that has the manipulate trait. A biotech zombie with disabled biotech is @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.xYTAsEpcJE1Ccni3]{Slowed 1} and can't use any reactions.
WiOLLZ7fx5vFpMJp.name: Biotech

dR0jqJMGfnaZW2Vq.description: The biotech zombie breathes a blast of flame that deals @Damage[4d6[fire]|options:area-damage] damage in a @Template[type:cone|distance:15] (@Check[reflex|dc:18|basic] save). The zombie can't use Dragon Gland again for [[/gmr 1d4 #Recharge Dragon Gland]]{1d4 rounds}.
dR0jqJMGfnaZW2Vq.name: Dragon Gland

dScQI1J1iUmapej0.description:
A biotech zombie must use this reaction unless its biotech is disabled

Trigger The zombie is reduced to 0 Hit Points

Effect The zombie melts into a caustic pool of biological goo, dealing @Damage[2d8[acid]|options:area-damage] damage in a @Template[type:emanation|distance:10] (@Check[reflex|dc:18|basic] save) and making that area hazardous terrain for 1 minute (1 acid damage). This ability destroys any organic items on the zombie (including biotech).
dScQI1J1iUmapej0.name: Genetic Instability

Sterieid.description:
Sterieids reside on asteroids, relishing the beauty of their rocky, icy surfaces. Due to the ubiquity of asteroids, sterieids are the most common type of space nymph. Since many asteroids exist near one another in asteroid belts, sterieids are more likely to form communities among their own kind than other nymphs. Conversely, they tend to be wary of outsiders, despite visitors being less of a novelty. Those sterieids who desire company, however, build way stations on their asteroids for passing starships, offering food, amenities, and information about the local system.

Mining is a contentious issue for sterieids, who usually react with hostility to such operations. Most mining corporations will survey an asteroid to ensure it isn't protected by a sterieid before setting up shop, though less ethical companies have been known to pay mercenaries to "relocate" sterieid guardians of asteroids that contain valuable resources.

Nymphs are beautiful fey who appear as humanoids with elven features. They generally take female forms, but nymphs of all genders and presentations exist. While many nymphs live on planets and act as protectors of natural ponds, forests, caves, and cliffsides, other nymphs—often called space nymphs—are known for their association with celestial bodies. Like their planet-bound kin, space nymphs guard their bonded territories from exploitation or harm.

As admirers of the arts, nymphs are especially friendly toward creatives, and offering to depict a nymph in story, picture, or song is a sure way to win their favor—unless the nymph doesn't like the final result and lashes out at the artist for insulting them with a mediocre product. Vidcasting and livestreaming are popular pastimes among more sociable nymphs, whether to show off their remote environments or find audiences for performances. Some nymphs entice movie crews to film in their territories, with two provisos: first, that the production not damage the environment, and second, that the nymph receive a prominent role in the film.

Unless their territories are threatened, most space nymphs are friendly or indifferent to mortals, but they have long memories. Anyone visiting a space nymph's territory would be wise to research that nymph's grudges, past encounters with mortals, or any recent events in the area that might color the nymph's perspective of those traveling near their home.

A mortal who demonstrates the right attitude and abilities, such as by protecting a stellar body from destruction or creating an especially beautiful work of art, might draw a space nymph's attention. From time to time, space nymphs will offer their services as mentors to solarians or mystics, though they seldom seek pupils on their own. Space nymphs rarely enter into more than one such arrangement at a time and typically only make commitments that promise to last decades or centuries, so they're extremely selective in their choice of mentee.

0gQrocHyD6aET4Ty.description: 10 feet. A sterieid's body radiates an icy chill. Creatures entering or starting their turns in the aura take @Damage[2d6[cold]] damage (@Check[fortitude|dc:21|basic] save); a creature that critically fails its save is also @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.i3OJZU2nk64Df3xm]{Clumsy 1} until the start of its next turn as it grows sluggish from the cold.
0gQrocHyD6aET4Ty.name: Icy Nimbus

Mf6U543YfznJPZgl.description:
Trigger The sterieid takes physical damage

Effect Shards of rocky debris fly off the sterieid's body, dealing @Damage[2d12[bludgeoning]] damage to all adjacent creatures (@Check[reflex|dc:21|basic] save) and giving the sterieid the @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.DmAIPqOBomZ7H95W]{Concealed} condition until the end of their next turn.
Mf6U543YfznJPZgl.name: Debris Field

TeaCW8c3BIBYPfBO.description: While on their bonded celestial body, a nymph can sense approaching starships within a day's travel from the celestial body. This doesn't give them any information about the ship, its occupants, or its exact position. The nymph can send a message to the ship as if using a personal comm unit.
TeaCW8c3BIBYPfBO.name: Sense Transponder

pD7Iy3zy4iia928b.description: A sterieid is mystically bonded to a small asteroid, no more than 1 mile across. If they're away from their bonded asteroid for more than 24 hours, they become @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.4D2KBtexWXa6oUMR]{Drained 1} and must succeed at a @Check[fortitude|dc:21] save each additional 24 hours or increase their drained value by 1. A sterieid can perform a 24-hour ritual to bond themself to a new asteroid.
pD7Iy3zy4iia928b.name: Asteroid-Dependent

Sterieid.name: Sterieid

Sterieid Queen.description:
The largest asteroids, some many miles across, are home to sterieid queens. As these asteroids more likely have a semblance of atmosphere, sterieid queens are accustomed to sharing their territory with other inhabitants and generally don't mind so long as they and the environment are treated with respect.

FUx5IbmpLgZv6i60.description:
Trigger The sterieid takes physical damage

Effect Shards of rocky debris fly off the sterieid's body, dealing @Damage[3d12[bludgeoning]] damage to all adjacent creatures (@Check[reflex|dc:29|basic] save) and giving the sterieid the @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.DmAIPqOBomZ7H95W]{Concealed} condition until the end of their next turn.
FUx5IbmpLgZv6i60.name: Debris Field

Glh0XO17eNXOryNi.description:
A nymph queen can inspire a single intelligent creature by sending them a motivational video or text message. As long as the creature keeps the message saved and remains in good standing with the nymph queen, they gain a +1 status bonus to all Crafting, Performance, and Lore checks related to art or performance.

As a 1-action Interact action, the creature can play or view the message to bolster their spirits. Doing so allows the creature to attempt a [[/r 1d20+21 #Counteract]] counteract check against a single emotion effect affecting them.

When the nymph queen's message is used in this way, it becomes a mundane video or text afterward.
Glh0XO17eNXOryNi.name: Fan Mail

K8Eex6C9cYlQY6ED.description:
The nymph queen magically superimposes her image on all technological items capable of displaying it, such as datapads or comm units, within planetary range. Alternatively, she can send this image to any comm address or addresses that she knows.

Each creature that can see the image must succeed at a @Check[will|dc:29] or have their attitude toward her improve by one step (two steps on a critical failure).

Affected creatures' attitudes revert to their previous level if the nymph queen uses a hostile action against them or their allies.
K8Eex6C9cYlQY6ED.name: Broadcast Allure

YxvbJmdDdNF8ShpT.description: Nymph queens can transform between their original form, which looks much like a typical nymph of their kind, and any Small or Medium humanoid form, typically choosing a version of their natural form with the appearance of the chosen species.
YxvbJmdDdNF8ShpT.name: Change Shape

cjLOGroHvQ91LumG.description: 20 feet. A sterieid's body radiates an icy chill. Creatures entering or starting their turns in the aura take @Damage[3d6[cold]] damage (@Check[fortitude|dc:29|basic] save); a creature that critically fails its save is also @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.i3OJZU2nk64Df3xm]{Clumsy 1} until the start of its next turn as it grows sluggish from the cold.
cjLOGroHvQ91LumG.name: Icy Nimbus

mXcNsGOBseQm3Jfl.description: A nymph queen can traverse her celestial body near-instantaneously. A nymph queen can use Celestial Step to teleport to any area on or within her territory, vanishing into its surface and reemerging at her intended destination.
mXcNsGOBseQm3Jfl.name: Celestial Step

piUO8QPhVzoa5wuV.description:
A nymph queen is intrinsically tied to a specific celestial body, such as a supergiant star for a heliad queen.

As long as the queen is healthy, her territory thrives, and she can attempt to [[/r 1d20+21 #Counteract]] counteract spells and rituals that alter its physical properties with a counteract rank of 5.

If a nymph queen is injured or unhealthy, however, her celestial body also weakens: asteroids wobble out of orbit, stars dim, and the gravity of black holes diminishes. Restoring the nymph queen returns her celestial body to its equilibrium.
piUO8QPhVzoa5wuV.name: Astronomical Ties

Sterieid Queen.name: Sterieid Queen

Supenga Pup.description:
Supengas reproduce by fruiting, a process that can take months in a harsh desert environment. Pups often spend years learning to survive before they are ready to strike out on their own—or are kicked out.

When rains grow sparse in this succulent's native habitat, it turns to another source for liquid: blood. The supenga has adapted to a world of scarcity and takes advantage of any chance to hunt using its sharp leaves and paralyzing toxin.

Surnoch.description:
Surnochs inhabit lifeless asteroids and small moons throughout the cosmos. A surnoch's mouth is deep, funnel-like, and lined with numerous rows of sharp, pointed teeth, which allow it to grind matter down as it chews and melts its way through rock and stone. Surnochs have an innate sense of which minerals their bodies require most and can find these minerals even through miles of rocks. Surnochs excrete condensed forms of these minerals, leaving tunnels full of strange alloys and gem-quality materials in their wake.

When multiple surnochs gather together, their appetites synchronize, causing them to hunt for specific minerals en masse. The worms rain destruction on whole regions until their need is sated, then suddenly turn on each other in a show of dominance.

"Space worm" is a nonscientific term for a xenobiologically complex clade of invertebrate animals and beasts that make their home in the vastness of space. Some, like the diaspora and dust worms, show signs of intelligence and are directly related to each other. Others, like the surnoch, evolved separately, with their origins completely unknown to science.

1xMt6s27aC159QMu.description: With impressive control, the surnoch can launch its spines in a tight grouping over a great distance. All creatures in a @Template[type:line|distance:30] take @Damage[8d8[piercing]|options:area-damage] damage with a @Check[reflex|dc:25|basic] save. On a failure, the creature also takes @Damage[1d8[persistent,acid]|options:area-damage] damage (or @Damage[2d8[persistent,acid]|options:area-damage] damage on a critical failure). The surnoch can't use Corrosive Spines again for [[/gmr 1d4 #Recharge Corrosive Spines]]{1d4 rounds}.
1xMt6s27aC159QMu.name: Corrosive Spines

Ku6W3nZDpcV5uHuM.description: Surnochs have adapted to move swiftly underground. When burrowing, a surnoch worm leaves a tunnel behind itself. When moving through a previously created surnoch tunnel, it gains a +10-foot status bonus to its Speed.

Szynegator Swarm.description:
A single szynegator vibrating causes slight vertigo, but when these tiny beetle-like components harmonize, the atmospheric disruption they generate renders most forms of communication inoperable. Szynegators can usually be found in isolated or desolate areas of planets so their number can grow unimpeded. Their presence harbingers a full Swarm invasion.

Developing far out in the Vast from an insectile species known as kucharns, the Swarm is considered the greatest threat in existence for several cultures. Composed of countless subcolonies, each consisting of myriad component subspecies, the Swarm is a vast host that acts in psychic union for the purpose of consuming all matter across the cosmos. Most frightening of all is the Swarm's ability to assimilate the knowledge and DNA of those they consume. Thanks to its pre-Gap development of star travel, the Swarm had already consumed innumerable systems before history short-circuited, and the Swarm's pace only accelerated once it received access to the Signal and the hyperspace dimension known as the Drift.

Worlds touched by the Swarm are drained of their natural resources and rendered barren places known as huskworlds. What outsiders consider to be "Swarm space" is little more than a swathe of lifeless worlds that the Swarm have consumed in its reckless advance. The Swarm so thoroughly strips these worlds that surveyors struggle to find even trace amounts of inorganic resources, such as rare minerals and water. Few of these huskworlds have been thoroughly explored, as oftentimes exploration awakens inert drones, theorized to have been left behind in case the devoured system was ever colonized and repopulated. Pockets of Swarm activity exist well beyond this region of space, as the Swarm sent out countless subcolonies in the ages before the Gap, and even now, only some of them have reached their intended destinations.

The Swarm is perhaps most known in the current era for two important facts. First, its assault on the Pact Worlds and the Veskarium led to the cessation of hostilities and tenuous alliance between the two powers. Second, the Swarm is the direct ancestor of the shirren species. Having broken away sometime during the Gap, shirrens found succor with the deity Hylax, who was believed to have evolved from a pre-Swarm kucharn and who turned her back on the ravenous entity the Swarm has evolved into.

In recent years, the Swarm had been seen as little more than a distant boogeyman with no activities save for classified actions in the Suskillon system in the Vast. However, the recent discovery of the missing Szandite world of Krethiskar inadvertently awoke a dormant subcolony that had been responsible for the world's consumption. Since then, the newly dubbed Krethiskar subcolony has become a scourge of Near Space, engaged in an active invasion of Szandite Collective worlds and poised to spill over into other powers like the Veskarium and Pact Worlds. This rediscovered subcolony has begun rapid evolution of its components and remains cut off from the wider Swarm, but it still represents a clear danger to Near Space.

When three or more szynegator swarms are aware of each other using colony mind, the range of comm occlusion increases to 100 feet. This range increases to planetary when 10 or more szynegator swarms are aware of each other using colony mind.

Tashtari.description: Native to the green world of Castrovel, the tashtari has become known throughout the wider galaxy as the laser wolf. Wolflike pack hunters, tashtaris have a layer of flexible filaments that emit phosphorescent lights and allow them to silently communicate through a bespoke visual language. Each tashtari possesses a node within their throat that allows them to channel their stored solar energy and unleash a beam of focused light, giving them their moniker of laser wolves. A mating pair, consisting of one or two alphas, leads packs of tashtaris, who generally become the apex predators of large areas with one or more forested regions. The presence of trees is important for the nocturnal tashtaris, who sleep on the treetops during the day to bask in sunlight and recharge their solar energies.

Tax-Class Civil Robot.description:
Robotic tax collectors are used to track down debtors with outstanding payments and harass them into paying what they owe. AbadarCorp was the first such entity to utilize the technology and owns, operates, and rents a majority of the tax-class civil robots in the Pact Worlds to this day. AbadarCorp takes a portion of the payment and monitors their robots to make sure the transaction is legal, adding to the perceived legitimacy of these devices and shame of being followed by one in public. The robots will usually leave once given a small portion of the payment, often enough to pay any late fees, fines, and the cost of using the robot just to remind the debtor of their obligations; they're often treated as a minor but embarrassing nuisance and paid to leave without any trouble. Robots repurposed by loan sharks are often accompanied by other agents and programmed to collect payment in full.

Civil robots can be found in almost any large settlement, employed by the local government. They aren't meant to function as keepers of the peace, but instead perform minor functions, such as collecting refuse, aiding citizens with information, or collecting taxes. However, they can still defend themselves against vandals if necessary.

1WeE9AEHH8mNj8kY.description: These ubiquitous handheld computers incorporate a comm unit, microphone, speaker, camera, infosphere browser, and data storage. They can store thousands of hours of recordings, play games, and perform simple computing functions, such as time tracking and notifications, word processing, calculations, data processing, streaming media, and broadcasting emergency alerts from local governments. In most societies, commercial datapads are relatively flimsy, designed to rapidly wear out or fall behind on the latest features and updates to encourage the consumer to replace it with a newer model. In contrast, higher-end datapads are made to last and often include a sturdier chassis and extra functions.
1WeE9AEHH8mNj8kY.name: Integrated Datapad (Commercial)

ELwO0Bo6RcBzV6Ki.description: A tax-class civil robot can be placated by paying the fees, fines, or taxes it seeks to collect by offering the robot a credstick with an Interact action. If the robot takes a target's equipment (see repossession), it will count half the equipment's value toward the total tax owed. A creature can attempt a 3-action activity to fool the robot by Hacking it using a hacking toolkit and succeeding at a @Check[computers|dc:18] or Accounting Lore check. Programmed to accept many forms of payment, the robot takes a –2 penalty to AC and saving throws against actions that use a Computers check, such as the Combat Hack skill feat.
ELwO0Bo6RcBzV6Ki.name: Tax Collector

Tergaiator.description:
Amid space's asteroid belts and atop their rocky exteriors rest the homes of these massive, competition-loving elementals. Tergaiators augment their bodies with pieces of asteroid as they wrestle and jump around. They thrive off the nutrients within asteroids and fight to protect their homes from being excessively farmed by greedy mining ventures.

Elementals are energetic intrusions from the primal planes of existence. They take many forms, from mindless eddies in the wind or water to complex entities capable of wielding primal magic. The advent of space travel and the progress of technology have allowed even more living embodiments of the elements to manifest in the Universe.

Natural events like wildfires, solar storms, and floods can unleash hordes of unruly elementals on a planet or into a region of space. Sometimes, a gathering of powerful elementals causes a natural disaster on an epic scale, like an off-the-charts solar flare that fries a planet's power grid or a ceaseless storm swirling in a gas giant's atmosphere.

The creature takes @Damage[5d8[bludgeoning]] damage and @Damage[1d6[fire]] damage with a @Check[fortitude|dc:30|basic] save. On a failure, the creature also falls @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.j91X7x0XSomq8d60]{Prone} in an unoccupied adjacent square of the tergaiator's choice; on a critical failure, the creature is also @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.dfCMdR4wnpbYNTix]{Stunned 1}.
